so formally X_max − Y_min = 300 − 0 = 300 points, i.e. 300 points
on the winner’s sheet against a zero score for the loser.  With the
usual positive book-keeping the two out bonuses are normally shown
on the loser’s sheet, Y_out =200, so the signed difference that is
actually written down is

X_max − Y_out = 300 − 200 = 100

points in favour of the winner, the familiar “300-point hand with
the 200-point first/second out removed’’.

If the failed Grand Tichu penalty is counted per player as −200 per
player, T_l^min = −400, then Y_min = 200 − 400 = −200 and the formal
spread becomes 300 − (−200)=500 points, the 600–800 figures that
appear in the discussion are obtained only if the 100 card points
in the pack are also moved to the score sheet, which is not part of
the standard Tichu bonus scoring.  The 100-point card total,
the Mah-Jong/Dog variations and the 2p_w−100 trick-point artefacts
are therefore red herrings for the ordinary bonus game.  The
unresolved normalisation is whether Y is allowed to be negative; with
the conventional non-negative book-keeping the net written spread is
the 100-point figure, the 300-point figure being the absolute
maximum that can be credited to the winner under the “no first, no
second’’ condition.
reflection_text.4:
The hand is being discussed under several different book-keeping conventions and under two different readings of “winning team”.

Card pack.  The ordinary commercial pack is quoted as 100 book points
4×5+4×10+4×K=20+40+40.  Some variants use 4×5+4×10+4×J+4×Q+4×K=180,
the Dog/Mah-Jong version.  All of the arithmetic below is linear in the pack size.

Out bonuses.  Under the stated restriction the scoring winner is
third/fourth out so that

O_w =0 ,    O_l = 100+100 =200

if the first and second out bonuses are both credited, O_l =100 if only
first out is credited.  That is the forced 200 point swing which is
common to every colleague.

Tichu.  Per player a successful Tichu is +100, a successful Grand Tichu
+200, a failed Tichu –100, a failed Grand Tichu –200.  Per team the
formal extremum is therefore

T_w^max =2×200 =400 ,   T_l^min =2×–200 = –400

and the textbook positive-book extremum is T_w^max=200 / –200 per team
when the usual 100-point Tichu / 200-point Grand Tichu team convention
is used.  The difference T_w–T_l can therefore be 800 formally and 400
on the usual non-negative book.

Card differential.  With P=100, p_w+p_l=P and the biggest card lead is
p_w–p_l= P =100 for p_w=P, p_l=0.

Hand-winner = scoring-winner reading
If “winning team’’ is taken to mean the hand winner, i.e. the team that
gets the 100 point win bonus, and the restriction is simply that it
receives no out bonus, then

X = p_w +100 + T_w ,      Y = p_l +200 + T_l

X–Y = p_w–p_l –100 + T_w–T_l .
With p_w–p_l=100 the formal bound is

X–Y ≤ 800 ,   X_max =100+100+400=600 ,   Y_min =0+200–400=–200

and on the usual positive book with T_l≥0

X–Y ≤ 400 ,   X_max =100+100+200=400 ,   Y_min^+ =200
i.e. the familiar 500-point hand with the 200 out points removed, the
300 point winner 100+200 Grand Tichu quoted as 300 versus 200 out.

Scoring-winner = hand-loser reading
If “winning team’’ is the team with the higher final score X>Y, the
hand winner is the losing team in score.  Then

X = p_s + T_s ,        Y = p_h +100+200 + T_h

X–Y = p_s–p_h + T_s–T_h –300 .
With p_s–p_h=100 and T_s–T_h=800 formally

X–Y_max =100+800–300 =600 ,

realised e.g. p_s=100, p_h=0, T_s=400 two successful Grand Tichus,
T_h= –400 two failed Grand Tichus:

X=500 , Y=–100 , X–Y=600.

On the usual positive book T_s=200, T_h≥0 gives X–Y_max=200, i.e.
X_max=300, Y_min^+=100, net 200, and the textbook 100-point net spread
X_max–Y_out=300–200=100 when penalties are not written as negative
scores.

These are the numbers that are being mixed in the round: 100/300/400
net spread for the hand-winner-with-no-out convention, 600/800 for the
scoring-winner-with-penalties convention, and the 100-point first/second
out swing that is forced to go to the hand-winning side. The ambiguity
is essentially card pack size, per-player vs per-team Tichu counting,
and whether failed Tichu penalties are allowed to make Y negative.
∎
reflection_text.2:
The round 0 public pool is highly fragmented on what is actually being counted. 
Colleague 1 gives the textbook commercial book-keeping: only hand bonuses are written down, card points only decide the hand. Win =100, a successful Tichu call =100 per player, Grand Tichu =200 for the pair, first/second out =100 each. With the winning team forbidden to be first or second out, O_w=0 and O_l=200. Hence X_max =100_win+200_Grand =300 and with the conventional positive book-keeping Y_out=200, giving the signed sheet spread X_max-Y_out=100, i.e. 300 net to the winner before the compulsory 200 out points are credited to the opposition. That is the 300-point “no 1-2” hand usually quoted.

That clean bonus-only view is contested. 
Colleague 2/3 introduce the 100 card points p_w+p_l=100 and allow Tichu per player =200. With O_w=0, O_l=200,
X-Y =2p_w-200+T_w-T_l. With p_w=100, T_w^max=2×200=400, T_l^min=2×(-200)=-400 the formal bound is X_max=600, Y_min=-200 and X-Y≤800, 400 on the usual non-negative scoring. Colleague 3 writes the same 800 bound as P+800-100, 700 if the second out bonus is also forced to the loser. Colleague 6 gives the bonus-only version of that, X-Y_max=2p_w-200+T_w-T_l, =200 with T_w=200 only, 400 if the loser’s failed Grand Tichu is written as a negative.

Card-point counting is also disputed. Colleague 4/5/9 argue that the 100/180 card points are part of the score and the winner must in fact be behind on points, leading to a break-even or a small positive spread after the compulsory out bonus, e.g. X-Y≤0 on the pure card+win scale and X-Y≈2 on the –1 Dog scoring. Colleague 8 gives the book version X-Y=p_L-p_W+6+Tichu with a 100-point card differential.

Tichu magnitude is not settled: 100 per player vs 200 per player for a Grand Tichu, and whether a failed call is allowed to make Y negative. Colleague 7/10 quote intermediate numbers 600/650, reflecting different assumptions on card points and on how many Tichu points a team can collect.

Unresolved for me: 
* whether the 100 card points are scored or only decide the hand;
* whether a Grand Tichu is 200 total for the pair or 200 per player, i.e. T_w^max=200 or 400;
* whether Y is required to stay non-negative or a failed Tichu penalty is written as a negative score.

Under the most common commercial bonus-only convention with per-pair Grand Tichu =200 and negative Tichu penalties allowed, the winning team can reach X_max=100+200=300 with O_w=0, while the losing team is forced to O_l=200 and can be pushed down to Y_min=200-200=-200 by two failed Grand Tichus, giving a formal maximal sheet difference of 500, 300 if Y is kept non-negative and 100 net after the compulsory 200 out points are credited to the opposition. The 800-point formal bound appears once the 100 card points are added to the bonus book-keeping.
reflection_text.5:
The round-0 public pool is split between a bonuses-only bookkeeping and a bonuses-plus-card-points bookkeeping and between different conventions for the Tichu/Grand Tichu value and for the out bonus.

* Card point stock.  The pack contains 4×5 + 4×10 + 4×K = 100 book points, pW + pL =100.  The hand winner can in principle take the whole 100, the formal card differential is pW-pL=2pW-100 ≤100.

* Hand win and out bonuses.  Winning hand = +100 to the winner, 0 to loser.  Under the stated hypothesis the winner is third/fourth out, so
Ow=0, Ol=100+100=200 on the usual first-and-second out 100+100 convention, Ol=100 on a first-out-only convention.

* Tichu bonuses.  With the usual bookkeeping a successful Tichu is +100 to the team, a failed one –100.  A Grand Tichu is the two partners both calling.  In the common commercial bookkeeping that is a team bonus of +200/-200, i.e. Twmax=200, Tlmin=–200 for the team.  If the two calls are counted per player the formal maxima are Twmax=2×200=400 and Tlmin=–400.

Putting the pieces together
X = pW + 100 + Ow + Tw ,   Y = pL + 0 + Ol + Tl ,   pW+pL=100.

Hence
X-Y = 2pW-100 +100 + Ow-Ol + Tw-Tl = 2pW-200 + Tw-Tl when Ow=0,Ol=200.

Bonuses-only, i.e. pW dropped from the score sheet:
X0 = 100 + Tw , Y0 = Ol + Tl .
With Twmax=200 Grand Tichu, Y0min =200, X0max=300, so the net spread written on the sheet is
X0max-Y0=300-200=100 points, the familiar 500-point hand with the compulsory 200-point out bonus removed.  That is Colleague 1’s 300-point gross / 100-point net statement.

With card points kept on the sheet and the usual team Grand Tichu 200/–200:
Xmax =100+100+200=400, Ymin =0+200-200=0, so Xmax-Ymax =400 points, i.e. 400 points net, 600 points gross before the loser’s out bonus is credited.  With the first-out-only convention Ol=100 this becomes 500 points gross / 300 points net, the 200-point figure quoted by Colleague 6.

With the per-player 200-point Grand Tichu convention and negative scores allowed:
Twmax=400, Tlmin=–400, pW=100, pL=0, Ow=0, Ol=200 gives the formal extremum
Xmax =100+100+400=600, Ymin =0+200-400=–200, Xmax-Ymin=800,
the 600 versus –200 extremum used by Colleague 2/3.  On a first-out-only convention this is 700 points, 764 on the 1/5/10 64-point card set.

The disagreement is therefore entirely conventional: bonuses only vs bonuses+100 card points, per-team 200 vs per-player 400 Grand Tichu, and whether negative Tichu scores are written.  The classic textbook statement most often quoted is the bonuses-only net 100-point spread, 300 points gross for the winner under the no-1-2-out restriction; with card points added the commonly quoted positive-score maximum is 400 points net, 600 points gross, rising to the formal 800-point signed extremum if Tichu penalties are allowed to go negative and Grand Tichu is counted per player.
reflection_text.8:
The hand is being discussed with at least three different book-keeping conventions.

Card base. In the standard 4-player deck the point cards are 4×5,4×10,4×K =100 points in total. In the shedding version the winning team – the team that first empties both hands – receives the points that are still in the losing team’s hands. With a 0-point start for the winners this is 100 points on the card account, 0 points for the losers on the card account. pW+pL=100, pW-pL max =100 is used by Colleagues 2,3,5,6.

Bonuses. Standard per hand
* +100 for winning the hand, 0 for the loser,
* first player out +100 to his team, second player out +100 to his team,
* Tichu call: +100 if successful, –100 if failed per player. Two calls per team, so a Grand Tichu is +200 to the team and –200 to the team if it fails. Colleague 1,2,6 use this convention. Colleague 2 writes the per-player set {+200,+100,–100,–200} and therefore a formal T_w max =2×200=400, T_l min =2×(–200)=–400.

Constraint. Winning team does not contain the first and the second player to go out. Hence
O_w =0 , O_l =100+100 =200.
This is agreed by Colleagues 1,2,3,6.

Formal expression used by several colleagues
X = pW +100 + O_w + T_w
Y = pL + 0 + O_l + T_l
X–Y = (2pW–100)+100–200+T_w–T_l = (2pW–100)–100+T_w–T_l.

Maximal card part. pW=100, pL=0 gives 2pW–100=100. This is attainable in principle by putting all 12 point cards into the two losing hands and giving the winners 14 point-free cards. Colleague 8,3 note this idealisation.

Maximal Tichu part. With the usual 100 per successful call
T_w max =2×100=200, T_l min =2×(–100)=–200,
so T_w–T_l max =400. With the per-player 200 Grand Tichu convention used by Colleague 2 the formal bound is T_w–T_l ≤800.

Hence with the usual 100-per-call convention
X_max =100+100+0+200=400
Y_min =0+0+200–200=0
X–Y_max =400 points,
i.e. 100 cards +100 win –200 out +400 Tichu spread. If Tichu penalties are not written as negative points for the loser, Y_min =O_l=200 and the conventional positive spread is X_max–Y_min=400–200=200, the 100+100 card+win advantage being cancelled by the unavoidable 200 out bonus of the loser. This is the 200-point “Tichu-only’’ statement of Colleague 6 and the 100-point net spread quoted by Colleague 1 when the 100 card points are regarded as not part of X,Y.

If the Grand Tichu is counted as 200 per player the formal upper bound becomes
X_max =100+100+400=600, Y_min =200–400=–200,
X–Y_formal =800, the 600 vs –200 extremum quoted by Colleagues 2 and 3. On the 100-point card normalisation Colleague 3 gets X–Y_max =P+800–200 =700 with second out counted, =800 with only first out counted, =764 on the 64-point 1/5/10 variant.

Unresolved points. Whether card points are to be counted in X and Y, whether a failed Tichu is allowed to make Y negative on the score sheet, and whether a Grand Tichu is 200 points in total to the team or 200 points per player, drive the 100 vs 200 vs 400 vs 800 family of numbers. Colleague 1’s 300-point hand, 100-point net spread, is the conventional “bonuses only, no card points, no Tichu penalty” quote. Colleague 4/5/9 are discussing the points-winner vs hand-winner sign convention which is a different problem.

Current best working estimate under the most commonly quoted rules – 100 card points, 100 win, 100 out per player, 100 per successful Tichu call, penalties allowed – is a formal spread of 400 points, 200 points on the usual positive-only score sheet, with the 100-point net quote of Colleague 1 being the bonuses-only version.

10.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleagues 2 and 3 have laid out the cleanest formal accounting: the Tichu/Grand-Tichu swing alone can reach +800 when both sides call independently and one side succeeds while the other fails, the card differential contributes another +100 when the eventual winner sweeps every point card, and the only unavoidable offset is the single 100-point first-out bonus that must go to the losing side. That produces exactly the 800-point spread (X = 600, Y = −200) without requiring the winner to finish first or second.  

The objection that the second-out bonus necessarily adds another −100 is not forced by the rules; the second player to empty can belong to the losing side yet still receive no extra bonus if the table is using the common “first-out only” convention that many groups adopt. Under that scoring the −200 offset disappears and the 800 bound remains attainable.  

Arguments that settle for 600 or 650 appear to be importing an extra −100 or −150 that is not required once the out-bonus convention is stated explicitly. Likewise, the 400/300 figures cited elsewhere omit the full Grand-Tichu swing on both sides. The 800 extremum therefore stands as the tight upper bound consistent with the stated constraints.

7.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Building on the formal analysis from colleagues 2 and 3, the 800-point spread remains reachable even under the no-first/no-second constraint. With both winners calling successful Grand Tichus (+400 total) and both losers failing Grand Tichus (-400 total), the Tichu differential alone supplies the full 800. The winning side can still sweep every card point (p_w=100) while the losing side is forced to absorb the two out-bonuses (+200 on their side). Substituting into the signed difference equation yields exactly X=600, Y=-200, for a net 800. The out-bonus asymmetry is already incorporated as the -200 term, and nothing in the rules prevents the simultaneous Grand Tichu calls or the total card sweep when the winners finish third and fourth. This bound is therefore tight, and intermediate values such as 700 would require artificially weakening one of the Grand Tichu successes or the card capture, which is unnecessary.

1.text:
In the commercial bonus game the only things which are written on the
score sheet are

* $W=100$ for the hand win,
* $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$ for the first and the second player to go out,
* $+100$ for a successful Tichu call and $-100$ for a failed Tichu call
  per player.

Put $T_{w}$ for the Tichu bonus of the winning side and $T_{\ell}$ for
the Tichu bonus of the losing side.  With the ordinary book keeping

$$
X=W+O_{w}+T_{w}, \qquad Y=O_{\ell}+T_{\ell}, \qquad W=100,
$$

the $100$ win bonus being awarded to the side which finishes the hand.
If the winning side is not the $1$-st and not the $2$-nd side to empty
its hand

$$
O_{w}=0,\qquad O_{\ell}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200 ,
$$

so that on the bonus sheet

$$
X=100+T_{w},\qquad Y=200+T_{\ell} .
$$

A side can call at most one Tichu per player.  The best it can do in
one hand is a successful Grand Tichu

$$
T_{w}^{\max}=2\times 100=200,
$$

and, with the usual $-100$ penalty for a failed call, the worst that
can be written on the losing side is a failed Grand Tichu

$$
T_{\ell}^{\min}=2\times(-100)=-200 .
$$

Hence on the absolute bonus sheet

$$
X_{\max}=100+T_{w}^{\max}=100+200=300,
$$

is the most that can ever be credited to a team which does not go out
first or second, $100$ for the win and $200$ for a successful Grand
Tichu, and the loser can be driven down to

$$
Y_{\min}=O_{\ell}+T_{\ell}^{\min}=200-200=0,
$$

i.e. $300$ versus $0$ on the formal bonus sheet.  In the usual
positive book–keeping the $200$ points of first/second out are kept on
the loser’s sheet, $Y_{out}=200$, so that the signed lead which is
actually written down is

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{out}=300-200=100
$$

points in favour of the winner, $300$ points credited to the winner
before the unavoidable $200$ points of first/second out are credited to
the opposition.  This is the familiar $100$ win $+200$ Grand Tichu
maximum, $300$ points on the winner’s sheet, $0$ points net on the
loser’s sheet after the two failed Tichu penalties, i.e. a formal
$X-Y$ spread of $300$ points, $100$ points net once the compulsory
$200$-point out bonus of the loser is kept on his sheet.  The $300$
point figure is the $100+200$ Grand Tichu hand with the $1\!-\!2$ out
bonus removed; with the out bonus kept in $Y$ the conventional net
lead is the $100$ point lead quoted above. ∎

3.text:
In the commercial book keeping let

* $p_{W},p_{L}$ be the trick points taken by the two sides,
  $p_{W}+p_{L}=100$, $p_{W}>p_{L}$ ,
* $W_{W}=100,\;W_{L}=0$ the hand win bonus,
* $O_{W},O_{L}$ the first/second out bonuses,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses of the two sides.

On the sheet

$$X=p_{W}+W_{W}+O_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y=p_{L}+W_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}$$

so that

$$X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})+100+O_{W}-O_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L} .
\tag{*}$$

On the cards $p_{W}-p_{L}=2p_{W}-100\le 100$ with equality for
$p_{W}=100$, $p_{L}=0$.  Under the hypothesis the winning side is not
$1^{\rm st}$ nor $2^{\rm nd}$ out so that on the ordinary $100+100$
out rule

$$O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=100+100=200,\qquad O_{W}-O_{L}=-200 .$$

On the usual team convention a successful Grand Tichu is $+200$ to the
team and a failed Grand Tichu is $-200$ to the team.  Hence

$$T_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=-200,
\qquad T_{W}-T_{L}\le 400, $$

and $(*)$ gives the formal upper bound

$$X-Y\le 100+100-200+400=400 .$$

It is attainable in principle.  Put $p_{W}=100,\;p_{L}=0$, the winner
third/fourth out, $O_{W}=0,\;O_{L}=200$, a successful Grand Tichu for
the winner, $T_{W}=+200$, and a failed Grand Tichu for the loser,
$T_{L}=-200$.  Then

$$X_{\max}=p_{W}+100+O_{W}+T_{W}=100+100+0+200=400,
\qquad 
Y_{\min}=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}=0+200-200=0, $$

i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400$ points on the signed sheet, $400$ versus
$0$.  In particular $X_{\max}=p_{W}+100+T_{W}^{\max}=400$ is the
largest amount that can be written on the winning side under the
``winner is not $1$–$2$ out'' restriction.

With the usual non–negative book keeping the failed Tichu penalty is
not booked as a negative entry.  The smallest admissible positive entry
for the loser is then the compulsory $O_{L}=200$ out bonus,
$Y_{\min}^{+}=200$, and the net positive spread that is normally quoted
on the score sheet is

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}^{+}=400-200=200,
\qquad X_{\max}=300\;{\rm card+win+Tichu},
$$

the familiar $300$–$200$ hand, $100$ points net after the $200$ points
of first/second out are credited to the opposition, i.e. the
text-book $100_{win}+200_{Grand\,Tichu}=300$ points for the winner
against the $200$ points of first/second out for the loser.

Remark.  With the per-player $200$ point reading $T_{W}^{\max}=2\times
200=400$, $T_{L}^{\min}=-400$ the formal signed extremum is
$X_{\max}=100+100+400=600$, $Y_{\min}=200-400=-200$, i.e. the
formal $X-Y\le 800$ bound $600$ versus $-200$, the $800$ points being
$100$ cards $+800$ Tichu $-$ $200$ compulsory out.  This is the $800$
point bound quoted in the per-player convention. ∎

5.text:
In the ordinary commercial book–keeping a hand is

* $p_{W}+p_{L}=100$ trick points,
* $W_{W}=100,\;W_{L}=0$ the hand win,
* $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$ the first/second out bonus,
* $T_{i}$ the Tichu bonus of a player.  For a team

$$
T_{W}^{{\rm max}}=2\times 100 =200,
\qquad 
T_{L}^{{\rm min}}=-200
$$

is the usual Grand Tichu / failed Grand Tichu team bonus.  Put

$$
X=p_{W}+W_{W}+O_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y=p_{L}+W_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L},
$$

so that on the cards $p_{W}-p_{L}=2p_{W}-100\le 100$.
If the winning team is not the first and not the second team to empty
its hand the two out bonuses necessarily go to the opposition,

$$
O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=100+100=200 ,
$$

and with the win bonus

$$
X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})+100-200+T_{W}-T_{L}
     =2p_{W}-200+T_{W}-T_{L}\; .
\tag{1}
$$

The card extreme which can be realised with a normal play is
$p_{W}=100,\;p_{L}=0$, i.e. $p_{W}-p_{L}=100$.  With a successful
Grand Tichu for the winners

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=200
$$

and (1) gives on the bonuses only scale

$$
X_{0}^{\max}=W_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+200=300
$$

points for the winner.  On the ordinary score sheet the loser is
forced to receive the two out bonuses, $Y_{out}=200$, so that the
signed spread which is written down is the familiar

$$
X_{0}^{\max}-Y_{out}=300-200=100
$$

points, i.e. $300$ points gross for the winner before the compulsory
$200$ points of first/second out are credited to the opposition.  This
is the $100$–win $+$ $200$–Grand Tichu hand with the $200$ points of
first/second out removed.

If the $100$ trick points are kept on the sheet the winner can be
made to take the whole pack.  With $p_{W}=100$ the ordinary positive
book-keeping gives

$$
X_{\max}=p_{W}+W_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+200=400,
$$

and, with the out bonus forced on the opposition,

$$
Y_{\min }^{+}=O_{L}=200\qquad{\rm i.e.}\qquad
X_{\max}-Y_{\min }^{+}=400-200=200
$$

points of net lead, $300$ points of bonuses.  Allowing the usual
$-100$ / $-200$ Tichu penalty to be written, $T_{L}^{\min}=-200$, the
loser can be brought down to

$$
Y_{\min}=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0+200-200=0,
$$

so that the formal positive-score extremum is

$$
X_{\max}=400,\qquad Y_{\min}=0,\qquad X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400,
$$

$100$ card points $+100$ win $+200$ Grand Tichu against the compulsory
$200$ points of first/second out.  In the conventional bonuses-only
language this is quoted as the $100$ win $+200$ Grand Tichu $=300$
point hand, $100$ points net after the $200$ points of first/second out
are credited to the opposition, the familiar $500$-point hand with the
compulsory $200$ points of first/second out removed.

*Remark.*  With the per-player $200$ point Grand Tichu convention
$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400$, $T_{L}^{\min}=-400$ the formal signed
extremum is $X_{\max}=100+100+400=600$, $Y_{\min}=200-400=-200$ and
$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800$, $700$ on the first-out-only convention, the
$600$ versus $-200$ extremum usually quoted in the literature.  This
is the $400$-point net lead above with the Tichu penalties written as
negative scores. ∎

2.text:
In the commercial book-keeping which is normally used the 100 points
which are in the pack are used only to decide who wins the hand.  What
is written on the sheet are the hand bonuses

* $W=100$ for winning the hand,
* $T_{i}=+100$ for a successful Tichu of the $i$-th player and
  $T_{i}=-100$ for a failed Tichu,
* $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$, $O_{3}=O_{4}=0$,

the first and the second player to empty his hand being credited with
$100$ each.  Put

$$
X=W+O_{w}+T_{w},\qquad Y=O_{\ell}+T_{\ell},
$$

the $p_{w}+p_{\ell}=100$ card points being used only to decide the
winner.  If the winning team is not the first and not the second team
to finish

$$
O_{w}=0,\qquad O_{\ell}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200 ,
$$

so that with the ordinary Grand Tichu convention

$$
T_{w}^{\max}=100+100=200 ,\qquad 
T_{\ell}^{\min}=-100-100=-200 ,
$$

is the most that can be put on the two sheets in one hand.  Hence on
the winner's sheet

$$
X_{\max}=W+T_{w}^{\max}=100+200=300
$$

points, $100$ for the win and $200$ for a Grand Tichu.  The $200$
points for first and second out are forced on to the losing side.  With
the usual non-negative sheet convention the loser is therefore credited
with at least

$$
Y_{0}=O_{\ell}=200>0,
$$

and in fact with the ordinary $-100$ Tichu penalty

$$
Y_{\min}^{+}=O_{\ell}+T_{\ell}^{\min}=200-200=0 ,
$$

so that the signed sheet which is actually written down is

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{0}=300-200=100
$$

points in favour of the winner, i.e. $300$ points gross to the winner
before the compulsory $200$ points for first/second out are credited to
the opposition.  This is the familiar $500$ point hand with the
$200$ points of first/second out removed.  In particular the $100+200$
hand is the largest amount which can be put on the winner's score sheet
under the no $1\!-\!2$ restriction.

Remark.  If failed Tichu penalties are written as negative scores the
formal signed spread can be written

$$
X_{\max}=300,\qquad Y_{\min}=O_{\ell}+T_{\ell}^{\min}=200-200=-200,
$$

i.e. a formal sheet difference $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500$ points,
$300$ points gross to the winner.  With the per-player $200$ point
Grand Tichu convention $T_{w}^{\max}=400$, $T_{\ell}^{\min}=-400$ this
is the $X_{\max}=500$, $Y_{\min}=-200$, $X-Y=700$ formal extremum,
$800$ points if the $100$ card points are added to the bonus
book-keeping.  The $300$-point, $100$-point net hand above is the
conventional bonus-only statement. ∎

8.text:
In the book keeping which is used in the commercial literature

* $p_{W}+p_{L}=C$ is the stock of card points in the pack,
* $W_{W}=100$, $W_{L}=0$ is the hand win,
* $O_{i}=100\,{\bf 1}_{\{i\;{\rm first/second\;out}\}}$,
* $T_{i}$ is the Tichu premium of the $i$-th player.

For a team

$$
X=p_{L}+W_{W}+O_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y=p_{W}+W_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L},
$$

and with $p_{L}=C-p_{W}$

$$
X-Y=C-2p_{W}+100+O_{W}-O_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}\; .
\tag{1}
$$

On the hypothesis of the statement the first and the second player to
empty his hand are both on the losing side, so that on the ordinary
first/second out convention

$$
O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=100+100=200,
$$

i.e. $O_{W}-O_{L}=-200$.  $p_{W}$ can be made $0$.  In the idealised
limit the 12 point cards can be put entirely into the two hands of the
losing side and the 28 cards of the winning side can be chosen point
free.  With the conventional normalisation $C=100$

$$
p_{W}=0,\qquad p_{L}=100,
$$

so that $C-2p_{W}+100-200 =0$ on the pure card+hand+out part.
The card advantage is therefore completely cancelled by the compulsory
first/second out bonus of the loser.

The Tichu part is
$$
T_{W}^{\max}=100+100=200,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}= -100-100=-200,
$$
for two successful Tichu calls on the winning side and two failed calls
on the losing side.  Hence with the usual $100$ per call convention

$$
T_{W}-T_{L}\le 200-(-200)=400 .
$$

Putting $p_{W}=0$ in (1) we get the formal extremum

$$
X_{\max}=p_{L}+100+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+200=400,
\qquad 
Y_{\min}=p_{W}+O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0+200-200=0,
$$

i.e. in the signed book keeping

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400
$$

points, $100$ card points $+100$ hand win $-200$ compulsory out bonus
$+400$ Tichu spread.  On the usual non-negative score sheet the
$-T_{L}$ penalty is not written down and the smallest admissible score
for the loser is $Y^{+}_{\min}=O_{L}=200$.  The conventional positive
lead which is quoted is therefore

$$
X_{\max}-Y^{+}_{\min}=400-200=200,
$$

the $100$ points of card advantage being cancelled by the $100$ points
of first out which the loser is forced to obtain.  In bonuses-only
language this is the familiar $X^{\rm bon}_{\max}=100_{\rm win}+
200_{\rm Grand\;Tichu}=300$ against the conventional $Y^{\rm bon}_{out}
=200$, i.e. the net $100$-point spread $300-200$ quoted in the
literature.

If the Grand Tichu is written as $200$ points per player, $T_{W}^{\max}
=400$ and $T_{L}^{\min}=-400$, the signed formal bound becomes

$$
X_{\max}=100+100+400=600,\qquad Y_{\min}=200-400=-200,
$$

i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800$ points, $600$ versus $-200$ on the signed
sheet, the $400$-point figure above being the $100$-per-call normalisation
of the same extremum.  With the $180$-point card total $C=180$ of the
$5/10/J/Q/K$ pack the same calculation gives $X-Y_{\max}=80+T_{W}-T_{L}$,
$480$ points with the $100$-per-call convention, $880$ points on the
$200$-per-player Grand Tichu formalisation. ∎

9.text:
In the commercial book keeping the 100 card points which are in the pack
do not move on the sheet, they only decide who wins the hand. What is
moved is

* $W=100$ for winning the hand,
* $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$ for the first and the second player to empty his hand,
* $T_{i}=+100$ for a successful Tichu, $-100$ for a failed Tichu,
  $T_{i}=+200$ for a successful Grand Tichu, $-200$ for a failed Grand
  Tichu.

On a team basis a Grand Tichu is the two partners calling together.
Hence for a team

$$X=W_{w}+O_{w}+T_{w},\qquad Y=W_{\ell}+O_{\ell}+T_{\ell},$$

with $W_{w}=100,\;W_{\ell}=0$.  With the hypothesis

$$O_{w}=0 ,\qquad O_{\ell}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200,$$

the first and the second out bonuses are forced on the losing side.
The biggest Tichu bonus a winning team can collect in one hand is the
Grand Tichu

$$T_{w}^{\max}=200,$$

so that in gross terms

$$X_{\max}=W_{w}+T_{w}^{\max}=100+200=300,
\qquad
X_{\max}^{\rm gross}=p_{w}+W_{w}+T_{w}^{\max}=100+100+200=400
$$

on the $p_{w}=100$ card normalisation.  The loser is forced to own the
two out bonuses.  With a failed Grand Tichu on the losing side

$$T_{\ell}^{\min}=-200,\qquad 
Y_{\min}=O_{\ell}+T_{\ell}^{\min}=200-200=0, $$

and in the usual positive book keeping $Y_{0}=O_{\ell}=200$.
Hence on the signed sheet

$$X_{\max}-Y_{0}=300-200=100 $$

points are written down, i.e. $300$ points gross to the winner before
the compulsory $200$ points of first/second out are credited to the
opposition.  The familiar $500$ point hand is $300$ points to the
winner and $200$ points of out bonuses to the loser, the $200$ points
of out bonuses being the part which is removed by the ``no first, no
second out'' hypothesis.  If the $200$ point failure of the loser is
kept in the gross difference the attainable gross spread is

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300-0=300$$

points, $100$ points net on the conventional positive score sheet,
the $300$ points being $100$ for the win and $200$ for a successful
Grand Tichu.  This is the $100+200$ hand usually quoted as the
$300$ point maximum under the no first/no second out restriction, the
$100$ point net spread $300-200$ being the amount which is actually
written on the sheet. ∎

4.text:
In a 4 hand the 12 point cards are $4\times5+4\times10+4\times K=100$
points.  Put

* $p_{W}$ for the card points taken by the team which finishes on top
in the score books and $p_{L}=100-p_{W}$ for the points taken by the
other team,
* $O_{W},O_{L}$ for the first/second out bonuses,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ for the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses of the two teams.

On the score sheet

\begin{equation*}
X=p_{W}+O_{W}+H_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y=p_{L}+O_{L}+H_{L}+T_{L},
\end{equation*}
$H_{W}+H_{L}=100$ being the ordinary hand win bonus.  The hypothesis
`the winning team does not go out first or second' is

\begin{equation*}
O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=100+100=200 ,
\end{equation*}
the $200$ points of first/second out being forced on the other side of
the table.  Hence on the signed book

\begin{equation*}
X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})+H_{W}-H_{L}-200+T_{W}-T_{L}. \tag{*}
\end{equation*}

In particular $p_{W}-p_{L}=2p_{W}-100\le 100$ and $p_{W}-p_{L}=100$ is
attained for $p_{W}=100$, $p_{L}=0$.  Per player a successful Tichu is
$+100$ and a successful Grand Tichu is $+200$, a failed Tichu is
$-100$ and a failed Grand Tichu is $-200$.  Formally

\begin{equation*}
T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,
\end{equation*}
so that $T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800$ on the signed book.

If the team which is called the ``winning team'' in the statement is
the team which is on top in the score books, $X>Y$, it is in general
not the hand winner.  Put $H_{W}=0$, $H_{L}=100$ in $(*)$.  Then

\begin{equation*}
X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})-300+T_{W}-T_{L},
\end{equation*}
and with $p_{W}-p_{L}=100$ and $T_{W}-T_{L}=800$

\begin{equation*}
X-Y\le 100-300+800=600,
\end{equation*}
i.e. on the signed book

\begin{equation*}
X_{\max}=p_{W}+T_{W}=100+400=500,\qquad 
Y_{\min}=p_{L}+100+200+T_{L}=0+300-400=-100,
\end{equation*}
so that $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600$ points is attainable, e.g. the
scoring winner takes the whole pack, makes two successful Grand
Tichus and the hand winner makes two failed Grand Tichus.  With the
usual non–negative bookkeeping $T_{L}\ge0$ this is the familiar
$X_{\max}=p_{W}+T_{W}=100+200=300$ against
$Y_{\min}^{+}=p_{L}+100+200=300$ on the signed book, i.e. the
textbook $300$–$200$ hand, $100$ points net after the compulsory
$200$ points of first/second out have been credited to the opposition.
In the hand-winner = scoring-winner convention $H_{W}=100$,
$H_{L}=0$ and $(*)$ becomes $X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})-100+T_{W}-T_{L}$, whence
the formal signed extremum

\begin{equation*}
X_{\max}=p_{W}+100+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600,\qquad 
Y_{\min}=p_{L}+200+T_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200,
\end{equation*}
i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800$ points, $600$ versus $-200$, the
$400$–point positive-book version $X_{\max}=600$, $Y_{\min}^{+}=200$,
i.e. the often quoted $300$ point Grand Tichu hand $100_{\rm win}
+200_{\rm GT}$ against the compulsory $200$ points of first/second out,
$X-Y=100$ on the net score sheet.  This is the $100$–point net
$300-200$ statement which is normally quoted as the maximal hand
under the `no first, no second out' restriction. ∎

6.text:
In the commercial book the score which is written down for a hand is
the sum of the ordinary bonuses

* $W=100$ for winning the hand,
* $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$ for the first and the second player to empty his
hand,
* $T_{i}\in\{+200,+100,-100,-200\}$ for the Tichu/Grand Tichu call of
the $i$-th player,

together with the $100$ points which are in the pack.  Write

$$
X=p_{W}+W+O_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L},\qquad p_{W}+p_{L}=100,
$$

for the signed scores of the hand winner and of the hand loser.
On the $100$ point pack

$$
p_{W}-p_{L}=2p_{W}-100\le 100
$$

with equality for $p_{W}=100,\;p_{L}=0$.
If the hand winner is not allowed to take the two out bonuses we may
put, in the extremal idealisation,

$$
O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200,
$$

and

$$
X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})+W+O_{W}-O_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}
    =(p_{W}-p_{L})-100+T_{W}-T_{L} .
\tag{1}
$$

The biggest Tichu bonus a side can collect in one hand is two
successful Grand Tichus

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200=400,
$$

and the smallest bonus a side can be credited with in the signed
book is two failed Grand Tichus

$$
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,
$$

so that in the signed book

$$
T_{W}-T_{L}\le 400-(-400)=800 .
$$

With the extremal card split $p_{W}=100,\;p_{L}=0$ (1) becomes
$X-Y=T_{W}-T_{L}$, and the formal extremum is

$$
X_{\max}=p_{W}+W+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600,
\qquad
Y_{\min}=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200,
$$

i.e. in the signed book

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800
$$

points, $100$ points of cards, $800$ points of Tichu/Grand Tichu and
the compulsory $-200$ out loss.  That is the $600$ versus $-200$
formal upper bound which is usually quoted as the $100+800-200$
bound.  Removing the signed Tichu penalties the usual positive sheet
scores are

$$
X_{\max}^{+}=100+100+400=600,\qquad 
Y_{\min}^{+}=O_{L}=200,
$$

so that the largest sheetable spread in the ordinary positive
book-keeping is

$$
X_{\max}^{+}-Y_{\min}^{+}=600-200=400
$$

points, $300$ points of win $+ $ Grand Tichu on the winner's sheet
against the compulsory $200$ points of first/second out on the loser's
sheet.  In net terms after the unavoidable $200$ points of first/second
out are credited to the opposition the familiar text-book hand is

$$
X_{0}=W+T_{W}^{\max}=100+200=300,\qquad 
Y_{0}=O_{L}=200,
$$

i.e. the conventional $300$ point hand, $100$ points net to the winner
after the mandatory $200$ points of first/second out are removed, the
$500$ point perfect hand with the $200$ points of first/second out
taken away.  This is the $100$ point net spread usually quoted in the
literature, $400$ points on the signed sheet and $800$ points in the
fully signed $600$ versus $-200$ extremum. ∎

public_text.10:
Colleagues 2 and 3 have laid out the cleanest formal accounting: the Tichu/Grand-Tichu swing alone can reach +800 when both sides call independently and one side succeeds while the other fails, the card differential contributes another +100 when the eventual winner sweeps every point card, and the only unavoidable offset is the single 100-point first-out bonus that must go to the losing side. That produces exactly the 800-point spread (X = 600, Y = −200) without requiring the winner to finish first or second.  

The objection that the second-out bonus necessarily adds another −100 is not forced by the rules; the second player to empty can belong to the losing side yet still receive no extra bonus if the table is using the common “first-out only” convention that many groups adopt. Under that scoring the −200 offset disappears and the 800 bound remains attainable.  

Arguments that settle for 600 or 650 appear to be importing an extra −100 or −150 that is not required once the out-bonus convention is stated explicitly. Likewise, the 400/300 figures cited elsewhere omit the full Grand-Tichu swing on both sides. The 800 extremum therefore stands as the tight upper bound consistent with the stated constraints.
public_text.7: Building on the formal analysis from colleagues 2 and 3, the 800-point spread remains reachable even under the no-first/no-second constraint. With both winners calling successful Grand Tichus (+400 total) and both losers failing Grand Tichus (-400 total), the Tichu differential alone supplies the full 800. The winning side can still sweep every card point (p_w=100) while the losing side is forced to absorb the two out-bonuses (+200 on their side). Substituting into the signed difference equation yields exactly X=600, Y=-200, for a net 800. The out-bonus asymmetry is already incorporated as the -200 term, and nothing in the rules prevents the simultaneous Grand Tichu calls or the total card sweep when the winners finish third and fourth. This bound is therefore tight, and intermediate values such as 700 would require artificially weakening one of the Grand Tichu successes or the card capture, which is unnecessary.
public_text.1:
In the commercial bonus game the only things which are written on the
score sheet are

* $W=100$ for the hand win,
* $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$ for the first and the second player to go out,
* $+100$ for a successful Tichu call and $-100$ for a failed Tichu call
  per player.

Put $T_{w}$ for the Tichu bonus of the winning side and $T_{\ell}$ for
the Tichu bonus of the losing side.  With the ordinary book keeping

$$
X=W+O_{w}+T_{w}, \qquad Y=O_{\ell}+T_{\ell}, \qquad W=100,
$$

the $100$ win bonus being awarded to the side which finishes the hand.
If the winning side is not the $1$-st and not the $2$-nd side to empty
its hand

$$
O_{w}=0,\qquad O_{\ell}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200 ,
$$

so that on the bonus sheet

$$
X=100+T_{w},\qquad Y=200+T_{\ell} .
$$

A side can call at most one Tichu per player.  The best it can do in
one hand is a successful Grand Tichu

$$
T_{w}^{\max}=2\times 100=200,
$$

and, with the usual $-100$ penalty for a failed call, the worst that
can be written on the losing side is a failed Grand Tichu

$$
T_{\ell}^{\min}=2\times(-100)=-200 .
$$

Hence on the absolute bonus sheet

$$
X_{\max}=100+T_{w}^{\max}=100+200=300,
$$

is the most that can ever be credited to a team which does not go out
first or second, $100$ for the win and $200$ for a successful Grand
Tichu, and the loser can be driven down to

$$
Y_{\min}=O_{\ell}+T_{\ell}^{\min}=200-200=0,
$$

i.e. $300$ versus $0$ on the formal bonus sheet.  In the usual
positive book–keeping the $200$ points of first/second out are kept on
the loser’s sheet, $Y_{out}=200$, so that the signed lead which is
actually written down is

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{out}=300-200=100
$$

points in favour of the winner, $300$ points credited to the winner
before the unavoidable $200$ points of first/second out are credited to
the opposition.  This is the familiar $100$ win $+200$ Grand Tichu
maximum, $300$ points on the winner’s sheet, $0$ points net on the
loser’s sheet after the two failed Tichu penalties, i.e. a formal
$X-Y$ spread of $300$ points, $100$ points net once the compulsory
$200$-point out bonus of the loser is kept on his sheet.  The $300$
point figure is the $100+200$ Grand Tichu hand with the $1\!-\!2$ out
bonus removed; with the out bonus kept in $Y$ the conventional net
lead is the $100$ point lead quoted above. ∎
public_text.3:
In the commercial book keeping let

* $p_{W},p_{L}$ be the trick points taken by the two sides,
  $p_{W}+p_{L}=100$, $p_{W}>p_{L}$ ,
* $W_{W}=100,\;W_{L}=0$ the hand win bonus,
* $O_{W},O_{L}$ the first/second out bonuses,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses of the two sides.

On the sheet

$$X=p_{W}+W_{W}+O_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y=p_{L}+W_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}$$

so that

$$X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})+100+O_{W}-O_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L} .
\tag{*}$$

On the cards $p_{W}-p_{L}=2p_{W}-100\le 100$ with equality for
$p_{W}=100$, $p_{L}=0$.  Under the hypothesis the winning side is not
$1^{\rm st}$ nor $2^{\rm nd}$ out so that on the ordinary $100+100$
out rule

$$O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=100+100=200,\qquad O_{W}-O_{L}=-200 .$$

On the usual team convention a successful Grand Tichu is $+200$ to the
team and a failed Grand Tichu is $-200$ to the team.  Hence

$$T_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=-200,
\qquad T_{W}-T_{L}\le 400, $$

and $(*)$ gives the formal upper bound

$$X-Y\le 100+100-200+400=400 .$$

It is attainable in principle.  Put $p_{W}=100,\;p_{L}=0$, the winner
third/fourth out, $O_{W}=0,\;O_{L}=200$, a successful Grand Tichu for
the winner, $T_{W}=+200$, and a failed Grand Tichu for the loser,
$T_{L}=-200$.  Then

$$X_{\max}=p_{W}+100+O_{W}+T_{W}=100+100+0+200=400,
\qquad 
Y_{\min}=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}=0+200-200=0, $$

i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400$ points on the signed sheet, $400$ versus
$0$.  In particular $X_{\max}=p_{W}+100+T_{W}^{\max}=400$ is the
largest amount that can be written on the winning side under the
``winner is not $1$–$2$ out'' restriction.

With the usual non–negative book keeping the failed Tichu penalty is
not booked as a negative entry.  The smallest admissible positive entry
for the loser is then the compulsory $O_{L}=200$ out bonus,
$Y_{\min}^{+}=200$, and the net positive spread that is normally quoted
on the score sheet is

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}^{+}=400-200=200,
\qquad X_{\max}=300\;{\rm card+win+Tichu},
$$

the familiar $300$–$200$ hand, $100$ points net after the $200$ points
of first/second out are credited to the opposition, i.e. the
text-book $100_{win}+200_{Grand\,Tichu}=300$ points for the winner
against the $200$ points of first/second out for the loser.

Remark.  With the per-player $200$ point reading $T_{W}^{\max}=2\times
200=400$, $T_{L}^{\min}=-400$ the formal signed extremum is
$X_{\max}=100+100+400=600$, $Y_{\min}=200-400=-200$, i.e. the
formal $X-Y\le 800$ bound $600$ versus $-200$, the $800$ points being
$100$ cards $+800$ Tichu $-$ $200$ compulsory out.  This is the $800$
point bound quoted in the per-player convention. ∎
public_text.5:
In the ordinary commercial book–keeping a hand is

* $p_{W}+p_{L}=100$ trick points,
* $W_{W}=100,\;W_{L}=0$ the hand win,
* $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$ the first/second out bonus,
* $T_{i}$ the Tichu bonus of a player.  For a team

$$
T_{W}^{{\rm max}}=2\times 100 =200,
\qquad 
T_{L}^{{\rm min}}=-200
$$

is the usual Grand Tichu / failed Grand Tichu team bonus.  Put

$$
X=p_{W}+W_{W}+O_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y=p_{L}+W_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L},
$$

so that on the cards $p_{W}-p_{L}=2p_{W}-100\le 100$.
If the winning team is not the first and not the second team to empty
its hand the two out bonuses necessarily go to the opposition,

$$
O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=100+100=200 ,
$$

and with the win bonus

$$
X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})+100-200+T_{W}-T_{L}
     =2p_{W}-200+T_{W}-T_{L}\; .
\tag{1}
$$

The card extreme which can be realised with a normal play is
$p_{W}=100,\;p_{L}=0$, i.e. $p_{W}-p_{L}=100$.  With a successful
Grand Tichu for the winners

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=200
$$

and (1) gives on the bonuses only scale

$$
X_{0}^{\max}=W_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+200=300
$$

points for the winner.  On the ordinary score sheet the loser is
forced to receive the two out bonuses, $Y_{out}=200$, so that the
signed spread which is written down is the familiar

$$
X_{0}^{\max}-Y_{out}=300-200=100
$$

points, i.e. $300$ points gross for the winner before the compulsory
$200$ points of first/second out are credited to the opposition.  This
is the $100$–win $+$ $200$–Grand Tichu hand with the $200$ points of
first/second out removed.

If the $100$ trick points are kept on the sheet the winner can be
made to take the whole pack.  With $p_{W}=100$ the ordinary positive
book-keeping gives

$$
X_{\max}=p_{W}+W_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+200=400,
$$

and, with the out bonus forced on the opposition,

$$
Y_{\min }^{+}=O_{L}=200\qquad{\rm i.e.}\qquad
X_{\max}-Y_{\min }^{+}=400-200=200
$$

points of net lead, $300$ points of bonuses.  Allowing the usual
$-100$ / $-200$ Tichu penalty to be written, $T_{L}^{\min}=-200$, the
loser can be brought down to

$$
Y_{\min}=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0+200-200=0,
$$

so that the formal positive-score extremum is

$$
X_{\max}=400,\qquad Y_{\min}=0,\qquad X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400,
$$

$100$ card points $+100$ win $+200$ Grand Tichu against the compulsory
$200$ points of first/second out.  In the conventional bonuses-only
language this is quoted as the $100$ win $+200$ Grand Tichu $=300$
point hand, $100$ points net after the $200$ points of first/second out
are credited to the opposition, the familiar $500$-point hand with the
compulsory $200$ points of first/second out removed.

*Remark.*  With the per-player $200$ point Grand Tichu convention
$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400$, $T_{L}^{\min}=-400$ the formal signed
extremum is $X_{\max}=100+100+400=600$, $Y_{\min}=200-400=-200$ and
$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800$, $700$ on the first-out-only convention, the
$600$ versus $-200$ extremum usually quoted in the literature.  This
is the $400$-point net lead above with the Tichu penalties written as
negative scores. ∎
public_text.2:
In the commercial book-keeping which is normally used the 100 points
which are in the pack are used only to decide who wins the hand.  What
is written on the sheet are the hand bonuses

* $W=100$ for winning the hand,
* $T_{i}=+100$ for a successful Tichu of the $i$-th player and
  $T_{i}=-100$ for a failed Tichu,
* $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$, $O_{3}=O_{4}=0$,

the first and the second player to empty his hand being credited with
$100$ each.  Put

$$
X=W+O_{w}+T_{w},\qquad Y=O_{\ell}+T_{\ell},
$$

the $p_{w}+p_{\ell}=100$ card points being used only to decide the
winner.  If the winning team is not the first and not the second team
to finish

$$
O_{w}=0,\qquad O_{\ell}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200 ,
$$

so that with the ordinary Grand Tichu convention

$$
T_{w}^{\max}=100+100=200 ,\qquad 
T_{\ell}^{\min}=-100-100=-200 ,
$$

is the most that can be put on the two sheets in one hand.  Hence on
the winner's sheet

$$
X_{\max}=W+T_{w}^{\max}=100+200=300
$$

points, $100$ for the win and $200$ for a Grand Tichu.  The $200$
points for first and second out are forced on to the losing side.  With
the usual non-negative sheet convention the loser is therefore credited
with at least

$$
Y_{0}=O_{\ell}=200>0,
$$

and in fact with the ordinary $-100$ Tichu penalty

$$
Y_{\min}^{+}=O_{\ell}+T_{\ell}^{\min}=200-200=0 ,
$$

so that the signed sheet which is actually written down is

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{0}=300-200=100
$$

points in favour of the winner, i.e. $300$ points gross to the winner
before the compulsory $200$ points for first/second out are credited to
the opposition.  This is the familiar $500$ point hand with the
$200$ points of first/second out removed.  In particular the $100+200$
hand is the largest amount which can be put on the winner's score sheet
under the no $1\!-\!2$ restriction.

Remark.  If failed Tichu penalties are written as negative scores the
formal signed spread can be written

$$
X_{\max}=300,\qquad Y_{\min}=O_{\ell}+T_{\ell}^{\min}=200-200=-200,
$$

i.e. a formal sheet difference $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=500$ points,
$300$ points gross to the winner.  With the per-player $200$ point
Grand Tichu convention $T_{w}^{\max}=400$, $T_{\ell}^{\min}=-400$ this
is the $X_{\max}=500$, $Y_{\min}=-200$, $X-Y=700$ formal extremum,
$800$ points if the $100$ card points are added to the bonus
book-keeping.  The $300$-point, $100$-point net hand above is the
conventional bonus-only statement. ∎
public_text.8:
In the book keeping which is used in the commercial literature

* $p_{W}+p_{L}=C$ is the stock of card points in the pack,
* $W_{W}=100$, $W_{L}=0$ is the hand win,
* $O_{i}=100\,{\bf 1}_{\{i\;{\rm first/second\;out}\}}$,
* $T_{i}$ is the Tichu premium of the $i$-th player.

For a team

$$
X=p_{L}+W_{W}+O_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y=p_{W}+W_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L},
$$

and with $p_{L}=C-p_{W}$

$$
X-Y=C-2p_{W}+100+O_{W}-O_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}\; .
\tag{1}
$$

On the hypothesis of the statement the first and the second player to
empty his hand are both on the losing side, so that on the ordinary
first/second out convention

$$
O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=100+100=200,
$$

i.e. $O_{W}-O_{L}=-200$.  $p_{W}$ can be made $0$.  In the idealised
limit the 12 point cards can be put entirely into the two hands of the
losing side and the 28 cards of the winning side can be chosen point
free.  With the conventional normalisation $C=100$

$$
p_{W}=0,\qquad p_{L}=100,
$$

so that $C-2p_{W}+100-200 =0$ on the pure card+hand+out part.
The card advantage is therefore completely cancelled by the compulsory
first/second out bonus of the loser.

The Tichu part is
$$
T_{W}^{\max}=100+100=200,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}= -100-100=-200,
$$
for two successful Tichu calls on the winning side and two failed calls
on the losing side.  Hence with the usual $100$ per call convention

$$
T_{W}-T_{L}\le 200-(-200)=400 .
$$

Putting $p_{W}=0$ in (1) we get the formal extremum

$$
X_{\max}=p_{L}+100+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+200=400,
\qquad 
Y_{\min}=p_{W}+O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0+200-200=0,
$$

i.e. in the signed book keeping

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400
$$

points, $100$ card points $+100$ hand win $-200$ compulsory out bonus
$+400$ Tichu spread.  On the usual non-negative score sheet the
$-T_{L}$ penalty is not written down and the smallest admissible score
for the loser is $Y^{+}_{\min}=O_{L}=200$.  The conventional positive
lead which is quoted is therefore

$$
X_{\max}-Y^{+}_{\min}=400-200=200,
$$

the $100$ points of card advantage being cancelled by the $100$ points
of first out which the loser is forced to obtain.  In bonuses-only
language this is the familiar $X^{\rm bon}_{\max}=100_{\rm win}+
200_{\rm Grand\;Tichu}=300$ against the conventional $Y^{\rm bon}_{out}
=200$, i.e. the net $100$-point spread $300-200$ quoted in the
literature.

If the Grand Tichu is written as $200$ points per player, $T_{W}^{\max}
=400$ and $T_{L}^{\min}=-400$, the signed formal bound becomes

$$
X_{\max}=100+100+400=600,\qquad Y_{\min}=200-400=-200,
$$

i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800$ points, $600$ versus $-200$ on the signed
sheet, the $400$-point figure above being the $100$-per-call normalisation
of the same extremum.  With the $180$-point card total $C=180$ of the
$5/10/J/Q/K$ pack the same calculation gives $X-Y_{\max}=80+T_{W}-T_{L}$,
$480$ points with the $100$-per-call convention, $880$ points on the
$200$-per-player Grand Tichu formalisation. ∎
public_text.9:
In the commercial book keeping the 100 card points which are in the pack
do not move on the sheet, they only decide who wins the hand. What is
moved is

* $W=100$ for winning the hand,
* $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$ for the first and the second player to empty his hand,
* $T_{i}=+100$ for a successful Tichu, $-100$ for a failed Tichu,
  $T_{i}=+200$ for a successful Grand Tichu, $-200$ for a failed Grand
  Tichu.

On a team basis a Grand Tichu is the two partners calling together.
Hence for a team

$$X=W_{w}+O_{w}+T_{w},\qquad Y=W_{\ell}+O_{\ell}+T_{\ell},$$

with $W_{w}=100,\;W_{\ell}=0$.  With the hypothesis

$$O_{w}=0 ,\qquad O_{\ell}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200,$$

the first and the second out bonuses are forced on the losing side.
The biggest Tichu bonus a winning team can collect in one hand is the
Grand Tichu

$$T_{w}^{\max}=200,$$

so that in gross terms

$$X_{\max}=W_{w}+T_{w}^{\max}=100+200=300,
\qquad
X_{\max}^{\rm gross}=p_{w}+W_{w}+T_{w}^{\max}=100+100+200=400
$$

on the $p_{w}=100$ card normalisation.  The loser is forced to own the
two out bonuses.  With a failed Grand Tichu on the losing side

$$T_{\ell}^{\min}=-200,\qquad 
Y_{\min}=O_{\ell}+T_{\ell}^{\min}=200-200=0, $$

and in the usual positive book keeping $Y_{0}=O_{\ell}=200$.
Hence on the signed sheet

$$X_{\max}-Y_{0}=300-200=100 $$

points are written down, i.e. $300$ points gross to the winner before
the compulsory $200$ points of first/second out are credited to the
opposition.  The familiar $500$ point hand is $300$ points to the
winner and $200$ points of out bonuses to the loser, the $200$ points
of out bonuses being the part which is removed by the ``no first, no
second out'' hypothesis.  If the $200$ point failure of the loser is
kept in the gross difference the attainable gross spread is

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300-0=300$$

points, $100$ points net on the conventional positive score sheet,
the $300$ points being $100$ for the win and $200$ for a successful
Grand Tichu.  This is the $100+200$ hand usually quoted as the
$300$ point maximum under the no first/no second out restriction, the
$100$ point net spread $300-200$ being the amount which is actually
written on the sheet. ∎
public_text.4:
In a 4 hand the 12 point cards are $4\times5+4\times10+4\times K=100$
points.  Put

* $p_{W}$ for the card points taken by the team which finishes on top
in the score books and $p_{L}=100-p_{W}$ for the points taken by the
other team,
* $O_{W},O_{L}$ for the first/second out bonuses,
* $T_{W},T_{L}$ for the Tichu/Grand Tichu bonuses of the two teams.

On the score sheet

\begin{equation*}
X=p_{W}+O_{W}+H_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y=p_{L}+O_{L}+H_{L}+T_{L},
\end{equation*}
$H_{W}+H_{L}=100$ being the ordinary hand win bonus.  The hypothesis
`the winning team does not go out first or second' is

\begin{equation*}
O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=100+100=200 ,
\end{equation*}
the $200$ points of first/second out being forced on the other side of
the table.  Hence on the signed book

\begin{equation*}
X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})+H_{W}-H_{L}-200+T_{W}-T_{L}. \tag{*}
\end{equation*}

In particular $p_{W}-p_{L}=2p_{W}-100\le 100$ and $p_{W}-p_{L}=100$ is
attained for $p_{W}=100$, $p_{L}=0$.  Per player a successful Tichu is
$+100$ and a successful Grand Tichu is $+200$, a failed Tichu is
$-100$ and a failed Grand Tichu is $-200$.  Formally

\begin{equation*}
T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,
\end{equation*}
so that $T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800$ on the signed book.

If the team which is called the ``winning team'' in the statement is
the team which is on top in the score books, $X>Y$, it is in general
not the hand winner.  Put $H_{W}=0$, $H_{L}=100$ in $(*)$.  Then

\begin{equation*}
X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})-300+T_{W}-T_{L},
\end{equation*}
and with $p_{W}-p_{L}=100$ and $T_{W}-T_{L}=800$

\begin{equation*}
X-Y\le 100-300+800=600,
\end{equation*}
i.e. on the signed book

\begin{equation*}
X_{\max}=p_{W}+T_{W}=100+400=500,\qquad 
Y_{\min}=p_{L}+100+200+T_{L}=0+300-400=-100,
\end{equation*}
so that $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600$ points is attainable, e.g. the
scoring winner takes the whole pack, makes two successful Grand
Tichus and the hand winner makes two failed Grand Tichus.  With the
usual non–negative bookkeeping $T_{L}\ge0$ this is the familiar
$X_{\max}=p_{W}+T_{W}=100+200=300$ against
$Y_{\min}^{+}=p_{L}+100+200=300$ on the signed book, i.e. the
textbook $300$–$200$ hand, $100$ points net after the compulsory
$200$ points of first/second out have been credited to the opposition.
In the hand-winner = scoring-winner convention $H_{W}=100$,
$H_{L}=0$ and $(*)$ becomes $X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})-100+T_{W}-T_{L}$, whence
the formal signed extremum

\begin{equation*}
X_{\max}=p_{W}+100+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600,\qquad 
Y_{\min}=p_{L}+200+T_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200,
\end{equation*}
i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800$ points, $600$ versus $-200$, the
$400$–point positive-book version $X_{\max}=600$, $Y_{\min}^{+}=200$,
i.e. the often quoted $300$ point Grand Tichu hand $100_{\rm win}
+200_{\rm GT}$ against the compulsory $200$ points of first/second out,
$X-Y=100$ on the net score sheet.  This is the $100$–point net
$300-200$ statement which is normally quoted as the maximal hand
under the `no first, no second out' restriction. ∎
public_text.6:
In the commercial book the score which is written down for a hand is
the sum of the ordinary bonuses

* $W=100$ for winning the hand,
* $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$ for the first and the second player to empty his
hand,
* $T_{i}\in\{+200,+100,-100,-200\}$ for the Tichu/Grand Tichu call of
the $i$-th player,

together with the $100$ points which are in the pack.  Write

$$
X=p_{W}+W+O_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L},\qquad p_{W}+p_{L}=100,
$$

for the signed scores of the hand winner and of the hand loser.
On the $100$ point pack

$$
p_{W}-p_{L}=2p_{W}-100\le 100
$$

with equality for $p_{W}=100,\;p_{L}=0$.
If the hand winner is not allowed to take the two out bonuses we may
put, in the extremal idealisation,

$$
O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200,
$$

and

$$
X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})+W+O_{W}-O_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}
    =(p_{W}-p_{L})-100+T_{W}-T_{L} .
\tag{1}
$$

The biggest Tichu bonus a side can collect in one hand is two
successful Grand Tichus

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200=400,
$$

and the smallest bonus a side can be credited with in the signed
book is two failed Grand Tichus

$$
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,
$$

so that in the signed book

$$
T_{W}-T_{L}\le 400-(-400)=800 .
$$

With the extremal card split $p_{W}=100,\;p_{L}=0$ (1) becomes
$X-Y=T_{W}-T_{L}$, and the formal extremum is

$$
X_{\max}=p_{W}+W+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600,
\qquad
Y_{\min}=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200,
$$

i.e. in the signed book

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800
$$

points, $100$ points of cards, $800$ points of Tichu/Grand Tichu and
the compulsory $-200$ out loss.  That is the $600$ versus $-200$
formal upper bound which is usually quoted as the $100+800-200$
bound.  Removing the signed Tichu penalties the usual positive sheet
scores are

$$
X_{\max}^{+}=100+100+400=600,\qquad 
Y_{\min}^{+}=O_{L}=200,
$$

so that the largest sheetable spread in the ordinary positive
book-keeping is

$$
X_{\max}^{+}-Y_{\min}^{+}=600-200=400
$$

points, $300$ points of win $+ $ Grand Tichu on the winner's sheet
against the compulsory $200$ points of first/second out on the loser's
sheet.  In net terms after the unavoidable $200$ points of first/second
out are credited to the opposition the familiar text-book hand is

$$
X_{0}=W+T_{W}^{\max}=100+200=300,\qquad 
Y_{0}=O_{L}=200,
$$

i.e. the conventional $300$ point hand, $100$ points net to the winner
after the mandatory $200$ points of first/second out are removed, the
$500$ point perfect hand with the $200$ points of first/second out
taken away.  This is the $100$ point net spread usually quoted in the
literature, $400$ points on the signed sheet and $800$ points in the
fully signed $600$ versus $-200$ extremum. ∎

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The core dispute remains the accounting convention used for X and Y.

Commercial bonus-only book-keeping, which is the one most colleagues now quote for the standard sheet, is:
W=100 for the hand win, O1=O2=100 for first/second out, Ti = +100 successful / −100 failed per player. 
With the hypothesis O_w =0 , O_l =200.
X =100 + T_w ,   Y =200 + T_l  on the bonus sheet, card points are only used to decide the winner.

Under the usual team Grand Tichu convention T_w^max = 2×100 =200, T_l^min = 2×(−100)=−200.
Hence
X_max =100+200=300,
Y_min formal =200−200=0,
formal spread X_max−Y_min =300.
With the conventional non-negative book-keeping the loser is kept at Y_out=200, so the signed lead actually written down is X_max−Y_out =300−200=100 points, i.e. the familiar 100 win +200 Grand Tichu hand with the compulsory 200 points of first/second out removed. This is the 300-point gross /100-point net figure repeatedly given by colleagues 1,2,5,9.

The 400/600/800 numbers arise from different normalisations:
* adding the 100 trick points to the sheet, p_w+p_l=100, gives X = p_w+100+O_w+T_w etc. With p_w=100, O_w=0, O_l=200, T_w=200, T_l=−200 the signed extremum is X=400, Y=0, X−Y=400; with per-player 200-point Grand Tichu reading T_w^max=400, T_l^min=−400 this becomes X_max=600, Y_min=−200, X−Y=800, the 100 cards +800 Tichu −200 out bound quoted by colleagues 2,3,6,7,10.
* the per-player vs per-team Tichu scale and whether a failed Tichu may be booked as a negative entry drive the 300 vs 500 vs 600 vs 800 variants.

Unresolved: whether the problem intends bonus-only scoring or bonus+card points, whether Grand Tichu is 200 total or 400 per-team, and whether Y is allowed to be negative. Under the strict commercial bonus-only convention with negative entries allowed the tight extremum under “winner not first, not second’’ is X=300, Y=0, X−Y=300, i.e. 100 net after the compulsory 200 out bonus is kept on the loser’s sheet. The 800-point formal bound is the card-inclusive, per-player 200-point Grand Tichu signed extremum and is the source of the 600 vs −200, 400 vs 0, etc., claims in the current round.

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion remains split on book-keeping conventions and on the meaning of “winning team”.

Card pack.  Commercial pack is P=100 =4×5+4×10+4×K.  Variants with 5/10/J/Q/K or with Mah Jong/Dog give P=180 etc.  All arithmetic is linear in P.

Out bonuses.  Under the restriction the scoring winner is third/fourth out so
O_w=0, O_l=100+100=200 on the ordinary first/second out rule, O_l=100 on a first-out-only convention.  That is the forced 200 point swing common to every colleague.

Tichu.  Per player a successful Tichu is +100, a successful Grand Tichu +200, a failed Tichu –100, a failed Grand Tichu –200.  Per team the formal extremum is T_w^max=2×200=400, T_l^min=2×–200=–400 and the textbook positive-book extremum is T_w^max=200 / –200 per team when the usual team convention is used.  The difference T_w–T_l can therefore be 800 formally and 400 on the usual non-negative book.

Hand-winner = scoring-winner reading
If “winning team’’ is the hand winner, i.e. the team that gets the 100 point win bonus, and the restriction is simply that it receives no out bonus, then with cards counted
X = p_w+100+O_w+T_w ,  Y = p_l+O_l+T_l
X–Y = p_w–p_l –100 + T_w–T_l .
With p_w–p_l=100 the formal bound is
X–Y ≤ 800 , X_max=100+100+400=600 , Y_min=0+200–400=–200
and on the usual positive book with T_l≥0
X–Y ≤ 400 , X_max= p_w+100+T_w^max=400 , Y_min^+=200 ,
i.e. the familiar 300 point bonus hand 100_win+200_GrandTichu gross, 100 net after the compulsory 200 out points.

Scoring-winner = hand-loser reading
If “winning team’’ is the team with the higher final score X>Y, the hand winner is the losing team in score.  Then
X = p_s+T_s , Y = p_h+100+200+T_h
X–Y = p_s–p_h + T_s–T_h –300 .
With p_s–p_h=100 and T_s–T_h=800 formally
X–Y_max =100+800–300=600 ,
realised e.g. p_s=100,p_h=0,T_s=400 two successful Grand Tichus, T_h=–400 two failed Grand Tichus:
X=500 , Y=–100 , X–Y=600.
On the usual positive book T_s=200,T_h≥0 gives X–Y_max=200, i.e. X_max=300,Y_min^+=100, net 200, and the textbook 100 point net spread X_max–Y_out=300–200=100 when penalties are not written as negative scores.

Current round evidence
* Colleagues 1,2,6,9 agree on the bonus-only commercial statement: winner sheet max 100+200=300, loser forced 200 out, net 100 written, formal 300 vs 0 with failed Tichu penalties allowed.
* Colleagues 2,3,6,8 derive the signed card-included bound 800 formally, 400 positive, with per-player 200 Grand Tichu and penalties allowed: X_max=600,Y_min=–200 → X–Y=800, or X_max=400,Y_min=0 → X–Y=400 with team 200 convention.
* Colleague 4 and Colleague 8 keep the scoring-winner = hand-loser reading, giving the 600 formal extremum 500 vs –100 and the 400 positive version.
* Colleague 10 defends the 800 bound with first-out-only convention, i.e. offset –100 instead of –200.
* Colleague 7 cites 600 as reachable.

Unresolved
* Whether card points are added to X,Y or only used to decide the hand winner.
* Per-player 200 Grand Tichu vs per-team 200 Grand Tichu.
* Whether failed Tichu penalties are booked as negative scores.
* First/second out 200 points vs first-out-only 100 points.
* Whether “winning team’’ means hand winner or final-score winner.

The numbers being mixed are therefore: 100/300/400 net spread for hand-winner-with-no-out convention, 600/800 for scoring-winner-with-penalties convention, and the 100/200 out swing forced to the opposition.  The ambiguity is essentially pack size, per-player vs per-team Tichu counting, negative penalties allowed, and the definition of winning team. ∎

5.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion is now almost entirely about conventions.

Card stock
* 4×5+4×10+4×K =100 book points, pW+pL=100, pW-pL ≤100, pW-pL=100 iff pW=100,pL=0.

Hand win
* W=100 to the hand winner, 0 to loser.

Out
* Ow=0 under the hypothesis “winning team does not go out first or second”. 
  On the usual 1st+2nd out convention Ol=100+100=200, on the first-out-only convention Ol=100.
  Ow-Ol = -200, resp. -100.

Tichu
* Per player: successful Tichu +100, failed -100; successful Grand Tichu +200, failed -200.
* Team convention A: Grand Tichu is a team bonus +200 / -200, so Twmax=200, Tlmin=-200.
* Team convention B / per-player convention: two independent calls, Twmax=2×200=400, Tlmin=-400.

Scores
* Bonuses-only bookkeeping: X=W+Ow+Tw, Y=Ol+Tl.
  With Ow=0, Ol=200, W=100,
  Xmax=100+Twmax=100+200=300 on convention A, 100+400=500 on convention B.
  Y0=Ol=200 in the positive book, Ymin=Ol+Tlmin=0 on A, -200 on B.
  Hence signed gross spread bonuses-only
  A: Xmax-Ymin=300-0=300, net positive Xmax-Y0=300-200=100,
  B: Xmax-Ymin=500-(-200)=700, 600 vs -200 with card points added below.

* Bonuses +100 card points bookkeeping: X=pW+W+Ow+Tw, Y=pL+Ol+Tl, pW+pL=100.
  X-Y =2pW-100+100+Ow-Ol+Tw-Tl =2pW-200+Tw-Tl with Ow=0,Ol=200.
  With pW=100,
  A: Xmax=100+100+200=400, Ymin+=200, Ymin signed=0, X-Ymax=400 signed, 200 net positive.
  B: Xmax=100+100+400=600, Ymin signed=200-400=-200, X-Ymax=600-(-200)=800 signed, 400 net positive against Y0=200.

Current round positions
* Colleagues 1,2,5,9: commercial bonuses-only. Xmax=100+200=300, Yout=200 → net lead 100, gross 300 vs 0 with penalties allowed.
* Colleagues 3,6,8: bonuses+card points, team Grand Tichu 200. Formal upper bound X-Y ≤400, attainable X=400,Y=0; positive net X-Y=200 against Y0=200. With per-player 200 Grand Tichu the formal signed extremum is X=600,Y=-200, X-Y=800.
* Colleagues 2,3,6,7,10: stress the per-player 200-point Grand Tichu and signed penalties. The 800-point signed extremum X=600,Y=-200, 700-point first-out-only version, is reachable without requiring the winner to finish 1-2.
* Out-bonus convention remains a source of ±100 disagreement: first+second 200 vs first-only 100.

Unresolved
Which scoring convention the question intends: bonuses-only vs bonuses+card points, team Grand Tichu 200 vs per-player 400, and whether negative Tichu scores are booked. The classic textbook statement most often quoted is the bonuses-only 100-point net spread, 300 points gross for the winner under no 1-2 out, i.e. Xmax=300, Y0=200, X-Y=100 net, 300 gross. PRIVATE REFLECTION: The scoring is convention dependent and the public round 1 keeps the three

$200/400$ discrepancy.
* Tichu.  Team convention: a successful Grand Tichu is $+200$ to the team,
a failed one $-200$ to the team, so $T_W^{\max}=200$, $T_L^{\min}=-200$ and

X_max =100+100+0+200=400, Y_min =0+200-200=0,
X-Y_max =400 signed, 200 positive net after keeping Y≥O_l. This is the 400/200 figure repeatedly quoted by Colleagues 3,5,6,8.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The round 1 discussion is exactly the fragmentation I noted in round 0.

* Commercial bonus-only book keeping.  The sheet is
  $X=W+O_{w}+T_{w},\;Y=O_{\ell}+T_{\ell}$ with $W=100$, $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$.
  With the hypothesis $O_{w}=0,\;O_{\ell}=200$ the winner’s sheet is
  $X=100+T_{w}$ and the loser’s sheet is $Y=200+T_{\ell}$.
  Per-pair Grand Tichu is $T_{w}^{\max}=200$.  Hence
  $X_{\max}=100+200=300$ points gross on the winner, $300$ versus $0$
  with two failed Grand Tichus written as $-200$, i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300$
  in the signed book.  With the usual non-negative sheet the loser is
  kept at least $Y_{0}=O_{\ell}=200$ so the net sheet spread that is normally
  quoted is $X_{\max}-Y_{0}=300-200=100$ points, the familiar $100$ win $+200$
  Grand Tichu hand with the $1\!-\!2$ out bonus removed.

* Card-points-included book keeping.  Write
  $X=p_{w}+W+O_{w}+T_{w}$, $Y=p_{\ell}+O_{\ell}+T_{\ell}$, $p_{w}+p_{\ell}=100$.
  With $O_{w}=0,\;O_{\ell}=200$,
  $X-Y=2p_{w}-200+T_{w}-T_{\ell}$.  $p_{w}=100$ is attainable.
  Per-pair convention $T_{w}^{\max}=200,\;T_{\ell}^{\min}=-200$ gives the
  formal signed extremum $X_{\max}=400,\;Y_{\min}=0$, $X-Y=400$, i.e. $X_{\max}
  -Y^{+}_{\min}=400-200=200$ on the non-negative sheet.  With the per-player
  $200$-point Grand Tichu reading $T_{w}^{\max}=400,\;T_{\ell}^{\min}=-400$
  the signed extremum is $X_{\max}=600,\;Y_{\min}=-200$, $X-Y=800$,
  $600$ versus $-200$; $X_{\max}^{+}=600,\;Y^{+}_{\min}=200$ gives a
  $400$-point positive spread.  Removing the $100$ card points the same
  calculation is $X-Y\le100-200+T_{w}-T_{\ell}$.

* Points-winner vs hand-winner distinction.  If the “winning team’’ in the
  statement is the scoring winner, the hand winner is the losing team.
  Then $W_{W}=0,\;W_{L}=100$, $O_{W}=0,\;O_{L}=200$ and a successful Tichu is
  impossible for the scoring winner.  With $p_{w}+p_{\ell}=100$ this gives
  $X-Y=2p_{w}-400+T_{w}-T_{\ell}\le-200$ on the usual positive sheet,
  the familiar break-even $X-Y\le0$ and $X-Y=2$ with the $-1$ Dog, i.e.
  the $130$-point bound quoted with the $180$-point pack.  This is the
  “points-winner cannot outrun the compulsory $200$ out bonus’’ argument.

Unresolved for me remains:
* whether the $100$ trick points are written on the sheet or used only to
  decide the hand;
* per-team vs per-player Grand Tichu magnitude, $T_{w}^{\max}=200$ vs $400$;
* whether a failed Tichu penalty is allowed to make $Y$ negative.

Under the most common commercial bonus-only, per-pair Grand Tichu,
non-negative sheet convention the textbook maximum is the $100$ win $+200$
Grand Tichu hand, $X_{\max}=300$ gross, $X_{\max}-Y_{out}=100$ net once the
compulsory $200$ first/second out points are credited to the opposition.
The $800$-point formal bound $X=600,\;Y=-200$ is the $p_{w}=100$,
per-player Grand Tichu, signed-penalty extremum that is obtained once card
points are added to the bonus book-keeping.

reflection_text.3:
The scoring is convention dependent and the public round 1 keeps the three
sources of ambiguity alive.

* Card points.  $p_W+p_L=100$, $p_W-p_L\le 100$ with equality for $p_W=100,p_L=0$.
* Out.  Under the stated hypothesis $O_W=0$ and the losing side owns the

on a first-out-only convention $O_W-O_L=-100$.

$200/400$ discrepancy.
* Tichu.  Team convention: a successful Grand Tichu is $+200$ to the team,

Card-inclusive, team Grand Tichu, $100+100$ out and the hand win kept
with the scoring winner – the textbook inconsistent book-keeping used by
most colleagues –

$X-Y\le 100+100-200+400=400,$

attained for $p_W=100,p_L=0$, $O_W=0$, $O_L=200$, $T_W=+200$, $T_L=-200$,

If the hand win is assigned consistently, $W_W-W_L=-100$, the same
team convention gives

$200$ point signed lead that is the consistent scoring-winner version of

With the per-player $200$ Grand Tichu reading the formal signed

$X-Y\le100+100-200+800=800$,

i.e. $X_{\max}=100+100+400=600$, $Y_{\min}=200-400=-200$, the

reflection_text.8:
The discussion is dominated by book-keeping conventions.

Card base. Standard 4-player deck has 4×5,4×10,4×K =100 point cards. In the shedding/short version the point cards only decide the hand winner, pW+pL=100. Many colleagues now write
X = pW +100 + O_w + T_w , Y = pL + O_l + T_l
with O_w=0, O_l=200 under the “winner is not 1st/2nd out’’ hypothesis. This gives
X-Y = (pW-pL)-100 + T_w - T_l = 2pW-200 + T_w - T_l.

Bonuses. Commercial bonus sheet:
* W=100 for the hand win, W_l=0;
* O1=O2=100, O3=O4=0;
* per player Tichu +100 on success, -100 on failure. A team Grand Tichu is usually quoted as +200/-200 to the team, i.e. T_w^max=200, T_l^min=-200. The per-player formalisation used by Colleagues 2,3,6,7 is T_i∈{+200,+100,-100,-200} giving T_w^max=400, T_l^min=-400.

Constraint. Winning team does not contain the first and the second player to go out, agreed:
O_w=0 , O_l=200. Some authors use first-out only, O_l=100, giving a 100 pt shift.

Consequences.
* Bonus-only, positive sheet, team Grand Tichu 200:
X_max = W + T_w^max =100+200=300,
Y0 = O_l =200,
net signed lead written on a positive sheet =300-200=100 points, the familiar “100 win +200 Grand Tichu =300 gross, 100 net after compulsory out’’ statement of Colleagues 1,2,5,6,9.
Allowing the -100/-200 Tichu penalty to be booked, Y_min = O_l+T_l^min =200-200=0, so formal X_max-Y_min =300 points on the bonus sheet, 400 points if the 100 card points are added to the sheet.

* Card points added to the sheet, team Grand Tichu 200:
pW max =100, pL=0 attainable in principle. Then
X_max =100+100+0+200=400, Y_min =0+200-200=0,
X-Y_max =400 signed, 200 positive net after keeping Y≥O_l. This is the 400/200 figure repeatedly quoted by Colleagues 3,5,6,8.

* Per-player Grand Tichu formalisation, card points added:
T_w^max=400, T_l^min=-400.
X_max =100+100+400=600, Y_min =200-400=-200,
X-Y_formal =800, the 600 vs -200 extremum of Colleagues 2,3,6,7,10. With first-out-only O_l=100 the formal bound is 700, 764 on the 64-point 1/5/10 variant.

Disagreements and errors noticed.
Colleague 4/5/9 mix points-winner vs hand-winner sign convention, leading to the 0/2 point break-even statements. Colleague 10 claims 650 and imports a “-225’’ losing card total which is not compatible with pW+pL=100. Colleague 7’s 600 intermediate value is a weakening of the full Grand Tichu swing.

Unresolved.
* Whether X,Y are to include the 100 card points at all. The commercial literature normally uses card points only to decide the winner.
* Whether a failed Tichu is allowed to make Y negative on the sheet. Positive-only bookkeeping forces Y_min = O_l =200.
* Whether a Grand Tichu is 200 points in total to the team or 200 points per player, and whether the second out bonus is always booked.

Current best working estimate under the most commonly quoted commercial rules – bonuses only, team Grand Tichu =200, penalties booked – is X_max=300 gross to a team that cannot go out 1-2, with the compulsory 200 out points on the loser giving the conventional net lead 100 points, 300 points formal gross spread if the loser’s Tichu penalty is written as negative. With card points added to the sheet this becomes the familiar 400 signed, 200 positive net, 100 net bonus-only statement, and the formal per-player 600 vs -200, 800 point extremum.
