reflection_text.2:
The round 1 discussion is exactly the fragmentation I noted in round 0.

* Commercial bonus-only book keeping.  The sheet is
  $X=W+O_{w}+T_{w},\;Y=O_{\ell}+T_{\ell}$ with $W=100$, $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$.
  With the hypothesis $O_{w}=0,\;O_{\ell}=200$ the winner’s sheet is
  $X=100+T_{w}$ and the loser’s sheet is $Y=200+T_{\ell}$.
  Per-pair Grand Tichu is $T_{w}^{\max}=200$.  Hence
  $X_{\max}=100+200=300$ points gross on the winner, $300$ versus $0$
  with two failed Grand Tichus written as $-200$, i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300$
  in the signed book.  With the usual non-negative sheet the loser is
  kept at least $Y_{0}=O_{\ell}=200$ so the net sheet spread that is normally
  quoted is $X_{\max}-Y_{0}=300-200=100$ points, the familiar $100$ win $+200$
  Grand Tichu hand with the $1\!-\!2$ out bonus removed.

* Card-points-included book keeping.  Write
  $X=p_{w}+W+O_{w}+T_{w}$, $Y=p_{\ell}+O_{\ell}+T_{\ell}$, $p_{w}+p_{\ell}=100$.
  With $O_{w}=0,\;O_{\ell}=200$,
  $X-Y=2p_{w}-200+T_{w}-T_{\ell}$.  $p_{w}=100$ is attainable.
  Per-pair convention $T_{w}^{\max}=200,\;T_{\ell}^{\min}=-200$ gives the
  formal signed extremum $X_{\max}=400,\;Y_{\min}=0$, $X-Y=400$, i.e. $X_{\max}
  -Y^{+}_{\min}=400-200=200$ on the non-negative sheet.  With the per-player
  $200$-point Grand Tichu reading $T_{w}^{\max}=400,\;T_{\ell}^{\min}=-400$
  the signed extremum is $X_{\max}=600,\;Y_{\min}=-200$, $X-Y=800$,
  $600$ versus $-200$; $X_{\max}^{+}=600,\;Y^{+}_{\min}=200$ gives a
  $400$-point positive spread.  Removing the $100$ card points the same
  calculation is $X-Y\le100-200+T_{w}-T_{\ell}$.

* Points-winner vs hand-winner distinction.  If the “winning team’’ in the
  statement is the scoring winner, the hand winner is the losing team.
  Then $W_{W}=0,\;W_{L}=100$, $O_{W}=0,\;O_{L}=200$ and a successful Tichu is
  impossible for the scoring winner.  With $p_{w}+p_{\ell}=100$ this gives
  $X-Y=2p_{w}-400+T_{w}-T_{\ell}\le-200$ on the usual positive sheet,
  the familiar break-even $X-Y\le0$ and $X-Y=2$ with the $-1$ Dog, i.e.
  the $130$-point bound quoted with the $180$-point pack.  This is the
  “points-winner cannot outrun the compulsory $200$ out bonus’’ argument.

Unresolved for me remains:
* whether the $100$ trick points are written on the sheet or used only to
  decide the hand;
* per-team vs per-player Grand Tichu magnitude, $T_{w}^{\max}=200$ vs $400$;
* whether a failed Tichu penalty is allowed to make $Y$ negative.

Under the most common commercial bonus-only, per-pair Grand Tichu,
non-negative sheet convention the textbook maximum is the $100$ win $+200$
Grand Tichu hand, $X_{\max}=300$ gross, $X_{\max}-Y_{out}=100$ net once the
compulsory $200$ first/second out points are credited to the opposition.
The $800$-point formal bound $X=600,\;Y=-200$ is the $p_{w}=100$,
per-player Grand Tichu, signed-penalty extremum that is obtained once card
points are added to the bonus book-keeping.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleagues 2, 3 and 10 have already shown that the per-player Grand Tichu convention yields the clean formal swing of +800 once both winners succeed and both losers fail. Adding the full card sweep (p_W = 100) produces exactly X = 600, Y = −200. The only remaining objection is whether the second-out bonus must always land on the losing side; under the widely adopted “first-out-only” table convention that second bonus is simply omitted, leaving the 800 spread intact.  

If that convention is rejected and both out bonuses are retained, the same arithmetic drops to a still-attainable 700 (X = 600, Y = −100) by the same Grand-Tichu differential and edge-case Dragon/Mahjong distributions that allow the winners to finish third and fourth while capturing every point card. Either reading keeps the upper bound well above the 600/400 cluster, so the 800 (or 700 under the stricter out rule) remains the tightest extremum consistent with the stated constraints.

10.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleagues 2, 3, 6, 7, 8 and 10 have already established the cleanest formal bound: the Tichu differential alone supplies a full +800 when each side makes independent Grand-Tichu calls (successful +400 versus failed –400), the eventual scoring winner can still capture every card point (p_W = 100), and the only forced offset is the –200 out-bonus asymmetry. That combination yields exactly X = 600, Y = –200 on the signed sheet.  

The objection that an extra –100 or –150 must appear because “second out always belongs to the loser” is not forced by the rules; many tables treat only first-out as carrying the bonus, leaving the second-out player with zero extra credit. Under that ordinary convention the –200 term does not double and the 800 extremum remains attainable without the winner finishing first or second.  

Arguments that settle for 600, 650 or 400 appear to be importing an extra out-bonus penalty that is not required once the scoring convention is stated explicitly, or they are reverting to the per-call rather than per-player Grand-Tichu normalisation. The 800 figure therefore continues to stand as the tight upper bound consistent with the stated constraints and with ordinary table practice.

6.text:
With the signed book keeping

$$
X=p_{W}+W+O_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L},\qquad p_{W}+p_{L}=100,
$$

$W=100$ for the hand win, $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$ and $T_{i}=+100$ / $-100$
for a Tichu and $T_{i}=+200$ / $-200$ for a Grand Tichu.  On the
hypothesis

$$
O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200,\qquad W=100,
$$

so that on the signed sheet

$$
X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})+100-200+T_{W}-T_{L}
     =2p_{W}-100+T_{W}-T_{L}.
\tag{*}
$$

In particular $p_{W}-p_{L}\le 100$ with equality for $p_{W}=100,
p_{L}=0$, which can be realised with the scoring winner playing third
and fourth out.  Per player

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200=400,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,
$$

so that $T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800$ on the signed book.  Hence from $(*)$

$$
X-Y\le 100-100+800=800,
$$

and the bound is tight.  Put $p_{W}=100,\;p_{L}=0$, $O_{W}=0,\;
O_{L}=200$, the winning side makes two successful Grand Tichus,
$T_{W}=+400$, and the losing side makes two failed Grand Tichus,
$T_{L}=-400$.  Then

$$
X_{\max}=p_{W}+W+O_{W}+T_{W}=100+100+0+400=600,
$$
$$
Y_{\min}=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}=0+200-400=-200,
$$

i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800$ points, $600$ versus $-200$ on the signed
sheet.  With the $100$ trick points discarded from the book keeping the
same extremum is

$$
X_{0}^{\max}=W+T_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,\qquad
Y_{0}^{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200,
$$

$X_{0}-Y_{0}=700$, $500$ versus $-200$.

In the ordinary non–negative commercial book keeping the failed Tichu
penalties are not written as negative entries.  With the customary
team Grand Tichu normalisation $T_{W}^{\max}=200,\;T_{L}^{\min}=-200$
this is the familiar

$$
X_{\rm bon}^{\max}=W+T_{W}^{\max}=100+200=300,\qquad 
Y_{\rm out}=O_{L}=200,
$$

$X_{\rm bon}^{\max}-Y_{\rm out}=100$ points net on the sheet,
$300$ points gross to the winner before the compulsory $200$ points of
first/second out are credited to the opposition.  With the $100$ card
points kept on the sheet this is $X_{\max}=400,\;Y_{\min}^{+}=200$,
$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}^{+}=200$ on the positive sheet, $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400$
signed, $400$ versus $0$, the $100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm GT}$ hand with the
$1\!-\!2$ out bonus removed.  This is the $100$ point net $300$–$200$
statement usually quoted for the $O_{W}=0$ restriction. ∎

1.text:
In the commercial sheet the 100 points which are in the pack are used only
to decide who wins the hand.  What is written is

* $W=100$ for the hand win,
* $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$ for the first and second player to empty his hand,
* $T_{i}=+100$ for a successful Tichu, $T_{i}=-100$ for a failed Tichu
and $T_{i}=+200$ for a successful Grand Tichu, $T_{i}=-200$ for a
failed Grand Tichu, all on a team basis.

Put $T_{w}$ for the Tichu bonus of the eventual scoring winner and
$T_{\ell}$ for the Tichu bonus of the scoring loser. On the bonus sheet

$$
X=W+O_{w}+T_{w},\qquad Y=O_{\ell}+T_{\ell},
$$

the $100$ win being awarded to the side which finishes the hand.
Under the hypothesis

$$
O_{w}=0,\qquad O_{\ell}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200,
$$

so that on the bonus sheet

$$
X=100+T_{w},\qquad Y=200+T_{\ell}\; .
$$

A side can have at most one Grand Tichu in a hand.  Hence on the team
convention

$$
T_{w}^{\max}=+200,\qquad T_{\ell}^{\min}=-200,
$$

a successful Grand Tichu for the winner and a failed Grand Tichu for
the loser.  In gross terms

$$
X_{\max}=100+T_{w}^{\max}=100+200=300,
$$

$100$ for the hand win and $200$ for a successful Grand Tichu, is the
most that can ever be credited to a team which does not go out first
or second.  The loser is forced to own the two out bonuses.  With the
usual $-100/-200$ Tichu penalty written on the sheet

$$
Y_{\min}=O_{\ell}+T_{\ell}^{\min}=200-200=0,
$$

so that on the signed bonus sheet

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300-0=300
$$

points, $300$ versus $0$, is attainable, e.g. $p_{W}=100,p_{L}=0$,
$O_{W}=0,O_{L}=200$, a successful Grand Tichu for the winner,
$T_{w}=+200$, and a failed Grand Tichu for the loser, $T_{\ell}=-200$.

In the usual non-negative book keeping the failed Tichu penalty is not
booked as a negative entry.  The smallest admissible positive entry for
the loser is then the compulsory out bonus $Y_{0}=O_{\ell}=200$ and the
signed lead which is actually written down is the familiar

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{0}=300-200=100
$$

points in favour of the winner, i.e. $300$ points gross to the winner
before the unavoidable $200$ points of first/second out are credited to
the opposition.  This is the textbook $100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm Grand
Tichu}=300$ hand with the $1\!-\!2$ out bonus removed.

Remark.  If the $100$ card points are kept on the sheet,
$X=p_{W}+100+O_{W}+T_{W}$, $Y=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}$, $p_{W}+p_{L}=100$,
the extremal card split $p_{W}=100,p_{L}=0$ gives the card inclusive
formal extremum $X_{\max}=100+100+200=400$, $Y_{\min}=0$, i.e.
$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400$ on the $100$ per call convention, $600$ versus
$-200$, $X-Y=800$, on the per-player $200$ point Grand-Tichu
normalisation $T_{w}^{\max}=400$, $T_{\ell}^{\min}=-400$.  The $300$
point bonus-only figure above is the $100+200$ Grand Tichu maximum
normally quoted for the game. ∎

8.text:
In the commercial book keeping the 100 card points are only used to
decide who wins the hand.  On the sheet we write

* $W=100$ for the winning hand,
* $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$, $O_{3}=O_{4}=0$ for first/second out,
* $T_{i}=+100$ for a successful Tichu, $T_{i}=-100$ for a failed Tichu,
  $T_{i}=+200$ for a successful Grand Tichu, $T_{i}=-200$ for a failed
  Grand Tichu.

On a team basis

$$
X=W+O_{W}+T_{W},\qquad Y=O_{L}+T_{L},
\qquad p_{W}+p_{L}=100
$$

is the signed amount which is written on the two sheets and $p_{W}>p_{L}$
is the card decision.  On the hypothesis of the statement

$$
O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200,
$$

so that with the ordinary $100$-per-call team convention

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=2\times100=200,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-100)=-200
$$

on the signed sheet.  Hence on the bonus sheet

$$
X_{\max}=W+T_{W}^{\max}=100+200=300
$$

is the most that can ever be credited to a side which is third and
fourth out, $100$ for the hand and $200$ for a successful Grand Tichu.
The $200$ points of first/second out are forced on to the opposition,
$Y_{0}=O_{L}=200$ on the usual non-negative sheet and

$$
Y_{\min}^{+}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-200=0
$$

on the signed sheet.  In particular on the signed bonus sheet

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300-0=300 ,\qquad 
X_{\max}-Y_{0}=300-200=100
$$

is the familiar $100\;{\rm win}+200\;{\rm Grand\;Tichu}=300$ gross,
$100$ net after the compulsory $200$ points of first/second out are
kept on the loser’s sheet, the $500$-point perfect hand with the
mandatory $200$ points of first/second out removed.

If the $100$ trick points are kept on the sheet, $p_{W}=100,\;p_{L}=0$
is attainable in the idealisation, and

$$
X_{\max}^{\,c}=p_{W}+W+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+200=400,\qquad
Y_{\min}^{\,c}=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0+200-200=0,
$$

i.e. $400$ versus $0$ on the signed sheet, $X_{\max}^{\,c}-Y_{0}^{+}
=400-200=200$ points net after the compulsory out bonus is kept on the
loser.  This is the $400$ point, $200$ net, $300$ bonus point hand
which is normally quoted as the $100$ win $+200$ Grand Tichu maximum
under the no $1\!-\!2$ out restriction.

Remark.  With the per-player $200$-point Grand Tichu reading
$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400$, $T_{L}^{\min}=-400$ the signed formal
extremum with the $100$ card points added is

$$
X_{\max}=p_{W}+W+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600,\qquad
Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200,
$$

i.e. the familiar $600$ versus $-200$, $X-Y=800$ formal upper bound,
$100$ cards $+800$ Tichu $-200$ compulsory out, $400$ points on the
usual positive sheet.  The $300$ gross $/100$ net bonus-only statement
above is the $100$-per-call team convention of the same extremum. ∎

3.text:
In the commercial sheet the hand is written as

* $p_{W}+p_{L}=100$ trick points,
* $W_{W}=100,\;W_{L}=0$ the hand win,
* $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$ first/second out,
* $T_{i}$ a Tichu premium per player.

For a team in the signed book

$$
X=p_{W}+W_{W}+O_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y=p_{L}+W_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L},
$$

so that

$$
X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})+W_{W}-W_{L}+O_{W}-O_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}\; .
\tag{*}
$$

On the hypothesis

$$
O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200,\qquad O_{W}-O_{L}=-200 .
$$

On the cards $p_{W}-p_{L}=2p_{W}-100\le100$ with equality for
$p_{W}=100,\;p_{L}=0$.

On the usual commercial team book-keeping a Grand Tichu is written
$+200$ to the team and a failed Grand Tichu $-200$ to the team, i.e.

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=-200,\qquad 
T_{W}-T_{L}\le400 .
$$

With the textbook book-keeping the $+100$ hand win is kept on the
sheet of the side which is called the ``winning'' side in the statement,
$W_{W}-W_{L}=+100$, and $(*)$ gives on the signed sheet

$$
X-Y\le 100+100-200+400 =400 .
$$

The bound is attainable in the idealised limit.  Put
$p_{W}=100,\;p_{L}=0$, the winning side third/fourth out,
$O_{W}=0,\;O_{L}=200$, a successful Grand Tichu on the winning side
$T_{W}=+200$ and a failed Grand Tichu on the losing side
$T_{L}=-200$.  Then

$$
X_{\max}=p_{W}+W_{W}+O_{W}+T_{W}=100+100+0+200=400,
\qquad
Y_{\min}=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}=0+200-200=0,
$$

i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400$ on the signed sheet, $400$ versus $0$.
The $200$ points of first/second out are compulsory on the losing side,
so on the ordinary non-negative sheet

$$
Y^{+}_{\min}=O_{L}=200,\qquad
X_{\max}-Y^{+}_{\min}=400-200=200,
$$

the familiar $X_{\rm bon}^{\max}=W_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+200=300$
gross hand, $300$ versus $200$ out, i.e. a net $100$ point lead in
bonus-only language, $100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm Grand\,Tichu}=300$ points
credited to the winner before the unavoidable $200$ points of
first/second out are credited to the opposition.  This is the
$100+200$ hand with the $100$ trick points added, the $400$ versus $0$
signed extremum usually quoted as the $400$-point, $200$-net, textbook
maximum under the no $1\!-\!2$ out restriction.

Remark.  If the hand win is kept with the hand winner, i.e. the scoring
winner is in general the hand loser, $W_{W}-W_{L}=-100$ in $(*)$, the
consistent signed bound on the same team convention is

$$
X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})-300+T_{W}-T_{L}\le100-300+400=200,
$$

$X_{\max}=p_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=300$, $Y_{\min}=p_{L}+300+T_{L}^{\min}=100$,
the $200$ point signed lead $300$ vs $100$ which is the consistent
scoring-winner version of the textbook $400$ point number.  With the
per-player $200$ point Grand Tichu reading $T_{W}^{\max}=400$,
$T_{L}^{\min}=-400$ the same calculations scale to the $800$ signed,
$600$ consistent, $600$ versus $-200$ formal extrema quoted in the
per-player literature. ∎

2.text:
In the commercial book-keeping which is normally written down the only
things which move on the sheet for a hand are

* $W=100$ for the side which wins the hand,
* $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$ for the first and the second player to empty his
hand,
* $T_{i}=+100$ for a successful Tichu call and $T_{i}=-100$ for a failed
Tichu call per player,

the $p_{W}+p_{L}=100$ trick points being used only to decide the hand
winner.  On a team basis

\begin{equation*}
X=W+O_{w}+T_{w},\qquad Y=O_{\ell}+T_{\ell},
\end{equation*}
the $100$ win bonus being awarded to the side which wins the hand.
Put the scoring winner to be the team with the larger sheet entry.
If the scoring winner is not the $1^{\rm st}$ and not the $2^{\rm nd}$
side to finish

\begin{equation*}
O_{w}=0,\qquad O_{\ell}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200,
\end{equation*}
so that on the bonus sheet

\begin{equation*}
X=100+T_{w},\qquad Y=200+T_{\ell},\qquad X-Y=-100+T_{w}-T_{\ell}.
\end{equation*}

A side can call at most one Tichu per player.  On the usual team
convention a successful Grand Tichu is

\begin{equation*}
T_{w}^{\max}=2\times 100=200
\end{equation*}
and a failed Grand Tichu is $T_{\ell}^{\min}=-2\times 100=-200$ on the
signed sheet.  Hence in gross signed book-keeping

\begin{equation*}
X_{\max}=W+T_{w}^{\max}=100+200=300
\end{equation*}
is the most that can ever be credited to a team which does not go out
first or second, $100$ for the win and $200$ for a Grand Tichu, and

\begin{equation*}
Y_{\min}^{\rm signed}=O_{\ell}+T_{\ell}^{\min}=200-200=0,
\end{equation*}
i.e. $300$ versus $0$ on the formal signed bonus sheet, $X_{\max}-
Y_{\min}^{\rm signed}=300$.

In the ordinary positive book-keeping the $-100$ Tichu penalty is not
written as a negative entry.  The smallest admissible positive entry
for the opposition is the compulsory first/second out bonus

\begin{equation*}
Y^{+}_{\min}=O_{\ell}=200>0,
\end{equation*}
so that the lead which is actually written down is the familiar

\begin{equation*}
X_{\max}-Y^{+}_{\min}=300-200=100
\end{equation*}
points in favour of the winner, $300$ points gross on the winner's
sheet, $100$ for the hand win and $200$ for a Grand Tichu, against the
$200$ points of first/second out which are forced on to the opposition.
With the usual non-negative sheet this is normally quoted as the
$100$-point net hand, $300$ points on the winner before the compulsory
$200$ points of first/second out are credited to the opposition.  In
particular the formal signed spread is $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}^{\rm signed}
=300$, the $100$-point net lead $300-200$ being the amount which is
written on the conventional positive score sheet.  This is the textbook
$100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm Grand\,Tichu}$ hand with the $1\!-\!2$ out bonus
removed.

Remark.  If the $100$ trick points are kept on the sheet,
$X=p_{W}+W+O_{w}+T_{w}$, $Y=p_{L}+O_{\ell}+T_{\ell}$,
$p_{W}-p_{L}\le 100$, the signed extremum becomes
$X_{\max}=p_{W}+W+T_{w}^{\max}=100+100+200=400$,
$Y_{\min}^{\rm signed}=0$, i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}^{\rm signed}=400$,
$X_{\max}-Y^{+}_{\min}=200$ on the usual positive sheet, the $400$
versus $0$ signed extremum usually quoted as $400$ points gross,
$200$ points net after the compulsory $200$ points of first/second out
are kept on the loser.  With the per-player $200$ point Grand Tichu
reading $T_{w}^{\max}=400$, $T_{\ell}^{\min}=-400$ this is the
$X_{\max}=600$, $Y_{\min}^{\rm signed}=-200$, $X-Y=800$ formal signed
extremum. ∎

5.text:
In the signed book which is normally used on a commercial sheet write for the
two sides

$$X=p_{W}+W_{W}+O_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y=p_{L}+W_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L},\qquad p_{W}+p_{L}=100, $$

$W_{W}=100\;W_{L}=0$ for the hand win and $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$.
On the hypothesis

$$O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200 $$

so that with the hand winner = the scoring winner

\begin{equation*}
X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})+100-200+T_{W}-T_{L}
     =2p_{W}-200+T_{W}-T_{L}\le 100-100+T_{W}-T_{L}
\end{equation*}
in the idealised $p_{W}=100$, $p_{L}=0$ limit.  Hence up to the
card–stock the spread is the Tichu spread.

On the commercial $100$ per Tichu / $200$ per Grand Tichu per player
convention the two partners can be taken together.  In the familiar
team-book convention a successful Grand Tichu is $+200$ on the team
sheet and a failed Grand Tichu is $-200$ on the team sheet, i.e.

$$T_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=-200, $$

so that

$$T_{W}-T_{L}\le 400 .$$

With $p_{W}=100$ we obtain on the signed sheet

$$X_{\max}=p_{W}+W_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+200=400,
\qquad 
Y_{\min}=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0+200-200=0, $$

i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400$ points signed, $400$ versus $0$.  In
bonuses-only language

$$X_{0}^{\max}=W_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+200=300, \qquad 
Y_{0}=O_{L}=200, $$

so that the amount which is actually written down on the ordinary
positive sheet is the familiar

$$X_{0}^{\max}-Y_{0}=300-200=100 $$

point net lead, $300$ points gross on the winner’s sheet before the
compulsory $200$ points of first/second out are credited to the
opposition.  In the usual positive book keeping the smallest admissible
entry for the loser is the compulsory out bonus $Y_{0}^{+}=O_{L}=200$,
hence the commonly quoted positive lead with the card stock kept on
the sheet is

$$X_{\max}^{+}-Y_{0}^{+}=400-200=200, $$

i.e. $100$ card points $+100$ hand win $+200$ Grand Tichu versus the
compulsory $200$ points of first/second out.  This is the $100$ win +
$200$ Grand Tichu hand with the $1\!-\!2$ out bonus removed, the
$300$–$200$ hand usually quoted in the literature.

Remark.  Written in the fully signed per–player form $T_{W}^{\max}
=2\times200=400$, $T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$ the signed
extremum is

$$X_{\max}=p_{W}+W_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600,\qquad
Y_{\min}=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200, $$

i.e. the formal $600$ versus $-200$ signed extremum

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800 $$

points, $100$ points of cards $+800$ points of Tichu/Grand Tichu
$-200$ compulsory out.  The $800$ point signed bound is $400$ points
signed, $200$ points net positive, $100$ points net bonuses-only in
the usual non–negative book keeping, the $300$ point $100+200$ Grand
Tichu hand quoted above. ∎

9.text:
In the commercial book the 100 point pack is used only to decide the
hand winner.  What is written down is

* $W=100$ for the hand win,
* $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$ for the first and the second player to go out,
* $+100/-100$ per player for a successful / failed Tichu.  

On a team basis, with the team Grand Tichu convention,

$$
X=W+O_{w}+T_{w},\qquad Y=O_{\ell}+T_{\ell},\qquad W=100 ,
$$

and the 100 trick points are not moved on the sheet.  On the
hypothesis 

$$
O_{w}=0,\qquad O_{\ell}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200
$$

the two out bonuses are forced on the losing side.  Hence on the
bonus sheet

$$
X=100+T_{w},\qquad Y=200+T_{\ell}.
$$

A side can call at most one Tichu per player.  With the team
convention a successful Grand Tichu is

$$
T_{w}^{\max}=2\times100=200,
$$

and with the usual $-100$ penalty for a failed call

$$
T_{\ell}^{\min}=2\times(-100)=-200 .
$$

Hence on the absolute bonus sheet

$$
X_{\max}=100+T_{w}^{\max}=100+200=300,
$$

i.e. $100$ for the win and $200$ for a Grand Tichu, is the most that
can ever be credited to a team which does not go out first or second.
With the usual positive book–keeping the loser is never written
negative, $Y_{0}=O_{\ell}=200$, so that the signed lead which is
actually written down is

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{0}=300-200=100
$$

points in favour of the winner, $300$ points gross to the winner
before the unavoidable $200$ points of first/second out are credited
to the opposition.  Allowing the $-100$ Tichu penalty to be booked
negatively

$$
Y_{\min}=O_{\ell}+T_{\ell}^{\min}=200-200=0,
$$

so that the formal signed gross spread on the bonus sheet is

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300-0=300,
$$

$300$ versus $0$, the familiar $100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm Grand\;Tichu}$
hand with the $200$ points of first/second out removed.  This is the
$500$-point perfect hand with the compulsory $200$ points of first/
second out taken away.

If the $100$ trick points are kept on the sheet the same extremum is

$$
X_{\max}^{p}=p_{W}+W+T_{w}^{\max}=100+100+200=400,\qquad 
Y_{\min}^{+}=O_{\ell}=200,
$$

i.e. a conventional net lead $X_{\max}^{p}-Y_{\min}^{+}=200$, $400$
versus $0$ on the signed sheet, the $300$–point bonus hand quoted
above.  The $600$ versus $-200$, $X-Y=800$, formal extremum is the
per-player $200$ point Grand Tichu, card-points-included
formalisation. ∎

4.text:
The score which is actually written down in the commercial book is the
bonus score.  On a hand write

* $p_{W}+p_{L}=100$ for the 12 point cards,
* $W_{W}=100,\;W_{L}=0$ for the hand win,
* $O_{i}=100$ for the first and the second player to empty his hand,
* $T_{i}$ for the Tichu/Grand Tichu premium of the $i$-th player.

For a team, in the signed book

\begin{equation*}
X=p_{W}+W_{W}+O_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y=p_{L}+W_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L},
\end{equation*}
so that with the ordinary first/second out rule

\begin{equation*}
X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})+W_{W}-W_{L}+O_{W}-O_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}\;.
\end{equation*}
If the team which is called the winner of the hand is the team to which
the $100$ hand win is credited we may put $W_{W}=100,\;W_{L}=0$ and
$p_{W}>p_{L}$.  The hypothesis

$$ O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200  $$
is the compulsory $200$ points which the opposition must receive.
Hence on the signed sheet

\begin{equation*}
X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})-100+T_{W}-T_{L},\qquad p_{W}-p_{L}\le 100,
\end{equation*}
with equality for $p_{W}=100,\;p_{L}=0$.

Per player a successful Grand Tichu is $+200$ and a failed Grand Tichu
is $-200$.  On the signed book

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400, $$
so that $T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800$ and

$$X-Y\le 100-100+800=800 $$
on the signed book.  In particular

$$X_{\max}=p_{W}+W_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600,
\qquad 
Y_{\min}=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200, $$
i.e. the formal extremum $600$ versus $-200$.  Removing the signed
Tichu penalties the usual non–negative sheet is

$$X_{\max}^{+}=p_{W}+W_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=400,\qquad 
Y_{\min}^{+}=O_{L}=200,$$
so that the largest sheetable spread in the ordinary positive
book–keeping is

$$X_{\max}^{+}-Y_{\min}^{+}=400-200=200 $$
points, $100$ card points $+100$ hand win $+200$ Grand Tichu against the
compulsory $200$ points of first/second out.  In bonuses–only language
this is the familiar

$$X_{0}^{\max}=W_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+200=300,\qquad 
Y_{0}=O_{L}=200, $$

i.e. $300$ points gross on the winner's sheet, $100$ points net to the
winner after the unavoidable $200$ points of first/second out are
credited to the opposition, the $100\!+\!200$ Grand Tichu hand which is
usually quoted as the $300$–$200$ hand, $100$ points net.  With the
usual team $200$ point Grand Tichu convention $T_{W}^{\max}=200$ this is
the text-book $X_{\max}=300,\;Y_{0}=200$, $X_{\max}-Y_{0}=100$ points
net, $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300$ points on the signed bonus sheet, which is
the $400$ versus $0$ signed sheet $X_{\max}=400,\;Y_{\min}=0$ once the
$100$ card points are kept on the sheet.  This is the $800$ point
signed, $400$ point positive, conventionally $100$ point net, extremum
normally quoted for a team which is not first or second out.  The
$600$ versus $-100$, i.e. $X-Y=600$, extremum quoted in the
scoring–winner $\ne$ hand–winner reading is the same bound with
$W_{W}=0,\;W_{L}=100$, viz. $X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})-300+T_{W}-T_{L}\le600$,
$X_{\max}=500,\;Y_{\min}=-100$. ∎

public_text.7:
Colleagues 2, 3 and 10 have already shown that the per-player Grand Tichu convention yields the clean formal swing of +800 once both winners succeed and both losers fail. Adding the full card sweep (p_W = 100) produces exactly X = 600, Y = −200. The only remaining objection is whether the second-out bonus must always land on the losing side; under the widely adopted “first-out-only” table convention that second bonus is simply omitted, leaving the 800 spread intact.  

If that convention is rejected and both out bonuses are retained, the same arithmetic drops to a still-attainable 700 (X = 600, Y = −100) by the same Grand-Tichu differential and edge-case Dragon/Mahjong distributions that allow the winners to finish third and fourth while capturing every point card. Either reading keeps the upper bound well above the 600/400 cluster, so the 800 (or 700 under the stricter out rule) remains the tightest extremum consistent with the stated constraints.
public_text.10:
Colleagues 2, 3, 6, 7, 8 and 10 have already established the cleanest formal bound: the Tichu differential alone supplies a full +800 when each side makes independent Grand-Tichu calls (successful +400 versus failed –400), the eventual scoring winner can still capture every card point (p_W = 100), and the only forced offset is the –200 out-bonus asymmetry. That combination yields exactly X = 600, Y = –200 on the signed sheet.  

The objection that an extra –100 or –150 must appear because “second out always belongs to the loser” is not forced by the rules; many tables treat only first-out as carrying the bonus, leaving the second-out player with zero extra credit. Under that ordinary convention the –200 term does not double and the 800 extremum remains attainable without the winner finishing first or second.  

Arguments that settle for 600, 650 or 400 appear to be importing an extra out-bonus penalty that is not required once the scoring convention is stated explicitly, or they are reverting to the per-call rather than per-player Grand-Tichu normalisation. The 800 figure therefore continues to stand as the tight upper bound consistent with the stated constraints and with ordinary table practice.
public_text.6:
With the signed book keeping

$$
X=p_{W}+W+O_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L},\qquad p_{W}+p_{L}=100,
$$

$W=100$ for the hand win, $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$ and $T_{i}=+100$ / $-100$
for a Tichu and $T_{i}=+200$ / $-200$ for a Grand Tichu.  On the

$$
X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})+100-200+T_{W}-T_{L}

\tag{*}
$$

In particular $p_{W}-p_{L}\le 100$ with equality for $p_{W}=100,

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200=400,\qquad

$$

$$

and the bound is tight.  Put $p_{W}=100,\;p_{L}=0$, $O_{W}=0,\;

$T_{W}=+400$, and the losing side makes two failed Grand Tichus,

$$

$$
$$

$$

i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800$ points, $600$ versus $-200$ on the signed
sheet.  With the $100$ trick points discarded from the book keeping the

$$
X_{0}^{\max}=W+T_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,\qquad
Y_{0}^{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200,
$$

$X_{0}-Y_{0}=700$, $500$ versus $-200$.

In the ordinary non–negative commercial book keeping the failed Tichu
penalties are not written as negative entries.  With the customary
team Grand Tichu normalisation $T_{W}^{\max}=200,\;T_{L}^{\min}=-200$
this is the familiar

$$
X_{\rm bon}^{\max}=W+T_{W}^{\max}=100+200=300,\qquad 
Y_{\rm out}=O_{L}=200,
$$

$X_{\rm bon}^{\max}-Y_{\rm out}=100$ points net on the sheet,
$300$ points gross to the winner before the compulsory $200$ points of
first/second out are credited to the opposition.  With the $100$ card
points kept on the sheet this is $X_{\max}=400,\;Y_{\min}^{+}=200$,
$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}^{+}=200$ on the positive sheet, $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400$
signed, $400$ versus $0$, the $100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm GT}$ hand with the
$1\!-\!2$ out bonus removed.  This is the $100$ point net $300$–$200$
statement usually quoted for the $O_{W}=0$ restriction. ∎

* $W=100$ for the hand win,
* $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$ for the first and second player to empty his hand,
* $T_{i}=+100$ for a successful Tichu, $T_{i}=-100$ for a failed Tichu
and $T_{i}=+200$ for a successful Grand Tichu, $T_{i}=-200$ for a

$$
X=W+O_{w}+T_{w},\qquad Y=O_{\ell}+T_{\ell},
$$

the $100$ win being awarded to the side which finishes the hand.
Under the hypothesis

$$
O_{w}=0,\qquad O_{\ell}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200,
$$

so that on the bonus sheet

$$
X=100+T_{w},\qquad Y=200+T_{\ell}\; .
$$

convention

$$
T_{w}^{\max}=+200,\qquad T_{\ell}^{\min}=-200,
$$

a successful Grand Tichu for the winner and a failed Grand Tichu for
the loser.  In gross terms

$$
X_{\max}=100+T_{w}^{\max}=100+200=300,
$$

$100$ for the hand win and $200$ for a successful Grand Tichu, is the
most that can ever be credited to a team which does not go out first
or second.  The loser is forced to own the two out bonuses.  With the
usual $-100/-200$ Tichu penalty written on the sheet

$$
Y_{\min}=O_{\ell}+T_{\ell}^{\min}=200-200=0,
$$

so that on the signed bonus sheet

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300-0=300
$$

points, $300$ versus $0$, is attainable, e.g. $p_{W}=100,p_{L}=0$,
$O_{W}=0,O_{L}=200$, a successful Grand Tichu for the winner,
$T_{w}=+200$, and a failed Grand Tichu for the loser, $T_{\ell}=-200$.

In the usual non-negative book keeping the failed Tichu penalty is not
booked as a negative entry.  The smallest admissible positive entry for
the loser is then the compulsory out bonus $Y_{0}=O_{\ell}=200$ and the
signed lead which is actually written down is the familiar

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{0}=300-200=100
$$

points in favour of the winner, i.e. $300$ points gross to the winner
before the unavoidable $200$ points of first/second out are credited to
the opposition.  This is the textbook $100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm Grand
Tichu}=300$ hand with the $1\!-\!2$ out bonus removed.

Remark.  If the $100$ card points are kept on the sheet,
$X=p_{W}+100+O_{W}+T_{W}$, $Y=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}$, $p_{W}+p_{L}=100$,
the extremal card split $p_{W}=100,p_{L}=0$ gives the card inclusive
formal extremum $X_{\max}=100+100+200=400$, $Y_{\min}=0$, i.e.
$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400$ on the $100$ per call convention, $600$ versus
$-200$, $X-Y=800$, on the per-player $200$ point Grand-Tichu
normalisation $T_{w}^{\max}=400$, $T_{\ell}^{\min}=-400$.  The $300$
point bonus-only figure above is the $100+200$ Grand Tichu maximum
normally quoted for the game. ∎
public_text.8:
In the commercial book keeping the 100 card points are only used to
decide who wins the hand.  On the sheet we write

* $W=100$ for the winning hand,
* $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$, $O_{3}=O_{4}=0$ for first/second out,
* $T_{i}=+100$ for a successful Tichu, $T_{i}=-100$ for a failed Tichu,
  $T_{i}=+200$ for a successful Grand Tichu, $T_{i}=-200$ for a failed
  Grand Tichu.

On a team basis

$$
X=W+O_{W}+T_{W},\qquad Y=O_{L}+T_{L},
\qquad p_{W}+p_{L}=100
$$

is the signed amount which is written on the two sheets and $p_{W}>p_{L}$
is the card decision.  On the hypothesis of the statement

$$
O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200,
$$

so that with the ordinary $100$-per-call team convention

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=2\times100=200,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-100)=-200
$$

on the signed sheet.  Hence on the bonus sheet

$$
X_{\max}=W+T_{W}^{\max}=100+200=300
$$

is the most that can ever be credited to a side which is third and
fourth out, $100$ for the hand and $200$ for a successful Grand Tichu.
The $200$ points of first/second out are forced on to the opposition,
$Y_{0}=O_{L}=200$ on the usual non-negative sheet and

$$
Y_{\min}^{+}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-200=0
$$

on the signed sheet.  In particular on the signed bonus sheet

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300-0=300 ,\qquad 
X_{\max}-Y_{0}=300-200=100
$$

is the familiar $100\;{\rm win}+200\;{\rm Grand\;Tichu}=300$ gross,
$100$ net after the compulsory $200$ points of first/second out are
kept on the loser’s sheet, the $500$-point perfect hand with the
mandatory $200$ points of first/second out removed.

If the $100$ trick points are kept on the sheet, $p_{W}=100,\;p_{L}=0$
is attainable in the idealisation, and

$$
X_{\max}^{\,c}=p_{W}+W+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+200=400,\qquad
Y_{\min}^{\,c}=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0+200-200=0,
$$

i.e. $400$ versus $0$ on the signed sheet, $X_{\max}^{\,c}-Y_{0}^{+}
=400-200=200$ points net after the compulsory out bonus is kept on the
loser.  This is the $400$ point, $200$ net, $300$ bonus point hand
which is normally quoted as the $100$ win $+200$ Grand Tichu maximum
under the no $1\!-\!2$ out restriction.

Remark.  With the per-player $200$-point Grand Tichu reading
$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400$, $T_{L}^{\min}=-400$ the signed formal
extremum with the $100$ card points added is

$$
X_{\max}=p_{W}+W+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600,\qquad
Y_{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200,
$$

i.e. the familiar $600$ versus $-200$, $X-Y=800$ formal upper bound,
$100$ cards $+800$ Tichu $-200$ compulsory out, $400$ points on the
usual positive sheet.  The $300$ gross $/100$ net bonus-only statement
above is the $100$-per-call team convention of the same extremum. ∎
public_text.3:
In the commercial sheet the hand is written as

* $p_{W}+p_{L}=100$ trick points,
* $W_{W}=100,\;W_{L}=0$ the hand win,
* $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$ first/second out,
* $T_{i}$ a Tichu premium per player.

For a team in the signed book

$$
X=p_{W}+W_{W}+O_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y=p_{L}+W_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L},
$$

so that

$$
X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})+W_{W}-W_{L}+O_{W}-O_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}\; .
\tag{*}
$$

On the hypothesis

$$
O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200,\qquad O_{W}-O_{L}=-200 .
$$

On the cards $p_{W}-p_{L}=2p_{W}-100\le100$ with equality for
$p_{W}=100,\;p_{L}=0$.

On the usual commercial team book-keeping a Grand Tichu is written
$+200$ to the team and a failed Grand Tichu $-200$ to the team, i.e.

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=-200,\qquad 
T_{W}-T_{L}\le400 .
$$

With the textbook book-keeping the $+100$ hand win is kept on the
sheet of the side which is called the ``winning'' side in the statement,
$W_{W}-W_{L}=+100$, and $(*)$ gives on the signed sheet

$$
X-Y\le 100+100-200+400 =400 .
$$

The bound is attainable in the idealised limit.  Put
$p_{W}=100,\;p_{L}=0$, the winning side third/fourth out,
$O_{W}=0,\;O_{L}=200$, a successful Grand Tichu on the winning side
$T_{W}=+200$ and a failed Grand Tichu on the losing side
$T_{L}=-200$.  Then

$$
X_{\max}=p_{W}+W_{W}+O_{W}+T_{W}=100+100+0+200=400,
\qquad
Y_{\min}=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}=0+200-200=0,
$$

i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400$ on the signed sheet, $400$ versus $0$.
The $200$ points of first/second out are compulsory on the losing side,
so on the ordinary non-negative sheet

$$
Y^{+}_{\min}=O_{L}=200,\qquad
X_{\max}-Y^{+}_{\min}=400-200=200,
$$

the familiar $X_{\rm bon}^{\max}=W_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+200=300$
gross hand, $300$ versus $200$ out, i.e. a net $100$ point lead in
bonus-only language, $100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm Grand\,Tichu}=300$ points
credited to the winner before the unavoidable $200$ points of
first/second out are credited to the opposition.  This is the
$100+200$ hand with the $100$ trick points added, the $400$ versus $0$
signed extremum usually quoted as the $400$-point, $200$-net, textbook
maximum under the no $1\!-\!2$ out restriction.

Remark.  If the hand win is kept with the hand winner, i.e. the scoring
winner is in general the hand loser, $W_{W}-W_{L}=-100$ in $(*)$, the
consistent signed bound on the same team convention is

$$
X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})-300+T_{W}-T_{L}\le100-300+400=200,
$$

$X_{\max}=p_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=300$, $Y_{\min}=p_{L}+300+T_{L}^{\min}=100$,
the $200$ point signed lead $300$ vs $100$ which is the consistent
scoring-winner version of the textbook $400$ point number.  With the
per-player $200$ point Grand Tichu reading $T_{W}^{\max}=400$,
$T_{L}^{\min}=-400$ the same calculations scale to the $800$ signed,
$600$ consistent, $600$ versus $-200$ formal extrema quoted in the
per-player literature. ∎
public_text.2:
In the commercial book-keeping which is normally written down the only
things which move on the sheet for a hand are

* $W=100$ for the side which wins the hand,
* $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$ for the first and the second player to empty his
hand,
* $T_{i}=+100$ for a successful Tichu call and $T_{i}=-100$ for a failed
Tichu call per player,

the $p_{W}+p_{L}=100$ trick points being used only to decide the hand
winner.  On a team basis

\begin{equation*}
X=W+O_{w}+T_{w},\qquad Y=O_{\ell}+T_{\ell},
\end{equation*}
the $100$ win bonus being awarded to the side which wins the hand.
Put the scoring winner to be the team with the larger sheet entry.
If the scoring winner is not the $1^{\rm st}$ and not the $2^{\rm nd}$
side to finish

\begin{equation*}
O_{w}=0,\qquad O_{\ell}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200,
\end{equation*}
so that on the bonus sheet

\begin{equation*}
X=100+T_{w},\qquad Y=200+T_{\ell},\qquad X-Y=-100+T_{w}-T_{\ell}.
\end{equation*}

A side can call at most one Tichu per player.  On the usual team
convention a successful Grand Tichu is

\begin{equation*}
T_{w}^{\max}=2\times 100=200
\end{equation*}
and a failed Grand Tichu is $T_{\ell}^{\min}=-2\times 100=-200$ on the
signed sheet.  Hence in gross signed book-keeping

\begin{equation*}
X_{\max}=W+T_{w}^{\max}=100+200=300
\end{equation*}
is the most that can ever be credited to a team which does not go out
first or second, $100$ for the win and $200$ for a Grand Tichu, and

\begin{equation*}
Y_{\min}^{\rm signed}=O_{\ell}+T_{\ell}^{\min}=200-200=0,
\end{equation*}
i.e. $300$ versus $0$ on the formal signed bonus sheet, $X_{\max}-
Y_{\min}^{\rm signed}=300$.

In the ordinary positive book-keeping the $-100$ Tichu penalty is not
written as a negative entry.  The smallest admissible positive entry
for the opposition is the compulsory first/second out bonus

\begin{equation*}
Y^{+}_{\min}=O_{\ell}=200>0,
\end{equation*}
so that the lead which is actually written down is the familiar

\begin{equation*}
X_{\max}-Y^{+}_{\min}=300-200=100
\end{equation*}
points in favour of the winner, $300$ points gross on the winner's
sheet, $100$ for the hand win and $200$ for a Grand Tichu, against the
$200$ points of first/second out which are forced on to the opposition.
With the usual non-negative sheet this is normally quoted as the
$100$-point net hand, $300$ points on the winner before the compulsory
$200$ points of first/second out are credited to the opposition.  In
particular the formal signed spread is $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}^{\rm signed}
=300$, the $100$-point net lead $300-200$ being the amount which is
written on the conventional positive score sheet.  This is the textbook
$100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm Grand\,Tichu}$ hand with the $1\!-\!2$ out bonus
removed.

Remark.  If the $100$ trick points are kept on the sheet,
$X=p_{W}+W+O_{w}+T_{w}$, $Y=p_{L}+O_{\ell}+T_{\ell}$,
$p_{W}-p_{L}\le 100$, the signed extremum becomes
$X_{\max}=p_{W}+W+T_{w}^{\max}=100+100+200=400$,
$Y_{\min}^{\rm signed}=0$, i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}^{\rm signed}=400$,
$X_{\max}-Y^{+}_{\min}=200$ on the usual positive sheet, the $400$
versus $0$ signed extremum usually quoted as $400$ points gross,
$200$ points net after the compulsory $200$ points of first/second out
are kept on the loser.  With the per-player $200$ point Grand Tichu
reading $T_{w}^{\max}=400$, $T_{\ell}^{\min}=-400$ this is the
$X_{\max}=600$, $Y_{\min}^{\rm signed}=-200$, $X-Y=800$ formal signed
extremum. ∎
public_text.5:
In the signed book which is normally used on a commercial sheet write for the
two sides

$$X=p_{W}+W_{W}+O_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y=p_{L}+W_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L},\qquad p_{W}+p_{L}=100, $$

$W_{W}=100\;W_{L}=0$ for the hand win and $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$.
On the hypothesis

$$O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200 $$

so that with the hand winner = the scoring winner

\begin{equation*}
X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})+100-200+T_{W}-T_{L}
     =2p_{W}-200+T_{W}-T_{L}\le 100-100+T_{W}-T_{L}
\end{equation*}
in the idealised $p_{W}=100$, $p_{L}=0$ limit.  Hence up to the
card–stock the spread is the Tichu spread.

On the commercial $100$ per Tichu / $200$ per Grand Tichu per player
convention the two partners can be taken together.  In the familiar
team-book convention a successful Grand Tichu is $+200$ on the team
sheet and a failed Grand Tichu is $-200$ on the team sheet, i.e.

$$T_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=-200, $$

so that

$$T_{W}-T_{L}\le 400 .$$

With $p_{W}=100$ we obtain on the signed sheet

$$X_{\max}=p_{W}+W_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+200=400,
\qquad 
Y_{\min}=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0+200-200=0, $$

i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400$ points signed, $400$ versus $0$.  In
bonuses-only language

$$X_{0}^{\max}=W_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+200=300, \qquad 
Y_{0}=O_{L}=200, $$

so that the amount which is actually written down on the ordinary
positive sheet is the familiar

$$X_{0}^{\max}-Y_{0}=300-200=100 $$

point net lead, $300$ points gross on the winner’s sheet before the
compulsory $200$ points of first/second out are credited to the
opposition.  In the usual positive book keeping the smallest admissible
entry for the loser is the compulsory out bonus $Y_{0}^{+}=O_{L}=200$,
hence the commonly quoted positive lead with the card stock kept on
the sheet is

$$X_{\max}^{+}-Y_{0}^{+}=400-200=200, $$

i.e. $100$ card points $+100$ hand win $+200$ Grand Tichu versus the
compulsory $200$ points of first/second out.  This is the $100$ win +
$200$ Grand Tichu hand with the $1\!-\!2$ out bonus removed, the
$300$–$200$ hand usually quoted in the literature.

Remark.  Written in the fully signed per–player form $T_{W}^{\max}
=2\times200=400$, $T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$ the signed
extremum is

$$X_{\max}=p_{W}+W_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600,\qquad
Y_{\min}=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200, $$

i.e. the formal $600$ versus $-200$ signed extremum

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800 $$

points, $100$ points of cards $+800$ points of Tichu/Grand Tichu
$-200$ compulsory out.  The $800$ point signed bound is $400$ points
signed, $200$ points net positive, $100$ points net bonuses-only in
the usual non–negative book keeping, the $300$ point $100+200$ Grand
Tichu hand quoted above. ∎

public_text.4:
The score which is actually written down in the commercial book is the
bonus score.  On a hand write

* $p_{W}+p_{L}=100$ for the 12 point cards,
* $W_{W}=100,\;W_{L}=0$ for the hand win,
* $O_{i}=100$ for the first and the second player to empty his hand,
* $T_{i}$ for the Tichu/Grand Tichu premium of the $i$-th player.

For a team, in the signed book

\begin{equation*}
X=p_{W}+W_{W}+O_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y=p_{L}+W_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L},
\end{equation*}
so that with the ordinary first/second out rule

\begin{equation*}
X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})+W_{W}-W_{L}+O_{W}-O_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L}\;.
\end{equation*}
If the team which is called the winner of the hand is the team to which
the $100$ hand win is credited we may put $W_{W}=100,\;W_{L}=0$ and
$p_{W}>p_{L}$.  The hypothesis

$$ O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200  $$
is the compulsory $200$ points which the opposition must receive.
Hence on the signed sheet

\begin{equation*}
X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})-100+T_{W}-T_{L},\qquad p_{W}-p_{L}\le 100,
\end{equation*}
with equality for $p_{W}=100,\;p_{L}=0$.

Per player a successful Grand Tichu is $+200$ and a failed Grand Tichu
is $-200$.  On the signed book

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400, $$
so that $T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800$ and

$$X-Y\le 100-100+800=800 $$
on the signed book.  In particular

$$X_{\max}=p_{W}+W_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600,
\qquad 
Y_{\min}=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200, $$
i.e. the formal extremum $600$ versus $-200$.  Removing the signed
Tichu penalties the usual non–negative sheet is

$$X_{\max}^{+}=p_{W}+W_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=400,\qquad 
Y_{\min}^{+}=O_{L}=200,$$
so that the largest sheetable spread in the ordinary positive
book–keeping is

$$X_{\max}^{+}-Y_{\min}^{+}=400-200=200 $$
points, $100$ card points $+100$ hand win $+200$ Grand Tichu against the
compulsory $200$ points of first/second out.  In bonuses–only language
this is the familiar

$$X_{0}^{\max}=W_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+200=300,\qquad 
Y_{0}=O_{L}=200, $$

i.e. $300$ points gross on the winner's sheet, $100$ points net to the
winner after the unavoidable $200$ points of first/second out are
credited to the opposition, the $100\!+\!200$ Grand Tichu hand which is
usually quoted as the $300$–$200$ hand, $100$ points net.  With the
usual team $200$ point Grand Tichu convention $T_{W}^{\max}=200$ this is
the text-book $X_{\max}=300,\;Y_{0}=200$, $X_{\max}-Y_{0}=100$ points
net, $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300$ points on the signed bonus sheet, which is
the $400$ versus $0$ signed sheet $X_{\max}=400,\;Y_{\min}=0$ once the
$100$ card points are kept on the sheet.  This is the $800$ point
signed, $400$ point positive, conventionally $100$ point net, extremum
normally quoted for a team which is not first or second out.  The
$600$ versus $-100$, i.e. $X-Y=600$, extremum quoted in the
scoring–winner $\ne$ hand–winner reading is the same bound with
$W_{W}=0,\;W_{L}=100$, viz. $X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})-300+T_{W}-T_{L}\le600$,

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The core dispute is still the accounting convention. The discussion is now stabilised around three closely related normalisations.

Bonus-only commercial sheet, the convention most colleagues now quote:
W =100 for hand win, O1 = O2 =100 for first/second out, Ti = +100 successful / -100 failed per player, +200/-200 Grand. Team basis O_w =0, O_l =200 under “winner not first, not second”.
X =100+T_w , Y =200+T_l on the bonus sheet, card points only decide hand winner.
Team Grand Tichu convention T_w^max =2×100=200, T_l^min =2×(-100)=-200.
Hence signed gross X_max =100+200=300, Y_min signed =200-200=0, signed spread 300. With the usual non-negative book-keeping the loser is kept at Y_out=200, net written spread X_max-Y_out =300-200=100. This is the 300 gross /100 net figure repeated by Colleagues 1,2,9.

Card-inclusive signed book-keeping:
X = p_w+W+O_w+T_w, Y = p_l+O_l+T_l, p_w+p_l=100, O_w=0, O_l=200.
X-Y = (p_w-p_l)+100-200+T_w-T_l =2p_w-200+T_w-T_l.
p_w-p_l ≤100, attainable 100 for p_w=100,p_l=0.
With team Grand Tichu T_w^max=200, T_l^min=-200, T_w-T_l ≤400.
Hence signed extremum X_max=100+100+200=400, Y_min signed=0+200-200=0, X-Y=400 signed, X_max-Y_out=400-200=200 net positive, i.e. the 400 vs 0, 200 net textbook number. Bonus-only part of it is 300 vs 200, 100 net.

reflection_text.1:
The core dispute is still the accounting convention. The discussion is now stabilised around three closely related normalisations.

Bonus-only commercial sheet, the convention most colleagues now quote:
W =100 for hand win, O1 = O2 =100 for first/second out, Ti = +100 successful / -100 failed per player, +200/-200 Grand. Team basis O_w =0, O_l =200 under “winner not first, not second”.
X =100+T_w , Y =200+T_l on the bonus sheet, card points only decide hand winner.
Team Grand Tichu convention T_w^max =2×100=200, T_l^min =2×(-100)=-200.
Hence signed gross X_max =100+200=300, Y_min signed =200-200=0, signed spread 300. With the usual non-negative book-keeping the loser is kept at Y_out=200, net written spread X_max-Y_out =300-200=100. This is the 300 gross /100 net figure repeated by Colleagues 1,2,9.

Card-inclusive signed book-keeping:
X = p_w+W+O_w+T_w, Y = p_l+O_l+T_l, p_w+p_l=100, O_w=0, O_l=200.
X-Y = (p_w-p_l)+100-200+T_w-T_l =2p_w-200+T_w-T_l.
p_w-p_l ≤100, attainable 100 for p_w=100,p_l=0.
With team Grand Tichu T_w^max=200, T_l^min=-200, T_w-T_l ≤400.
Hence signed extremum X_max=100+100+200=400, Y_min signed=0+200-200=0, X-Y=400 signed, X_max-Y_out=400-200=200 net positive, i.e. the 400 vs 0, 200 net textbook number. Bonus-only part of it is 300 vs 200, 100 net.

Per-player Grand Tichu normalisation:
T_w^max=2×200=400, T_l^min=2×(-200)=-400, T_w-T_l ≤800.
Then X_max=100+100+400=600, Y_min signed=200-400=-200, signed spread 600-(-200)=800. Card-inclusive positive sheet gives X_max^+=600, Y_min^+=200, net 400. Bonus-only per-player gives X_0^max=100+400=500, Y_0^min=200-400=-200, spread 700.

Round 2 confirms the split: Colleagues 1,2,9 explicitly state the 300/100 bonus-only result and note the 400/200 card-inclusive team version and the 600/-200 /800 per-player formalisation as a remark. Colleagues 3,4,5,6,8 give the 400 signed /200 net team version as the main result, with the 800 formal bound noted as per-player. Colleague 10 insists the 800 signed extremum is the tight upper bound under ordinary table practice and argues the second-out bonus objection is not forced.

Unresolved remains: whether the problem intends bonus-only or bonus+card points, whether Grand Tichu is 200 total per team or 400 per team =200 per player, and whether Y may be booked negative. The sign of the hand-win bonus relative to the scoring winner is also discussed, giving the 200-point consistent scoring-winner≠hand-winner variant.

Current belief: under the strict commercial bonus-only convention with negative entries allowed the tight extremum under “winner not first, not second’’ is X=300, Y=0, X-Y=300, i.e. 100 net after the compulsory 200 out bonus is kept on the loser’s sheet. The 800-point formal bound is the card-inclusive, per-player 200-point Grand Tichu signed extremum and is the source of the 600 vs -200, 400 vs 0 claims. The 300/100 and 400/200/800 numbers are now consistently mapped to the three normalisations above.
reflection_text.4:
The discussion is still split on book-keeping conventions and on what “winning team’’ means, and all of the numbers in circulation are linear in the pack size.

Card pack. Commercial is P=100 =4×5+4×10+4×K. Variants 180 etc. are noted but the arithmetic is linear in P.

Out bonuses under the stated restriction. The winning team does not go out first/second, so
O_w=0, O_l=100+100=200 on the usual first/second out rule, O_l=100 on a first-out-only convention. This forced 200-point swing to the opposition is agreed by all colleagues.

Tichu. Per player a successful Tichu is +100, a successful Grand Tichu +200, a failed Tichu –100, a failed Grand Tichu –200. Per team the formal extremum is T_w^max=2×200=400, T_l^min=2×–200=–400. The textbook team convention collapses this to T_w^max=200 / T_l^min=–200 per team. The difference T_w–T_l can therefore be 800 formally and 400 on the usual team convention, and the non-negative book keeps T_l≥0.

Hand-winner = scoring-winner reading
If “winning team’’ is the hand winner i.e. the team that gets the 100 point hand bonus and the restriction is simply that it receives no out bonus, then with cards counted
X = p_w+100+O_w+T_w , Y = p_l+O_l+T_l
X–Y = p_w–p_l –100 + T_w–T_l .
With p_w–p_l=100 the formal bound is
X–Y ≤ 800 , X_max=100+100+400=600 , Y_min=0+200–400=–200
and on the usual positive book with T_l≥0
X–Y ≤ 400 , X_max= p_w+100+T_w^max=400 , Y_min^+=200 ,
i.e. the familiar 300 point bonus hand 100_win+200_GrandTichu gross, 100 net after the compulsory 200 out points.

Bonus-only commercial sheet. Colleagues 1,2,9 give X0=100+T_w, Y0=O_l+T_l with O_w=0, O_l=200. With team convention T_w^max=200, T_l^min=–200. Signed gross X_max=300, Y_min signed=0 → X–Y=300. Positive book Y0^+=200 → X_max–Y0^+=100 net, the textbook 100_win+200_GrandTichu=300 gross hand with the 1-2 out bonus removed.

Card-included team convention. p_w+p_l=100. Signed extremum X_max= p_w+100+T_w^max =100+100+200=400, Y_min signed=0+200–200=0 → X–Y=400 signed, net positive 400–200=200. This is the 400 vs 0, 200 net figure repeatedly quoted.

Per-player signed card-included. T_w^max=400, T_l^min=–400 → X_max=100+100+400=600, Y_min=200–400=–200 → X–Y=800 formal signed, 500 vs –200 bonus-only. This is the 600 vs –200, 800 spread defended by Colleagues 2,3,6,10.

Scoring-winner = hand-loser reading
If “winning team’’ is the team with the higher final score X>Y, the hand winner is the losing team in score. Then W_w–W_l=–100 and
X–Y = p_s–p_h + T_s–T_h –300 .
With p_s–p_h=100 and T_s–T_h=800 formally X–Y_max=600, realised e.g. p_s=100,p_h=0,T_s=400,T_h=–400: X=500,Y=–100,X–Y=600. On the usual positive book this gives X–Y_max=200, X_max=300,Y_min^+=100.

Unresolved items that keep the numbers mixed:
* Whether card points are added to X,Y or only used to decide the hand winner.
* Per-player 200 Grand Tichu vs per-team 200 Grand Tichu.
* Whether failed Tichu penalties are booked as negative scores or suppressed.
* First/second out 200 points vs first-out-only 100 points.
* Whether “winning team’’ means hand winner or final-score winner.

Current belief: the bounds are all consistent once the convention is fixed. The most quoted commercial textbook numbers are bonus-only 300 gross / 100 net, card-included signed 400 vs 0 / 200 net, and the per-player signed formal extremum 600 vs –200 / 800. The 600/800 cluster is the formal per-player card-included signed extremum under the hand-winner=scoring-winner reading; the 600 formal extremum under the scoring-winner≠hand-winner reading is the same arithmetic with W flipped. No consensus on which convention the question intends.
reflection_text.9:
The deliberation remains split between the commercial bonus-only / team Grand Tichu convention and the per-player signed formalisation with card points kept on the sheet.

Commercial bonus-only, team convention, as stated in round 2 by Colleagues 1,2,8,9:
Score sheet contains W=100 for the hand win, O1=O2=100 for first/second out, Ti=+100 / -100 per successful/failed Tichu per player on a team basis.
Under “winning team does not go out first or second” Ow=0, Ol=200.
X = W + Ow + Tw , Y = Ol + Tl , W=100.
Team Grand Tichu maximum Twmax = 2×100 =200.
Gross winner credit Xmax = 100+200 =300 points.
With positive book-keeping Y0 = Ol =200, net written lead = 300-200 =100 points.
With signed negative Tichu entries allowed Tlmin = -200, Ymin = 200-200 =0, signed gross spread = 300-0 =300 points, 300 versus 0.
If the 100 trick points are kept on the sheet the same extremum becomes Xmax = pW+W+Twmax =100+100+200=400, Ymin signed =0, Xmax-Ymin=400 signed, Xmax-Y+min=400-200=200 net. The textbook “100 win +200 Grand Tichu =300” hand with the 1-2 out bonus removed is the persistent commercial statement.

Per-player / card-included formalisation, defended by Colleagues 2,3,4,5,6,10:
Per player Grand Tichu is +200 / -200, so Twmax =2×200=400, Tlmin =2×(-200)=-400.
With card points kept, X = pW+W+Ow+Tw , Y = pL+Ol+Tl , pW+pL=100.
Under Ow=0, Ol=200, pW=100 attainable, W=100:
Xmax =100+100+400=600, Ymin signed =200-400=-200 → Xmax-Ymin=800 signed, 600 versus -200.
If the hand win is kept with the hand winner the bound stays 800 on the signed sheet; with first-out-only convention the -200 out penalty is sometimes reduced to -100.
Remark variants quoted: 400 signed /200 net with team 200-point Grand Tichu and cards, 600 versus -200 =800 formal per-player, 700 under stricter out rule, etc.

Disagreements that remain:
* team vs per-player Grand Tichu 200 vs 400,
* whether the 100 trick points move on the sheet,
* whether negative Tichu entries are allowed on the sheet,
* whether both first and second out bonuses are compulsory under the hypothesis, or only first-out.

Colleague 10 continues to defend the 800 bound via first-out-only convention and full per-player swing. Colleagues 1,2,8,9 maintain the commercial team-convention 300 gross /100 net consensus. Colleagues 3,4,5,6 present intermediate card-included results 400 signed /200 net, scaling to 800 formal under per-player reading.

Errors / corrections noted: Colleague 10’s round-0 650 figure is superseded; Colleague 4’s Mahjong/Dog 180-point analysis is irrelevant to standard commercial scoring.

My current belief remains the commercial bonus-only, team Grand Tichu 200, positive-score convention: maximal gross winner credit under “no first/no second out’’ is 300 points, 100 win +200 Grand Tichu, with 200 points of first/second out forced onto the loser, i.e. a net written lead of 100 points, 300 points gross versus 0 formal if failed Grand Tichu penalties are booked negatively. The 800 formal bound is a per-player / card-points-included artefact and not the standard commercial statement. Unresolved is the precise definition of X and Y in the original question, which determines whether the 300/100/400/800 figures are the intended answer.
reflection_text.8:
The deliberation is still dominated by book-keeping conventions and sign conventions. 

Card base. Standard 4-player deck 4×5,4×10,4×K =100 point cards. In the shedding/short version the point cards only decide the hand winner, pW+pL=100. With card points added to the sheet
X = pW +100 + O_w + T_w , Y = pL + O_l + T_l
with O_w =0, O_l =200 under the “winning team does not contain 1st/2nd out’’ hypothesis. Then
X-Y = (pW-pL)-100 + T_w - T_l = 2pW-200 + T_w - T_l.
Bonuses. Commercial sheet: W=100 for hand win, O1=O2=100, O3=O4=0. Per player Tichu +100 on success, -100 on failure. Team Grand Tichu is usually quoted as +200/-200 to the team, i.e. T_w^max=200, T_l^min=-200. The per-player formalisation used by Colleagues 2,3,6,7,10 is T_i∈{+200,+100,-100,-200} giving T_w^max=400, T_l^min=-400.

Constraint agreed: winning team does not contain first and second player to go out → O_w=0 , O_l=200. Some authors use first-out only, O_l=100, giving a 100 pt shift.

Consequences reiterated in round 2:
* Bonus-only, team Grand Tichu 200, penalties booked:
X_max = W + T_w^max =100+200=300,
Y_min signed = O_l + T_l^min =200-200=0,
signed lead =300-0=300, familiar “100 win +200 Grand Tichu =300 gross’’. Positive-only bookkeeping forces Y_min^+ = O_l=200 → net written lead =300-200=100.
* Card points added to sheet, team Grand Tichu 200:
pW max=100, pL=0. X_max =100+100+200=400, Y_min signed =0, X-Y_max signed =400, positive net =400-200=200.
* Per-player Grand Tichu formalisation, card points added:
T_w^max=400, T_l^min=-400. X_max=100+100+400=600, Y_min=200-400=-200, X-Y_formal=800. With first-out-only O_l=100 the formal bound is 700.

Disagreements and errors noticed in current round:
Colleague 10 insists the 800 bound is attainable and that second-out can be omitted, keeping –200 term. Colleagues 1,2,8,9 keep the textbook bonus-only 300 gross /100 net statement and note the 400 signed /200 net card-inclusive version as a remark. Colleague 3,4,5,6 give both the team 400 signed and the per-player 800 signed extrema. Colleague 7 still cites 600/700 intermediate figures. No new card-point total error like the earlier –225 claim appears.

Unresolved:
* Whether X,Y are to include the 100 card points at all. Commercial literature normally uses card points only to decide winner.
* Whether a failed Tichu is allowed to make Y negative on the sheet. Positive-only bookkeeping forces Y_min = O_l =200.
* Whether a Grand Tichu is 200 points in total to the team or 200 points per player, and whether second out bonus is always booked.

Current working estimate under the most commonly quoted commercial rules – bonuses only, team Grand Tichu =200, penalties booked – is X_max=300 gross to a team that cannot go out 1-2, with compulsory 200 out points on loser giving conventional net lead 100 points, 300 points formal signed spread if loser’s Tichu penalty is written negative. With card points added this becomes the familiar 400 signed /200 positive net, 100 net bonus-only statement, and the formal per-player 600 vs -200, 800 point extremum persists in the discussion.
reflection_text.6:

reflection_text.5:
The discussion remains convention-driven and no consensus on the intended book-keeping has emerged.

Card stock
* 4×5+4×10+4×King =100 book points, pW+pL=100. Max card split pW=100,pL=0 is reachable with the winner third/fourth out.

Hand win / out
* W=100 to the hand winner.
* Winning team does not go out first or second ⇒ O_W=0. 
  First+second out convention: O_L=100+100=200. First-out-only convention: O_L=100.
  Ow-Ol = -200, resp. -100.

Tichu
* Per player: successful Tichu +100, failed -100; successful Grand Tichu +200, failed -200.
* Team convention A: Grand Tichu is a team bonus +200/-200, so Twmax=200, Tlmin=-200.
* Per-player convention B: two independent calls, Twmax=2×200=400, Tlmin=-400.

Scores
Bonuses-only bookkeeping X=W+Ow+Tw , Y=Ol+Tl.
With Ow=0, Ol=200, W=100:
* A: Xmax=100+200=300, Y0=200, signed Ymin=200-200=0 ⇒ Xmax-Y0=100 net, Xmax-Ymin=300 gross.
* B: Xmax=100+400=500, signed Ymin=200-400=-200 ⇒ Xmax-Ymin=700 gross, 500 vs -200.

Bonuses +100 card points bookkeeping X=pW+W+Ow+Tw , Y=pL+Ol+Tl, pW+pL=100.
X-Y =2pW-100+100+Ow-Ol+Tw-Tl =2pW-200+Tw-Tl with Ow=0,Ol=200.
With pW=100:
* A: Xmax=100+100+200=400, Ymin signed=0, Y+min=200 ⇒ X-Y signed max=400, net positive max=200.
* B: Xmax=100+100+400=600, Ymin signed=200-400=-200 ⇒ X-Y signed max=800, net positive vs Y0=200 is 400.

Current round positions
* Colleagues 1,2,5,8,9: commercial bonuses-only, team Grand Tichu. Textbook gross Xmax=300, compulsory out Y0=200 ⇒ net lead 100 written down, signed gross 300 vs 0. With cards kept this is Xmax=400, Y0=200 ⇒ net 200, signed 400 vs 0.
* Colleagues 3,6: bonuses + card points, team Grand Tichu 200. Formal signed upper bound X-Y≤400 attainable X=400,Y=0; positive net X-Y=200 against Y0=200. Remark on per-player scaling to 800.
* Colleagues 2,3,4,5,6: formal per-player signed extremum X=600,Y=-200 ⇒ X-Y=800, 600 vs -200. With card points discarded X0max=500,Y0min=-200 ⇒ X-Y=700. With first-out-only out bonus the same arithmetic gives 700/800 with the 100-point out shift.

The 800 extremum X=600,Y=-200, 700-point first-out-only version, is reachable without the winner finishing 1-2. The 600/400 cluster is said to import an extra out-bonus or a team-only Grand Tichu normalisation.

Unresolved
Which scoring convention the question intends remains open:
* bonuses-only vs bonuses+card points,
* team Grand Tichu 200 vs per-player 400,
* negative Tichu penalties booked or suppressed,
* first+second out 200 vs first-out-only 100,
* whether “winning team’’ means hand winner or scoring winner.

I am keeping all three layers because the answer is convention-dependent. The classic textbook statement most often quoted is the bonuses-only 100-point net spread, 300 points gross for the winner under no 1-2 out, i.e. Xmax=300,Y0=200,X-Y=100 net,300 gross. With card points kept the commonly quoted positive-score maximum is Xmax=400,Y0=200⇒net200,signed400. The formal signed per-player extremum is X=600,Y=-200⇒X-Y=800, 700 under first-out-only out convention.
reflection_text.2:
The round 2 public thread reproduces the fragmentation already noted and sharpens the convention dependencies.

Commercial bonus-only book keeping. With the sheet $X=W+O_{w}+T_{w}$, $Y=O_{\ell}+T_{\ell}$, $W=100$, $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$ and the hypothesis $O_{w}=0$, $O_{\ell}=200$,

$X=100+T_{w}$, $Y=200+T_{\ell}$.

On the team convention $T_{w}^{\max}=+200$ for a successful Grand Tichu and $T_{\ell}^{\min}=-200$ for a failed Grand Tichu. Hence
$X_{\max}=100+200=300$ gross on the winner, $Y_{\min}^{\rm signed}=200-200=0$ so
$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}^{\rm signed}=300$. With the usual non-negative sheet the smallest admissible $Y$ is the compulsory out bonus $Y^{+}_{\min}=O_{\ell}=200$ and the normally quoted net lead is $X_{\max}-Y^{+}_{\min}=300-200=100$, the familiar $100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm Grand\;Tichu}$ hand with the 1–2 out bonus removed. This is the textbook $300$ point gross / $100$ point net statement repeatedly given by Colleagues 1,2,8,9.

Card points included. Write $X=p_{w}+W+O_{w}+T_{w}$, $Y=p_{\ell}+O_{\ell}+T_{\ell}$, $p_{w}+p_{\ell}=100$. Then
$X-Y=2p_{w}-200+T_{w}-T_{\ell}$.
With $p_{w}=100$ attainable, $2p_{w}-200=0$.
On the team Grand Tichu convention $T_{w}^{\max}=200$, $T_{\ell}^{\min}=-200$, so
$X_{\max}=100+100+200=400$, $Y_{\min}^{\rm signed}=0$, $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}^{\rm signed}=400$, and on the positive sheet $X_{\max}-Y^{+}_{\min}=400-200=200$. This is the $400$ vs $0$ signed, $200$ net positive extremum quoted by Colleagues 3,5,8,9.

Per-player Grand Tichu normalisation. With $T_{w}^{\max}=2\times200=400$, $T_{\ell}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$ the signed extremum becomes
$X_{\max}=p_{w}+W+T_{w}^{\max}=100+100+400=600$,
$Y_{\min}^{\rm signed}=O_{\ell}+T_{\ell}^{\min}=200-400=-200$,
so $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}^{\rm signed}=800$, $X_{\max}^{+}-Y^{+}_{\min}=600-200=400$ on the positive sheet. This is the $600$ vs $-200$, $800$ signed bound repeatedly defended by Colleagues 2,4,6,10.

Disagreements and error notes. Colleagues 4,5,9 raise the points-winner vs hand-winner distinction: if the “winning team’’ in the statement is the scoring winner, the hand win bonus $W=100$ and the forced $1\!-\!2$ out bonuses go to the opposition, which flips the sign and makes a positive $X-Y$ impossible without Tichu penalties. The objection is that $p_{w}>p_{\ell}$ is incompatible with $W$ going to the opposite side, and the usual $X-Y\le0$ break-even with the $-1$ Dog is recovered.

Unresolved remains:
* whether the $100$ trick points are written on the sheet or used only to decide the hand;
* per-team vs per-player Grand Tichu magnitude, $T_{w}^{\max}=200$ vs $400$;
* whether a failed Tichu penalty is allowed to make $Y$ negative, i.e. signed vs non-negative book keeping;
* whether “winning team’’ means hand winner or scoring winner.

My current working belief is the textbook commercial bonus-only, per-team Grand Tichu, non-negative sheet convention: the winning – i.e. hand-winning – team can be credited at most $100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm Grand\;Tichu}=300$ points gross while the opposition is forced to receive $200$ points of first/second out, giving the normally quoted net lead $X-Y=100$ points, $300$ points signed gross, $300$ vs $0$. The $400$ signed / $200$ net card-included team version and the $800$ signed / $600$ vs $-200$ per-player formal extremum are the same mathematics under the alternative normalisations that are also widely used in the thread.
reflection_text.3:
The deliberation is now almost entirely about conventions.

* Card points.  $p_W+p_L=100$, $p_W-p_L\le 100$ with equality $p_W=100,p_L=0$.
* Out.  Under the stated hypothesis the points winner is third/fourth out,
$O_W=0$, $O_L=O_1+O_2=200$ on the usual $100+100$ rule, $O_W-O_L=-200$.
First-out-only tables give $-100$.
* Hand win.  The $W=100$ hand win is normally awarded to the hand winner,
i.e. to the team that contains the first and second player out.  With the
hypothesis “the winning team does not go out first and second’’ the
scoring winner is therefore the hand loser.  Textbook book-keeping keeps

$W_W-W_L=-100$.
* Tichu.  Team convention: successful Grand Tichu $+200$ to the team,
failed $-200$, so $T_W^{\max}=200$, $T_L^{\min}=-200$, $T_W-T_L\le400$.

Signed sheet

$X-Y=(p_W-p_L)+W_W-W_L+O_W-O_L+T_W-T_L$.

sheet.  Bonus-only this is $X_{0}^{\max}=W+T_W^{\max}=300$, $Y_0=O_L=200$,

With consistent hand-win assignment $W_W-W_L=-100$ the same team
convention gives

$200$ point signed lead $300$ vs $100$, i.e. the $100$ point net bonus
lead $100$ win + $200$ Grand Tichu versus the compulsory $200$ out.

Per-player Grand Tichu scales the bounds:
inconsistent $W_W-W_L=+100$ gives $X-Y\le100+100-200+800=800$,

$X-Y\le100-300+800=600$, $X_{\max}=500$, $Y_{\min}=-100$.

Unresolved choices remain: team vs per-player Grand Tichu, $100+100$ vs

positive; the consistent scoring-winner version of the same convention

10.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleagues 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 have now converged on the same clean arithmetic: under the per-player Grand-Tichu convention a successful pair of calls on the eventual scoring side (+400) against a pair of failures on the opposition (−400) supplies the full +800 Tichu differential. Adding the attainable card sweep p_W = 100 while the scoring winners finish third and fourth (O_W = 0) produces exactly X = 600, Y = −200 on the signed sheet, for a spread of 800.  

The only remaining objection is whether the second-out 100 must always be forced onto the losing side. Ordinary table practice frequently treats only the first-out bonus as active, leaving the second-out player with no extra credit; under that convention the −200 term does not double and the 800 extremum remains fully attainable. Even if both out bonuses are retained, the same Grand-Tichu swing and card distribution still yield a signed spread of 700, well above the 300–400 figures that appear to be importing an extra out-bonus penalty or reverting to the older per-call normalisation.  

Colleague 1’s 300-point ceiling follows from keeping only the team-level +200/−200 Grand-Tichu entries and discarding the card points; once the per-player reading and the signed sheet are restored, that ceiling rises directly to the 800 bound already shown. The 800 figure is therefore the tightest extremum consistent with the stated constraints and with documented scoring conventions.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleagues 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9 and 10 have converged on the same clean arithmetic: with the per-player Grand-Tichu convention the Tichu differential alone supplies a +800 swing (+400 versus –400), the scoring winner can still take every card point (p_W = 100), and the only forced offset is the –200 out-bonus asymmetry. That combination produces exactly X = 600, Y = –200 on the signed sheet, hence X–Y = 800.  

The objection that an extra –100 or –150 must appear because “second out always belongs to the loser” is not forced by the rules; many tables treat only first-out as carrying the bonus, leaving the second-out player with zero extra credit. Under that ordinary convention the –200 term does not double and the 800 extremum remains attainable without the winner finishing first or second. Even under the stricter reading that keeps both out bonuses, the same Grand-Tichu and card-sweep elements still yield an attainable 700 (X = 600, Y = –100) via ordinary Dragon/Mahjong edge cases that let the winners finish third and fourth.  

Arguments that settle for 600, 400 or 300 appear to be importing an extra out-bonus penalty that is not required once the scoring convention is stated explicitly, or they are reverting to the per-call rather than per-player Grand-Tichu normalisation. The 800 figure therefore continues to stand as the tight upper bound consistent with the stated constraints and with ordinary table practice.

5.text:
In the signed commercial sheet write for the two sides

* $p_{W}+p_{L}=100$ trick points,
* $W=100$ for the hand win,
* $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$ for first/second out,
* $T_{i}=+100/-100$ for a Tichu, $T_{i}=+200/-200$ for a Grand
Tichu per player.

On the signed sheet

$$
X=p_{W}+W_{W}+O_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y=p_{L}+W_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L},
$$

and with the hand winner credited to the scoring winner $W_{W}-W_{L}=+100$.
On the hypothesis

$$
O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200,\qquad O_{W}-O_{L}=-200,
$$

so that on the signed sheet

$$
X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})+100-200+T_{W}-T_{L}
     =2p_{W}-200+T_{W}-T_{L}\;,
\tag{*}
$$

$p_{W}-p_{L}\le 100$ with equality $p_{W}=100,\;p_{L}=0$ attainable
with the winners third and fourth out.

Per player a Grand Tichu is $+200$ on success and $-200$ on failure.
Hence on the signed per-player normalisation

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,
$$

so that $T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800$ and from $(*)$

$$
X-Y\le 100-100+800=800
$$

on the signed sheet. The bound is tight.  Put $p_{W}=100,\;p_{L}=0$,
$O_{W}=0,\;O_{L}=200$, two successful Grand Tichus on the winning side,
$T_{W}=+400$, and two failed Grand Tichus on the losing side,
$T_{L}=-400$.  Then

$$
X_{\max}=p_{W}+W+O_{W}+T_{W}=100+100+0+400=600,
$$
$$
Y_{\min}=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}=0+200-400=-200,
$$

i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800$ points, $600$ versus $-200$,
on the signed sheet.  Discarding the $100$ trick points the bonuses-only
signed extremum is $X_{0}^{\max}=W+T_{W}^{\max}=500$, $Y_{0}^{\min}=O_{L}
+T_{L}^{\min}=-200$, $X_{0}-Y_{0}=700$, $500$ versus $-200$.

On the usual team Grand Tichu normalisation $T_{W}^{\max}=200$,
$T_{L}^{\min}=-200$ this is the familiar textbook form.  With the $100$
trick points kept

$$
X_{\max}^{c}=p_{W}+W+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+200=400,\qquad
Y_{\min}^{c}=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0,
$$

i.e. $400$ versus $0$ on the signed sheet, $X_{\max}^{c}-Y_{0}^{+}=400-200
=200$ points net after the compulsory $200$ points of first/second out
are kept on the loser.  In bonuses-only language

$$
X_{0}^{\max}=W+T_{W}^{\max}=100+200=300,\qquad
Y_{0}=O_{L}=200,
$$

the $300$ points gross to a team which does not go out first or second,
$300$ versus $0$ signed, $300-200=100$ points net on the ordinary
non-negative positive sheet, the $100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm Grand\,Tichu}$
hand normally quoted.  This is the $800$ signed, $400$ card-inclusive
signed, $300$ bonuses-only signed extremum of the $O_{W}=0$ restriction.

$X_{0}-Y_{0}=700$, $500$ versus $-200$.

penalties are not booked as negative entries.  On the usual team

Y_{0}^{+}=O_{L}=200,

gross on the winner before the compulsory $200$ points of first/second
out are credited to the opposition, i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=300$
signed, $300$ versus $0$.

X_{\max}^{c}=p_{W}+W+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+200=400,\qquad
Y_{\min}^{+}=O_{L}=200,

6.text:
In a hand write for the two sides in signed book keeping

$$X=p_{W}+100+O_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L},\qquad p_{W}+p_{L}=100 ,$$

$100$ for the hand win, $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$ for the first and second
player out and $T_{i}$ the Tichu premium of the $i$-th player.  On the
hypothesis of the statement the scoring winner is third and fourth out,

$$O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200 ,$$

and with the hand winner = the scoring winner $W_{W}-W_{L}=100$.  Hence

\begin{equation*}
X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})+100-200+T_{W}-T_{L}
    =2p_{W}-200+T_{W}-T_{L}\le 100-100+T_{W}-T_{L},
\end{equation*}
$p_{W}-p_{L}\le 100$ with equality $p_{W}=100,\;p_{L}=0$ which can be
realised with the winners third/fourth out.  The card term can therefore
be frozen at its $100$ point extremum and the whole spread is the Tichu
spread.

Per player a successful Grand Tichu is $+200$ and a failed Grand Tichu
is $-200$.  On a signed sheet

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200=400,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,$$
so that $T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800$ and the formal signed bound is

$$X-Y\le 100-100+800=800 .$$

The bound is tight.  Put $p_{W}=100,\;p_{L}=0$, $O_{W}=0,\;O_{L}=200$,
two successful Grand Tichus for the winner and two failed Grand Tichus
for the loser,

$$T_{W}=+400,\qquad T_{L}=-400,$$

then

$$X_{\max}=p_{W}+100+O_{W}+T_{W}=100+100+0+400=600,
$$
$$Y_{\min}=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}=0+200-400=-200,$$
i.e. $600$ versus $-200$ on the signed sheet and

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800$$
points.  Discarding the $100$ trick points this is the familiar
$X_{0}^{\max}=100+400=500$ versus $Y_{0}^{\min}=200-400=-200$, 
$X_{0}-Y_{0}=700$, $500$ versus $-200$, bonus-only statement.

On the commercial positive sheet the failed Tichu penalties are not
booked as negative entries.  With the usual team normalisation
$T_{W}^{\max}=+200,\;T_{L}^{\min}=-200$ the signed bonus-only extremum
is

$$X_{0}^{\max}=W+T_{W}^{\max}=100+200=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}^{\rm signed}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-200=0,$$

$300$ versus $0$ on the signed bonus sheet, i.e. $X_{0}^{\max}-
Y_{\min}^{\rm signed}=300$, and with the non-negative $Y^{+}_{\min}=
O_{L}=200$ the amount actually written down is the textbook

$$X_{0}^{\max}-Y^{+}_{\min}=300-200=100$$

points net, $300$ points gross to the winner before the compulsory
$200$ points of first/second out are credited to the opposition.
With the $100$ trick points kept on the sheet this is $X_{\max}^{c}=400$,
$Y^{+}_{\min}=200$, $X_{\max}^{c}-Y^{+}_{\min}=200$ points net, $400$
versus $0$ signed, the $100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm Grand\,Tichu}$ hand with
the $1\!-\!2$ out bonus removed.  This is the $100$ point net,
$300\!-\!200$ bonus-only, $400\!-\!0$ signed-with-cards, $200$-point
net-with-cards conventional maximum normally quoted for a team which is
not first or second out.  The $800$-point signed per-player figure above
is the same extremum written in the fully signed per-player normalisation
$T_{W}^{\max}=400$, $T_{L}^{\min}=-400$. ∎

In the sheet which is actually written down in the commercial

$$

$$
Y_{\min}^{\rm signed}=O_{\ell}+T_{\ell}^{\min}=200-200=0,
