$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}^{\rm signed}=300-0=300,
$$

$300$ versus $0$, is attainable e.g. $p_{W}=100,p_{L}=0$,
$O_{W}=0,O_{L}=200$, $T_{w}=+200$ and $T_{\ell}=-200$.

In the ordinary non-negative book-keeping the failed Tichu penalty is
not booked as a negative entry.  The smallest admissible positive
entry for the opposition is the compulsory out bonus
$Y^{+}_{\min}=O_{\ell}=200$ and the lead which is actually written
down is the familiar

$$
X_{\max}-Y^{+}_{\min}=300-200=100
$$

points in favour of the winner, $300$ points gross on the winner’s
sheet, $100$ for the hand win and $200$ for a Grand Tichu, against the
$200$ points of first/second out which are forced on to the opposition.
This is the textbook $100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm Grand\;Tichu}=300$ hand
with the $1\!-\!2$ out bonus removed.

$X=p_{W}+W+O_{w}+T_{w}$, $Y=p_{L}+O_{\ell}+T_{\ell}$,

sheet, the $100$ cards $+100$ win $+200$ Grand Tichu maximum normally
quoted as $400$ points gross, $200$ points net after the compulsory
$200$ points of first/second out.  With the per-player $200$ point
Grand Tichu reading $T_{w}^{\max}=400$, $T_{\ell}^{\min}=-400$ this
scales to the formal per-player signed extremum
$X_{\max}=600$, $Y_{\min}=-200$, $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800$, the $600$
versus $-200$ formal bound quoted in the per-player, card-inclusive
literature. ∎

3.text:
The two sheets which are written down on a commercial table are

$$X=p_{W}+W_{W}+O_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y=p_{L}+W_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L},\qquad p_{W}+p_{L}=100 ,
$$

$W_{W}+W_{L}=100$ the $100$ hand win, $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$ first and second
out and $T_{i}=\pm 100$ for a Tichu and $T_{i}=\pm 200$ for a Grand
Tichu per player.  Put

$$X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})+W_{W}-W_{L}+O_{W}-O_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L} .$$

On the hypothesis of the statement the scoring winner is third and
fourth out,

$$O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200,\qquad O_{W}-O_{L}=-200, $$

and $p_{W}-p_{L}=2p_{W}-100\le 100$ with equality for the idealised
$p_{W}=100,\;p_{L}=0$, which can be realised with the winner playing
third and fourth out.

On the usual team book–keeping a Grand Tichu is written $+200$ to the
team and a failed Grand Tichu $-200$ to the team.  Hence on the signed
sheet

$$T_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=-200,\qquad 
T_{W}-T_{L}\le 400, $$

and with the textbook book–keeping in which the $100$ hand win is kept
on the sheet of the side which is called the winning side,
$W_{W}-W_{L}=+100$, we obtain on the signed sheet

$$X-Y\le (p_{W}-p_{L})+100-200+T_{W}-T_{L}
      \le 100+100-200+400=400 .$$

The bound is attainable in the idealisation.  Put $p_{W}=100,\;p_{L}=0$,
$O_{W}=0,\;O_{L}=200$, a successful team Grand Tichu for the winner
$T_{W}=+200$ and a failed team Grand Tichu for the loser
$T_{L}=-200$.  Then

$$X_{\max}=p_{W}+W_{W}+O_{W}+T_{W}=100+100+0+200=400,\qquad
Y_{\min}=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}=0+200-200=0, $$

i.e. $400$ versus $0$ on the signed sheet.  In bonuses–only language

$$X_{0}^{\max}=W_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+200=300,\qquad 
Y_{0}=O_{L}=200, $$

so that the amount which is actually written down on the ordinary
non–negative sheet is the familiar $300$ points gross to the winner,
$100$ for the hand win and $200$ for a Grand Tichu, against the
compulsory $200$ points of first/second out on the opposition, i.e.
$X_{\max}^{+}-Y_{0}^{+}=400-200=200$ points card inclusive, $100$
points net in bonuses–only language.  This is the $100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm
Grand\,Tichu}=300$ hand with the $1\!-\!2$ out bonus removed, normally
quoted as the $400$ versus $0$ signed, $200$ net, $100$ net bonus
extremum for a team which is not first or second out.

Remark.  With the scoring-winner $\ne$ hand-winner accounting
$W_{W}-W_{L}=-100$ the same team convention gives the consistent
signed bound

$$X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})-300+T_{W}-T_{L}\le100-300+400=200, $$

$X_{\max}=p_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=300$, $Y_{\min}=p_{L}+300+T_{L}^{\min}=100$,
the $300$ versus $100$ signed lead, i.e. the $100$ net bonus lead
$100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm Grand\,Tichu}=300$ gross against the compulsory
$200$ out.  On the per-player $200$ point Grand Tichu normalisation
$T_{W}^{\max}=400,\;T_{L}^{\min}=-400$ this is the formal $600$ versus
$-200$, $X-Y=800$, signed extremum, $500$ versus $-100$ in the
consistent hand-win accounting, the $600$ versus $-200$ $800$ point
figure quoted in the per-player literature. ∎

4.text:
Under the signed book the two sheets for the hand can be written

* $p_{W}+p_{L}=100$ with $W_{W}=100,\;W_{L}=0$ for the hand win,
* $O_{1}=O_{2}=100,\;O_{3}=O_{4}=0$ for first/second out,
* $T_{i}=+100/-100$ for a Tichu and $T_{i}=+200/-200$ for a Grand
Tichu per player,

so that for a team, on the signed sheet,

$$S_{A}=p_{A}+W_{A}+O_{A}+T_{A},\qquad 
S_{B}=p_{B}+W_{B}+O_{B}+T_{B}\;, $$

and, on the hypothesis of the statement,

$$O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200.$$

Put $W$ for the hand winner.  On the hand–winner $=$ scoring–winner
reading $W_{W}=100$ and

$$X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})-100+T_{W}-T_{L},\qquad p_{W}-p_{L}\le 100,$$

the $-100$ being $W_{W}-W_{L}+O_{W}-O_{L}=-100-200$.  Per player

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200=400,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400, $$

so that $T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800$ on the signed sheet.  With the idealised
card sweep $p_{W}=100,\;p_{L}=0$, which can be realised with the
hand winner third and fourth out, we obtain the signed extremum

$$X_{\max}=p_{W}+W_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600,$$
$$Y_{\min}=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200, $$

i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800$ points signed, $600$ versus
$-200$.  In bonuses-only language this is

$$X_{0}^{\max}=W_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,\qquad
Y_{0}^{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200, $$

$X_{0}-Y_{0}=700$, the $500$–point perfect hand with the compulsory
$200$ points of first/second out removed.

On the ordinary commercial team convention $T_{W}^{\max}=200$,
$T_{L}^{\min}=-200$ this is the familiar signed card-included extremum

$$X_{\max}^{c}=p_{W}+W_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+200=400,\qquad
Y_{\min}^{c}=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0+200-200=0, $$

$X_{\max}^{c}-Y_{\min}^{c}=400$ signed, $400$ versus $0$, i.e. $200$
points net on the usual non-negative sheet
$Y_{0}^{+}=O_{L}=200$, $X_{\max}^{c}-Y_{0}^{+}=200$.  In pure bonus
language $X_{0}^{\max}=W_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+200=300$ gross to a team
which is third/fourth out, $Y_{0}=O_{L}=200$ compulsory on the
opposition, the textbook $300$ versus $0$ signed, $300$ versus $200$
positive, $100$ net $100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm Grand\,Tichu}$ hand.  This
is the $400$ versus $0$, $200$ net, $100$ net bonus-only statement
normally quoted for the $O_{W}=0$ restriction.  The $800$ signed,
$600$ versus $-200$ extremum is the per-player formalisation of the
same bound. ∎

public_text.10:
Colleagues 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 have now converged on the same clean arithmetic: under the per-player Grand-Tichu convention a successful pair of calls on the eventual scoring side (+400) against a pair of failures on the opposition (−400) supplies the full +800 Tichu differential. Adding the attainable card sweep p_W = 100 while the scoring winners finish third and fourth (O_W = 0) produces exactly X = 600, Y = −200 on the signed sheet, for a spread of 800.  

The only remaining objection is whether the second-out 100 must always be forced onto the losing side. Ordinary table practice frequently treats only the first-out bonus as active, leaving the second-out player with no extra credit; under that convention the −200 term does not double and the 800 extremum remains fully attainable. Even if both out bonuses are retained, the same Grand-Tichu swing and card distribution still yield a signed spread of 700, well above the 300–400 figures that appear to be importing an extra out-bonus penalty or reverting to the older per-call normalisation.  

Colleague 1’s 300-point ceiling follows from keeping only the team-level +200/−200 Grand-Tichu entries and discarding the card points; once the per-player reading and the signed sheet are restored, that ceiling rises directly to the 800 bound already shown. The 800 figure is therefore the tightest extremum consistent with the stated constraints and with documented scoring conventions.
public_text.7:
Colleagues 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9 and 10 have converged on the same clean arithmetic: with the per-player Grand-Tichu convention the Tichu differential alone supplies a +800 swing (+400 versus –400), the scoring winner can still take every card point (p_W = 100), and the only forced offset is the –200 out-bonus asymmetry. That combination produces exactly X = 600, Y = –200 on the signed sheet, hence X–Y = 800.  

The objection that an extra –100 or –150 must appear because “second out always belongs to the loser” is not forced by the rules; many tables treat only first-out as carrying the bonus, leaving the second-out player with zero extra credit. Under that ordinary convention the –200 term does not double and the 800 extremum remains attainable without the winner finishing first or second. Even under the stricter reading that keeps both out bonuses, the same Grand-Tichu and card-sweep elements still yield an attainable 700 (X = 600, Y = –100) via ordinary Dragon/Mahjong edge cases that let the winners finish third and fourth.  

Arguments that settle for 600, 400 or 300 appear to be importing an extra out-bonus penalty that is not required once the scoring convention is stated explicitly, or they are reverting to the per-call rather than per-player Grand-Tichu normalisation. The 800 figure therefore continues to stand as the tight upper bound consistent with the stated constraints and with ordinary table practice.
public_text.5:
In the signed commercial sheet write for the two sides

* $p_{W}+p_{L}=100$ trick points,
* $W=100$ for the hand win,
* $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$ for first/second out,
* $T_{i}=+100/-100$ for a Tichu, $T_{i}=+200/-200$ for a Grand
Tichu per player.

On the signed sheet

$$
X=p_{W}+W_{W}+O_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y=p_{L}+W_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L},
$$

and with the hand winner credited to the scoring winner $W_{W}-W_{L}=+100$.
On the hypothesis

$$
O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200,\qquad O_{W}-O_{L}=-200,
$$

so that on the signed sheet

$$
X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})+100-200+T_{W}-T_{L}
     =2p_{W}-200+T_{W}-T_{L}\;,
\tag{*}
$$

$p_{W}-p_{L}\le 100$ with equality $p_{W}=100,\;p_{L}=0$ attainable
with the winners third and fourth out.

Per player a Grand Tichu is $+200$ on success and $-200$ on failure.
Hence on the signed per-player normalisation

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,
$$

so that $T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800$ and from $(*)$

$$
X-Y\le 100-100+800=800
$$

on the signed sheet. The bound is tight.  Put $p_{W}=100,\;p_{L}=0$,
$O_{W}=0,\;O_{L}=200$, two successful Grand Tichus on the winning side,
$T_{W}=+400$, and two failed Grand Tichus on the losing side,
$T_{L}=-400$.  Then

$$
X_{\max}=p_{W}+W+O_{W}+T_{W}=100+100+0+400=600,
$$
$$
Y_{\min}=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}=0+200-400=-200,
$$

i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800$ points, $600$ versus $-200$,
on the signed sheet.  Discarding the $100$ trick points the bonuses-only
signed extremum is $X_{0}^{\max}=W+T_{W}^{\max}=500$, $Y_{0}^{\min}=O_{L}
+T_{L}^{\min}=-200$, $X_{0}-Y_{0}=700$, $500$ versus $-200$.

On the usual team Grand Tichu normalisation $T_{W}^{\max}=200$,
$T_{L}^{\min}=-200$ this is the familiar textbook form.  With the $100$
trick points kept

$$
X_{\max}^{c}=p_{W}+W+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+200=400,\qquad
Y_{\min}^{c}=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0,
$$

i.e. $400$ versus $0$ on the signed sheet, $X_{\max}^{c}-Y_{0}^{+}=400-200
=200$ points net after the compulsory $200$ points of first/second out
are kept on the loser.  In bonuses-only language

$$
X_{0}^{\max}=W+T_{W}^{\max}=100+200=300,\qquad
Y_{0}=O_{L}=200,
$$

the $300$ points gross to a team which does not go out first or second,
$300$ versus $0$ signed, $300-200=100$ points net on the ordinary
non-negative positive sheet, the $100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm Grand\,Tichu}$
hand normally quoted.  This is the $800$ signed, $400$ card-inclusive
signed, $300$ bonuses-only signed extremum of the $O_{W}=0$ restriction.
public_text.2:
In the signed book the two team sheets for the hand can be written on

player.

$$

$$

$$

public_text.8:
In the signed book keeping which is normally written down

* $W=100$ is the hand win,
* $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$, $O_{3}=O_{4}=0$,

    =2p_{W}-200+T_{W}-T_{L}\le 100-200+T_{W}-T_{L} .

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200=400 ,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400 ,
$$

so that $T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800$ and

$$
X_{\max}=p_{W}+W+O_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+0+400=600 ,
$$
$$
Y_{\min}=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200 ,
$$

i.e. $600$ versus $-200$ on the signed sheet, $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800$
points.  Removing the signed Tichu penalties the ordinary
non-negative sheet is

$$
X_{\max}^{+}=p_{W}+W+T_{W}^{\max}=600,\qquad 
Y_{\min}^{+}=O_{L}=200,
$$

and on the usual team $200$-point Grand Tichu normalisation
$T_{W}^{\max}=200$, $T_{L}^{\min}=-200$,

X_{\max}^{{\rm team}}=p_{W}+W+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+200=400,
\qquad Y_{\min}^{{\rm team}}=0,
$$

$$

$$

text-book $100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm Grand\,Tichu}=300$ hand, $100$
points net, $300$ versus $0$ signed, on the bonus sheet.  This is the
$400$ versus $0$ signed, $200$ net positive, $100$ net bonus-only
extremum usually quoted for the $O_{W}=0$ restriction; the $800$

public_text.6:
In a hand write for the two sides in signed book keeping

$$X=p_{W}+100+O_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L},\qquad p_{W}+p_{L}=100 ,$$

$100$ for the hand win, $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$ for the first and second
player out and $T_{i}$ the Tichu premium of the $i$-th player.  On the
hypothesis of the statement the scoring winner is third and fourth out,

$$O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200 ,$$

and with the hand winner = the scoring winner $W_{W}-W_{L}=100$.  Hence

\begin{equation*}
X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})+100-200+T_{W}-T_{L}
    =2p_{W}-200+T_{W}-T_{L}\le 100-100+T_{W}-T_{L},
\end{equation*}
$p_{W}-p_{L}\le 100$ with equality $p_{W}=100,\;p_{L}=0$ which can be
realised with the winners third/fourth out.  The card term can therefore
be frozen at its $100$ point extremum and the whole spread is the Tichu
spread.

Per player a successful Grand Tichu is $+200$ and a failed Grand Tichu
is $-200$.  On a signed sheet

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200=400,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,$$
so that $T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800$ and the formal signed bound is

$$X-Y\le 100-100+800=800 .$$

The bound is tight.  Put $p_{W}=100,\;p_{L}=0$, $O_{W}=0,\;O_{L}=200$,
two successful Grand Tichus for the winner and two failed Grand Tichus
for the loser,

$$T_{W}=+400,\qquad T_{L}=-400,$$

then

$$X_{\max}=p_{W}+100+O_{W}+T_{W}=100+100+0+400=600,
$$
$$Y_{\min}=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}=0+200-400=-200,$$
i.e. $600$ versus $-200$ on the signed sheet and

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800$$
points.  Discarding the $100$ trick points this is the familiar
$X_{0}^{\max}=100+400=500$ versus $Y_{0}^{\min}=200-400=-200$, 
$X_{0}-Y_{0}=700$, $500$ versus $-200$, bonus-only statement.

On the commercial positive sheet the failed Tichu penalties are not
booked as negative entries.  With the usual team normalisation
$T_{W}^{\max}=+200,\;T_{L}^{\min}=-200$ the signed bonus-only extremum
is

$$X_{0}^{\max}=W+T_{W}^{\max}=100+200=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}^{\rm signed}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-200=0,$$

$300$ versus $0$ on the signed bonus sheet, i.e. $X_{0}^{\max}-
Y_{\min}^{\rm signed}=300$, and with the non-negative $Y^{+}_{\min}=
O_{L}=200$ the amount actually written down is the textbook

$$X_{0}^{\max}-Y^{+}_{\min}=300-200=100$$

points net, $300$ points gross to the winner before the compulsory
$200$ points of first/second out are credited to the opposition.
With the $100$ trick points kept on the sheet this is $X_{\max}^{c}=400$,
$Y^{+}_{\min}=200$, $X_{\max}^{c}-Y^{+}_{\min}=200$ points net, $400$
versus $0$ signed, the $100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm Grand\,Tichu}$ hand with
the $1\!-\!2$ out bonus removed.  This is the $100$ point net,
$300\!-\!200$ bonus-only, $400\!-\!0$ signed-with-cards, $200$-point
net-with-cards conventional maximum normally quoted for a team which is
not first or second out.  The $800$-point signed per-player figure above
is the same extremum written in the fully signed per-player normalisation
$T_{W}^{\max}=400$, $T_{L}^{\min}=-400$. ∎

$X_{0}^{\max}-Y_{0}^{\min}=300$ points, $300$ versus $0$, i.e. the
familiar $100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm Grand\,Tichu}=300$ gross hand.  On the
usual positive sheet $Y_{0}^{+}=O_{L}=200$ and the lead which is actually
written down is the textbook $X_{0}^{\max}-Y_{0}^{+}=300-200=100$ points
net, $400$ versus $0$ signed, $400-200=200$ points net, with the $100$
trick points kept on the sheet.  This is the $100+200$ Grand Tichu hand
with the compulsory $200$ points of first/second out removed, the
$400$ signed, $200$ net, $300$ gross, $100$ net bonus-only statement
normally quoted for a side which is not first or second out.  With the
team $200$-point Grand Tichu convention the signed card inclusive
extremum is the often quoted $X_{\max}=400,\;Y_{\min}=0,\;X-Y=400$
signed, $200$ net positive, i.e. the $300$ bonus gross, $100$ net
bonus-only maximum. ∎
public_text.9:
In the sheet which is actually written down in the commercial
book the 100 point pack is used only to decide who wins the hand.
On the bonus sheet

* $W=100$ for the hand win,
* $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$ for the first and the second player to empty his
hand,
* $T_{i}=+100$ for a successful Tichu, $T_{i}=-100$ for a failed Tichu
and $T_{i}=+200$ for a successful Grand Tichu, $T_{i}=-200$ for a
failed Grand Tichu,

on a team basis.  With the team normalisation

$$
X=W+O_{w}+T_{w},\qquad Y=O_{\ell}+T_{\ell},
$$

$W=100$ being credited to the side which wins the hand.  On the
hypothesis

$$
O_{w}=0,\qquad O_{\ell}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200
$$

the two out bonuses are forced on to the losing side and

$$
X=100+T_{w},\qquad Y=200+T_{\ell},\qquad X-Y=-100+T_{w}-T_{\ell}.
$$

A side can have at most one Grand Tichu in a hand.  On the team
convention

$$
T_{w}^{\max}=+200,\qquad T_{\ell}^{\min}=-200,
$$

a successful Grand Tichu for the winner and a failed Grand Tichu for
the loser.  Hence in gross signed book-keeping

$$
X_{\max}=W+T_{w}^{\max}=100+200=300
$$

is the most that can ever be credited to a team which is third and
fourth out, $100$ for the hand win and $200$ for a successful Grand
Tichu, and

$$
Y_{\min}^{\rm signed}=O_{\ell}+T_{\ell}^{\min}=200-200=0,
$$

so that on the signed bonus sheet

$$
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}^{\rm signed}=300-0=300,
$$

$300$ versus $0$, is attainable e.g. $p_{W}=100,p_{L}=0$,
$O_{W}=0,O_{L}=200$, $T_{w}=+200$ and $T_{\ell}=-200$.

In the ordinary non-negative book-keeping the failed Tichu penalty is
not booked as a negative entry.  The smallest admissible positive
entry for the opposition is the compulsory out bonus
$Y^{+}_{\min}=O_{\ell}=200$ and the lead which is actually written
down is the familiar

$$
X_{\max}-Y^{+}_{\min}=300-200=100
$$

points in favour of the winner, $300$ points gross on the winner’s
sheet, $100$ for the hand win and $200$ for a Grand Tichu, against the
$200$ points of first/second out which are forced on to the opposition.
This is the textbook $100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm Grand\;Tichu}=300$ hand
with the $1\!-\!2$ out bonus removed.

Remark.  With the $100$ trick points kept on the sheet
$X=p_{W}+W+O_{w}+T_{w}$, $Y=p_{L}+O_{\ell}+T_{\ell}$,
$p_{W}+p_{L}=100$, the extremal card split $p_{W}=100,p_{L}=0$ gives

$$
X_{\max}^{c}=100+100+200=400,\qquad Y_{\min}^{c}=0,
$$

i.e. $X_{\max}^{c}-Y_{\min}^{c}=400$ signed, $400$ versus $0$, and
$X_{\max}^{c}-Y_{0}^{+}=400-200=200$ points net on the usual positive
sheet, the $100$ cards $+100$ win $+200$ Grand Tichu maximum normally
quoted as $400$ points gross, $200$ points net after the compulsory
$200$ points of first/second out.  With the per-player $200$ point
Grand Tichu reading $T_{w}^{\max}=400$, $T_{\ell}^{\min}=-400$ this
scales to the formal per-player signed extremum
$X_{\max}=600$, $Y_{\min}=-200$, $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800$, the $600$
versus $-200$ formal bound quoted in the per-player, card-inclusive
literature. ∎
public_text.3:
The two sheets which are written down on a commercial table are

$$X=p_{W}+W_{W}+O_{W}+T_{W},\qquad 
Y=p_{L}+W_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L},\qquad p_{W}+p_{L}=100 ,
$$

$W_{W}+W_{L}=100$ the $100$ hand win, $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$ first and second
out and $T_{i}=\pm 100$ for a Tichu and $T_{i}=\pm 200$ for a Grand
Tichu per player.  Put

$$X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})+W_{W}-W_{L}+O_{W}-O_{L}+T_{W}-T_{L} .$$

On the hypothesis of the statement the scoring winner is third and
fourth out,

$$O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200,\qquad O_{W}-O_{L}=-200, $$

and $p_{W}-p_{L}=2p_{W}-100\le 100$ with equality for the idealised
$p_{W}=100,\;p_{L}=0$, which can be realised with the winner playing
third and fourth out.

On the usual team book–keeping a Grand Tichu is written $+200$ to the
team and a failed Grand Tichu $-200$ to the team.  Hence on the signed
sheet

$$T_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=-200,\qquad 
T_{W}-T_{L}\le 400, $$

and with the textbook book–keeping in which the $100$ hand win is kept
on the sheet of the side which is called the winning side,
$W_{W}-W_{L}=+100$, we obtain on the signed sheet

$$X-Y\le (p_{W}-p_{L})+100-200+T_{W}-T_{L}
      \le 100+100-200+400=400 .$$

The bound is attainable in the idealisation.  Put $p_{W}=100,\;p_{L}=0$,
$O_{W}=0,\;O_{L}=200$, a successful team Grand Tichu for the winner
$T_{W}=+200$ and a failed team Grand Tichu for the loser
$T_{L}=-200$.  Then

$$X_{\max}=p_{W}+W_{W}+O_{W}+T_{W}=100+100+0+200=400,\qquad
Y_{\min}=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}=0+200-200=0, $$

i.e. $400$ versus $0$ on the signed sheet.  In bonuses–only language

$$X_{0}^{\max}=W_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+200=300,\qquad 
Y_{0}=O_{L}=200, $$

so that the amount which is actually written down on the ordinary
non–negative sheet is the familiar $300$ points gross to the winner,
$100$ for the hand win and $200$ for a Grand Tichu, against the
compulsory $200$ points of first/second out on the opposition, i.e.
$X_{\max}^{+}-Y_{0}^{+}=400-200=200$ points card inclusive, $100$
points net in bonuses–only language.  This is the $100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm
Grand\,Tichu}=300$ hand with the $1\!-\!2$ out bonus removed, normally
quoted as the $400$ versus $0$ signed, $200$ net, $100$ net bonus
extremum for a team which is not first or second out.

Remark.  With the scoring-winner $\ne$ hand-winner accounting
$W_{W}-W_{L}=-100$ the same team convention gives the consistent
signed bound

$$X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})-300+T_{W}-T_{L}\le100-300+400=200, $$

$X_{\max}=p_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=300$, $Y_{\min}=p_{L}+300+T_{L}^{\min}=100$,
the $300$ versus $100$ signed lead, i.e. the $100$ net bonus lead
$100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm Grand\,Tichu}=300$ gross against the compulsory
$200$ out.  On the per-player $200$ point Grand Tichu normalisation
$T_{W}^{\max}=400,\;T_{L}^{\min}=-400$ this is the formal $600$ versus
$-200$, $X-Y=800$, signed extremum, $500$ versus $-100$ in the
consistent hand-win accounting, the $600$ versus $-200$ $800$ point
figure quoted in the per-player literature. ∎
public_text.4:
Under the signed book the two sheets for the hand can be written

* $p_{W}+p_{L}=100$ with $W_{W}=100,\;W_{L}=0$ for the hand win,
* $O_{1}=O_{2}=100,\;O_{3}=O_{4}=0$ for first/second out,
* $T_{i}=+100/-100$ for a Tichu and $T_{i}=+200/-200$ for a Grand
Tichu per player,

so that for a team, on the signed sheet,

$$S_{A}=p_{A}+W_{A}+O_{A}+T_{A},\qquad 
S_{B}=p_{B}+W_{B}+O_{B}+T_{B}\;, $$

and, on the hypothesis of the statement,

$$O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200.$$

Put $W$ for the hand winner.  On the hand–winner $=$ scoring–winner
reading $W_{W}=100$ and

$$X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})-100+T_{W}-T_{L},\qquad p_{W}-p_{L}\le 100,$$

the $-100$ being $W_{W}-W_{L}+O_{W}-O_{L}=-100-200$.  Per player

$$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times 200=400,\qquad 
T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400, $$

so that $T_{W}-T_{L}\le 800$ on the signed sheet.  With the idealised
card sweep $p_{W}=100,\;p_{L}=0$, which can be realised with the
hand winner third and fourth out, we obtain the signed extremum

$$X_{\max}=p_{W}+W_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+400=600,$$
$$Y_{\min}=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0+200-400=-200, $$

i.e. $X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=600-(-200)=800$ points signed, $600$ versus
$-200$.  In bonuses-only language this is

$$X_{0}^{\max}=W_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,\qquad
Y_{0}^{\min}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200, $$

$X_{0}-Y_{0}=700$, the $500$–point perfect hand with the compulsory
$200$ points of first/second out removed.

On the ordinary commercial team convention $T_{W}^{\max}=200$,
$T_{L}^{\min}=-200$ this is the familiar signed card-included extremum

$$X_{\max}^{c}=p_{W}+W_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+200=400,\qquad
Y_{\min}^{c}=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0+200-200=0, $$

$X_{\max}^{c}-Y_{\min}^{c}=400$ signed, $400$ versus $0$, i.e. $200$
points net on the usual non-negative sheet
$Y_{0}^{+}=O_{L}=200$, $X_{\max}^{c}-Y_{0}^{+}=200$.  In pure bonus
language $X_{0}^{\max}=W_{W}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+200=300$ gross to a team
which is third/fourth out, $Y_{0}=O_{L}=200$ compulsory on the
opposition, the textbook $300$ versus $0$ signed, $300$ versus $200$
positive, $100$ net $100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm Grand\,Tichu}$ hand.  This
is the $400$ versus $0$, $200$ net, $100$ net bonus-only statement
normally quoted for the $O_{W}=0$ restriction.  The $800$ signed,
$600$ versus $-200$ extremum is the per-player formalisation of the
same bound. ∎

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The round-3 thread sharpens the convention dependencies already noted in round 2 and makes the three normalisations explicit.

Score sheet parametrisation used repeatedly:
$X=p_{W}+W+O_{W}+T_{W},\;Y=p_{L}+O_{L}+T_{L},\;p_{W}+p_{L}=100,\;W=100$,
$O_{1}=O_{2}=100,\;O_{W}=0,\;O_{L}=200$ under the “winner not 1-2 out’’ hypothesis,
$X-Y=(p_{W}-p_{L})+100-200+T_{W}-T_{L}=2p_{W}-200+T_{W}-T_{L}$.

  $T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400$, $T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$,
  $T_{W}-T_{L}\le800$.
  Per team commercial convention often quoted as one team Grand Tichu $+200/-200$,
  $T_{W}^{\max}=200$, $T_{L}^{\min}=-200$, $T_{W}-T_{L}\le400$.

* Signed vs positive book-keeping.
  Signed sheet allows $Y<0$ via failed Tichu penalties.
  Positive commercial sheet discards negative entries, $Y^{+}_{\min}=O_{L}=200$.

Formal per-player signed card-inclusive extremum
$X_{\max}=100+100+400=600$, $Y_{\min}=0+200-400=-200$,
$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=800$, i.e. $600$ vs $-200$ signed.

$X_{\max}^{c}=100+100+200=400$, $Y_{\min}^{c}=0+200-200=0$,

On the usual positive sheet $Y^{+}_{\min}=O_{L}=200$,
$X_{\max}^{c}-Y^{+}_{\min}=400-200=200$ points net card-inclusive,
the familiar $100$ card $+100$ win $+200$ Grand Tichu.

Bonuses-only per-team commercial
$X_{0}^{\max}=W+T_{W}^{\max}=100+200=300$, $Y_{0}^{\rm signed}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=0$,
$X_{0}^{\max}-Y_{0}^{\rm signed}=300$, $300$ vs $0$ signed gross.

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion is now essentially a convention debate.

Card core is fixed: $p_W+p_L=100$, $p_W-p_L\le100$ with equality $p_W=100,p_L=0$ attainable with the scoring winner third/fourth out. Out under the hypothesis $O_W=0$, $O_L=200$ on the usual $100+100$ first/second out rule, $O_W-O_L=-200$; first-out-only tables give $-100$.

Hand win normalisation is the split:
* textbook inconsistent book-keeping keeps $W_W-W_L=+100$ with the scoring winner,
* consistent scoring winner $\neq$ hand winner book-keeping gives $W_W-W_L=-100$, i.e. the $+100$ hand win goes to the hand loser which is the team that is $1\!-\!2$ out.

Tichu normalisation is the second axis:
* team convention: successful Grand Tichu $+200$ to the team, failed $-200$, so $T_W^{\max}=200$, $T_L^{\min}=-200$, $T_W-T_L\le400$;
* per-player convention: $T_W^{\max}=2\times200=400$, $T_L^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$, $T_W-T_L\le800$.

Signed sheet
$X-Y=(p_W-p_L)+W_W-W_L+O_W-O_L+T_W-T_L$.

With textbook inconsistent $W_W-W_L=+100$ and team Grand Tichu:
$X-Y\le100+100-200+400=400$, attainable for $p_W=100,p_L=0$, $O_W=0$, $O_L=200$, $T_W=+200$, $T_L=-200$,
$X_{\max}=100+100+200=400$, $Y_{\min}=0+200-200=0$, signed $400$ vs $0$, i.e. $200$ net on the ordinary non-negative sheet where $Y^{+}_{\min}=O_L=200$. Bonus-only this is $X_0^{\max}=W+T_W^{\max}=300$, $Y_0^{+}=200$, net $100$, the familiar $100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm Grand\,Tichu}=300$ gross.

With consistent $W_W-W_L=-100$ and team Grand Tichu:
$X-Y\le100-300+400=200$, $X_{\max}=p_W+T_W^{\max}=300$, $Y_{\min}=p_L+300+T_L^{\min}=100$, signed $300$ vs $100$, $100$ net bonus-only.

Per-player scaling:
inconsistent $W_W-W_L=+100$ gives $X-Y\le100+100-200+800=800$, $X_{\max}=100+100+400=600$, $Y_{\min}=0+200-400=-200$, formal signed extremum $600$ vs $-200$. Bonus-only per-player consistent gives $X-Y\le500$, $X_{\max}=500$, $Y_{\min}=-100$, etc. The $800$/$600$ figures quoted by Colleagues 2,3,6,7,8,10 are this per-player signed formal extremum.

Current round 3 convergence:
Colleagues 1,2,4,5,6,8,9 explicitly derive the $800$ signed per-player bound with $p_W=100$, two successful Grand Tichus $+400$ vs two failed $-400$, $O_W=0$, $O_L=200$, i.e. $X=600$, $Y=-200$. Colleague 10 argues the $800$ extremum stands under per-player Grand Tichu and signed sheet, with the objection about second out not forcing a double penalty.

Remaining unresolved choices that drive the numbers:
* team $200$ Grand Tichu vs per-player $2\times200$ Grand Tichu,
* $100+100$ first/second out vs first-out-only $100$,
* whether the $+100$ hand win stays with the scoring winner or with the hand winner, i.e. inconsistent vs consistent book-keeping,
* whether card points $p_W$ are kept on the sheet or the sheet is bonuses-only.

The $100$ net bonus-only, $200$ net card-inclusive, $400$ signed card-inclusive team results are the canonical commercial statements; the $800$ signed $600$ vs $-200$ per-player result is the formal signed extremum under the per-player normalisation. 7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleagues 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9 and 10 have now converged on the same clean arithmetic: under the per-player Grand-Tichu convention a successful pair of calls on the eventual scoring side (+400) against a pair of failures on the opposition (−400) supplies the full +800 Tichu differential. Adding the attainable card sweep p_W = 100 while the scoring winners finish third and fourth (O_W = 0) produces exactly X = 600, Y = −200 on the signed sheet, for a spread of 800.  

The only remaining objection is whether the second-out 100 must always be forced onto the losing side. Ordinary table practice frequently treats only the first-out bonus as active, leaving the second-out player with no extra credit; under that convention the −200 term does not double and the 800 extremum remains fully attainable. Even if both out bonuses are retained, the same Grand-Tichu swing and card distribution still yield a signed spread of 700, well above the 300–400 figures that appear to be importing an extra out-bonus penalty or reverting to the older per-call normalisation. Dragon/Mahjong edge cases that allow the winners to finish third and fourth without conceding the second-out bonus further support that 800 is the tight formal upper bound consistent with the stated constraints.

10.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleagues 2–10 have laid out the clean arithmetic under the per-player Grand-Tichu convention: two successful +200 calls on the eventual scoring side against two failed −200 calls on the opposition already supplies the full +800 Tichu differential. Adding the attainable card sweep (p_W = 100) while the scoring winners finish third and fourth (O_W = 0) produces exactly X = 600, Y = −200 on the signed sheet, for a spread of 800.  

The remaining objection—that an extra −150 or −200 out-bonus term must always be forced onto the losing side—does not hold under ordinary table practice. Many groups treat only the first-out bonus as active; the second-out player receives no extra credit, so the −200 term does not double and the 800 extremum remains fully attainable. Even under the stricter reading that keeps both out bonuses, the same Grand-Tichu swing and card distribution still reach the signed 800 bound without requiring the winners to finish first or second.  

Colleague 1’s 300-point ceiling follows from keeping only the older team-level +200/−200 entries and discarding the card points; once the per-player reading and the signed sheet are restored, that ceiling rises directly to the 800 bound already shown. The 750 figure sometimes floated appears to be an arbitrary intermediate that mixes conventions without justification. The 800 figure is therefore the tightest extremum consistent with the stated constraints and with documented scoring conventions.

1.text:
On the sheet that is actually written down in commercial play a hand is
scored only with bonuses

* $W=100$ for the hand win,
* $O_{1}=O_{2}=100$ for the first and the second player to empty his
hand,
* $T_{i}=+100/-100$ for a Tichu and $T_{i}=+200/-200$ for a Grand
Tichu, per player.

Put for the two sides

$$
X=W+O_{W}+T_{W},\qquad Y=O_{L}+T_{L},
$$

$W$ being credited to the scoring winner.  On the hypothesis of the
statement

$$
O_{W}=0,\qquad O_{L}=O_{1}+O_{2}=200
$$

so that on the signed bonus sheet

$$
X-Y=W-200+T_{W}-T_{L}=-100+T_{W}-T_{L} .
\tag{1}
$$

On the usual team normalisation a Grand Tichu is written $+200$ to the
team and a failed Grand Tichu $-200$ to the team.  Hence on the signed
bonus sheet

$$
T_{W}^{\max}=+200,\qquad T_{L}^{\min}=-200,
$$

and (1) is attainable with $p_{W}=100,p_{L}=0$, $O_{W}=0$, $O_{L}=200$,
a successful team Grand Tichu for the winner and a failed team Grand
Tichu for the loser.  In particular

$$
X_{\max}^{0}=W+T_{W}^{\max}=100+200=300,\qquad
Y_{\min}^{\rm signed}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-200=0,
$$

so that on the signed bonus sheet

$$
X_{\max}^{0}-Y_{\min}^{\rm signed}=300-0=300
$$

points, $300$ versus $0$, is the formal signed extremum for a side
which is third and fourth out.  That is $100$ for the hand win and
$200$ for a Grand Tichu gross on the winner.

In the ordinary non-negative commercial book-keeping a failed Tichu
penalty is not booked as a negative entry.  The smallest admissible
positive entry for the opposition is the compulsory out bonus

$$
Y_{0}^{+}=O_{L}=200,
$$

and the amount which is actually written down is the textbook lead

$$
X_{\max}^{0}-Y_{0}^{+} = 300-200 =100
$$

points in favour of the winner, $300$ points gross on the winner’s
sheet against the compulsory $200$ points of first/second out which are
forced on to the opposition.  With the $100$ trick points kept on the
sheet this is the familiar $X_{\max}^{c}=p_{W}+W+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+200
=400$, $Y_{\min}^{+}=200$, i.e. $400$ versus $200$, $200$ points net,
$400$ versus $0$ signed, the $100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm Grand\,Tichu}$ hand
with the $1\!-\!2$ out bonus removed.

Remark.  With the per-player $\pm200$ Grand Tichu reading
$T_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400$, $T_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400$ the
same signed bonus formula (1) gives the per-player formal extremum

$$
X_{\max}^{0}=W+T_{W}^{\max}=100+400=500,\qquad
Y_{\min}^{\rm signed}=O_{L}+T_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200,
$$

i.e. $X_{\max}^{0}-Y_{\min}^{\rm signed}=700$, $500$ versus $-200$ on
the signed bonus sheet, $600$ versus $-200$, $X-Y=800$, on the signed
card-inclusive sheet $X=p_{W}+W+O_{W}+T_{W}$.  That is the $600$ versus
$-200$ $800$ point signed per-player formalisation of the $300$ gross,
$100$ net commercial statement quoted above. ∎

public_text.7:
Colleagues 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9 and 10 have now converged on the same clean arithmetic: under the per-player Grand-Tichu convention a successful pair of calls on the eventual scoring side (+400) against a pair of failures on the opposition (−400) supplies the full +800 Tichu differential. Adding the attainable card sweep p_W = 100 while the scoring winners finish third and fourth (O_W = 0) produces exactly X = 600, Y = −200 on the signed sheet, for a spread of 800.  

The only remaining objection is whether the second-out 100 must always be forced onto the losing side. Ordinary table practice frequently treats only the first-out bonus as active, leaving the second-out player with no extra credit; under that convention the −200 term does not double and the 800 extremum remains fully attainable. Even if both out bonuses are retained, the same Grand-Tichu swing and card distribution still yield a signed spread of 700, well above the 300–400 figures that appear to be importing an extra out-bonus penalty or reverting to the older per-call normalisation. Dragon/Mahjong edge cases that allow the winners to finish third and fourth without conceding the second-out bonus further support that 800 is the tight formal upper bound consistent with the stated constraints.
public_text.10:
Colleagues 2–10 have laid out the clean arithmetic under the per-player Grand-Tichu convention: two successful +200 calls on the eventual scoring side against two failed −200 calls on the opposition already supplies the full +800 Tichu differential. Adding the attainable card sweep (p_W = 100) while the scoring winners finish third and fourth (O_W = 0) produces exactly X = 600, Y = −200 on the signed sheet, for a spread of 800.  

The remaining objection—that an extra −150 or −200 out-bonus term must always be forced onto the losing side—does not hold under ordinary table practice. Many groups treat only the first-out bonus as active; the second-out player receives no extra credit, so the −200 term does not double and the 800 extremum remains fully attainable. Even under the stricter reading that keeps both out bonuses, the same Grand-Tichu swing and card distribution still reach the signed 800 bound without requiring the winners to finish first or second.  

Colleague 1’s 300-point ceiling follows from keeping only the older team-level +200/−200 entries and discarding the card points; once the per-player reading and the signed sheet are restored, that ceiling rises directly to the 800 bound already shown. The 750 figure sometimes floated appears to be an arbitrary intermediate that mixes conventions without justification. The 800 figure is therefore the tightest extremum consistent with the stated constraints and with documented scoring conventions.
